110.s:
brahmovāca
pippalaṃ tīrtham ākhyātaṃ cakratīrthād anantaram
yatra cakreśvaro devaś cakram āpa yato hariḥ //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पिप्पलं तीर्थम् आख्यातं चक्रतीर्थाद् अनन्तरम्
यत्र चक्रेश्वरो देवश् चक्रम् आप यतो हरिः ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / The Pippala tīrtha is proclaimed next to Cakra-tīrtha, / where the god Cakreśvara is, [and] where Hari obtained the disc.

110.s:
yatra viṣṇuḥ svayaṃ sthitvā cakrārthaṃ śaṃkaraṃ vibhum
pūjayām āsa tat tīrthaṃ cakratīrtham udāhṛtam //
110.d:
यत्र विष्णुः स्वयं स्थित्वा चक्रार्थं शंकरं विभुम्
पूजयाम् आस तत् तीर्थं चक्रतीर्थम् उदाहृतम् ॥
110.m: Where Viṣṇu himself remained and worshipped the all-pervading Śaṅkara / for the sake of the disc, that tīrtha is declared as Cakra-tīrtha.

110.s:
yatra prīto 'bhavad viṣṇoḥ śaṃbhus tat pippalaṃ viduḥ
mahimānaṃ yasya vaktuṃ na kṣamo 'py ahināyakaḥ //
110.d:
यत्र प्रीतो ऽभवद् विष्णोः शंभुस् तत् पिप्पलं विदुः
महिमानं यस्य वक्तुं न क्षमो ऽप्य् अहिनायकः ॥
110.m: Where Śambhu was pleased with Viṣṇu, they know that as Pippala, / whose greatness even the lord of serpents is unable to recount.

110.s:
cakreśvaro pippaleśo nāmadheyasya kāraṇam
śṛṇu nārada tad bhaktyā sākṣād vedoditaṃ mayā //
110.d:
चक्रेश्वरो पिप्पलेशो नामधेयस्य कारणम्
शृणु नारद तद् भक्त्या साक्षाद् वेदोदितं मया ॥
110.m: Cakreśvara and Pippaleśa: hear with devotion, O Nārada, / the cause of that name, directly declared by me in accordance with the Veda.

110.s:
dadhīcir iti vikhyāto munir āsīd guṇānvitaḥ
tasya bhāryā mahāprājñā kulīnā ca pativratā //
110.d:
दधीचिर् इति विख्यातो मुनिर् आसीद् गुणान्वितः
तस्य भार्या महाप्राज्ञा कुलीना च पतिव्रता ॥
110.m: There was an illustrious sage endowed with virtues named Dadhīci; / his wife was exceedingly wise, of noble family, and devoted to her husband.

110.s:
lopāmudreti yā khyātā svasā tasyā gabhastinī
iti nāmnā ca vikhyātā vaḍaveti prakīrtitā //
110.d:
लोपामुद्रेति या ख्याता स्वसा तस्या गभस्तिनी
इति नाम्ना च विख्याता वडवेति प्रकीर्तिता ॥
110.m: She was known as Lopāmudrā; her sister was Gabhastinī, / renowned by that name and celebrated as Vaḍavā.

110.s:
dadhīceḥ sā priyā nityaṃ tapas tepe tayā mahat
dadhīcir agnimān nityaṃ gṛhadharmaparāyaṇaḥ //
110.d:
दधीचेः सा प्रिया नित्यं तपस् तेपे तया महत्
दधीचिर् अग्निमान् नित्यं गृहधर्मपरायणः ॥
110.m: She was always beloved of Dadhīci; with her he practiced great ascetic heat. / Dadhīci always maintained the sacred fire and was dedicated to the duties of a householder.

110.s:
bhāgīrathīṃ samāśritya devātithiparāyaṇaḥ
svakalatrarataḥ śāntaḥ kumbhayonir ivāparaḥ //
110.d:
भागीरथीं समाश्रित्य देवातिथिपरायणः
स्वकलत्ररतः शान्तः कुम्भयोनिर् इवापरः ॥
110.m: Resorting to the Bhāgīrathī, devoted to the gods and guests, / content with his own wife, peaceful, he was like a second Agastya.

110.s:
tasya prabhāvāt taṃ deśaṃ nārayo daityadānavāḥ
ājagmur muniśārdūla yatrāgastyasya cāśramaḥ //
110.d:
तस्य प्रभावात् तं देशं नारयो दैत्यदानवाः
आजग्मुर् मुनिशार्दूल यत्रागस्त्यस्य चाश्रमः ॥
110.m: Because of his power, enemies—the Daityas and Dānavas—did not come to that region, / O tiger among sages, where the hermitage of Agastya was.

110.s:
tatra devāḥ samājagmū rudrādityās tathāśvinau
indro viṣṇur yamo 'gniś ca jitvā daityān upāgatān //
110.d:
तत्र देवाः समाजग्मू रुद्रादित्यास् तथाश्विनौ
इन्द्रो विष्णुर् यमो ऽग्निश् च जित्वा दैत्यान् उपागतान् ॥
110.m: The gods assembled there: the Rudras, Ādityas, and the two Aśvins, / Indra, Viṣṇu, Yama, and Agni, having conquered the Daityas who had approached.

110.s:
jayena jātasaṃharṣāḥ stutāś caiva marudgaṇaiḥ
dadhīciṃ muniśārdūlaṃ dṛṣṭvā nemuḥ sureśvarāḥ //
110.d:
जयेन जातसंहर्षाः स्तुताश् चैव मरुद्गणैः
दधीचिं मुनिशार्दूलं दृष्ट्वा नेमुः सुरेश्वराः ॥
110.m: Filled with joy by victory and praised by the hosts of Maruts, / the lords of the gods, having seen Dadhīci, the tiger among sages, bowed down to him.

110.s:
dadhīcir jātasaṃharṣaḥ surān pūjya pṛthak pṛthak
gṛhakṛtyaṃ tataś cakre surebhyo bhāryayā saha //
110.d:
दधीचिर् जातसंहर्षः सुरान् पूज्य पृथक् पृथक्
गृहकृत्यं ततश् चक्रे सुरेभ्यो भार्यया सह ॥
110.m: Dadhīci, filled with joy, having worshipped the gods individually, / then performed the household rites for the gods together with his wife.

110.s:
pṛṣṭāś ca kuśalaṃ tena kathāś cakruḥ surā api
dadhīcim abruvan devā bhāryayā sukhitaṃ punaḥ //
110.d:
पृष्टाश् च कुशलं तेन कथाश् चक्रुः सुरा अपि
दधीचिम् अब्रुवन् देवा भार्यया सुखितं पुनः ॥
110.m: Asked about their welfare by him, the gods engaged in conversation; / the gods spoke again to Dadhīci, who was happy with his wife,

110.s: āsīnaṃ hṛṣṭamanasa ṛṣiṃ natvā punaḥ punaḥ //
110.d: आसीनं हृष्टमनस ऋषिं नत्वा पुनः पुनः ॥
110.m: bowing repeatedly to the sage who was seated with a delighted mind:

110.s:
devā ūcuḥ
kim adya durlabhaṃ loke ṛṣe 'smākaṃ bhaviṣyati
tvādṛśaḥ sakṛpo yeṣu munir bhūkalpapādapaḥ //
110.d:
देवा ऊचुः
किम् अद्य दुर्लभं लोके ऋषे ऽस्माकं भविष्यति
त्वादृशः सकृपो येषु मुनिर् भूकल्पपादपः ॥
110.m: The gods said: / What today will be difficult to attain in the world for us, O sage, / upon whom a sage like you, compassionate, is an earthly wishing tree?

110.s:
etad eva phalaṃ puṃsāṃ jīvatāṃ munisattama
tīrthāplutir bhūtadayā darśanaṃ ca bhavādṛśām //
110.d:
एतद् एव फलं पुंसां जीवतां मुनिसत्तम
तीर्थाप्लुतिर् भूतदया दर्शनं च भवादृशाम् ॥
110.m: This alone is the fruit for men while living, O best of sages: / ablution in a tīrtha, compassion for living beings, and the sight of those like you.

110.s:
yat snehād ucyate 'smābhir avadhāraya tan mune
jitvā daityān iha prāptā hatvā rākṣasapuṃgavān //
110.d:
यत् स्नेहाद् उच्यते ऽस्माभिर् अवधारय तन् मुने
जित्वा दैत्यान् इह प्राप्ता हत्वा राक्षसपुंगवान् ॥
110.m: Take heed, O sage, of what is spoken by us out of affection: / Having conquered the Daityas, having slain the foremost Rākṣasas, we have arrived here.

110.s:
vayaṃ ca sukhino brahmaṃs tvayi dṛṣṭe viśeṣataḥ
nāyudhaiḥ phalam asmākaṃ voḍhuṃ naiva kṣamā vayam //
110.d:
वयं च सुखिनो ब्रह्मंस् त्वयि दृष्टे विशेषतः
नायुधैः फलम् अस्माकं वोढुं नैव क्षमा वयम् ॥
110.m: And we are happy, O holy one, especially when you are seen; / we have no use for our weapons, nor are we able to carry them.

110.s:
sthāpyadeśaṃ na paśyāma āyudhānāṃ munīśvara
svarge suradviṣo jñātvā sthāpitāni haranti ca //
110.d:
स्थाप्यदेशं न पश्याम आयुधानां मुनीश्वर
स्वर्गे सुरद्विषो ज्ञात्वा स्थापितानि हरन्ति च ॥
110.m: We see no place to deposit the weapons, O lord of sages; / knowing that they are deposited in heaven, the enemies of the gods would seize them,

110.s:
nayeyur āyudhānīti tathaiva ca rasātale
tasmāt tavāśrame puṇye sthāpyante 'strāṇi mānada //
110.d:
नयेयुर् आयुधानीति तथैव च रसातले
तस्मात् तवाश्रमे पुण्ये स्थाप्यन्ते ऽस्त्राणि मानद ॥
110.m: and likewise they would carry off the weapons in Rasātala; / therefore, O giver of honor, the weapons are deposited in your holy hermitage.

110.s:
naivātra kiṃcid bhayam asti vipra
na dānavebhyo rākṣasebhyaś ca ghoram
tvadājñayā rakṣitapuṇyadeśo
na vidyate tapasā te samānaḥ
110.d:
नैवात्र किंचिद् भयम् अस्ति विप्र
न दानवेभ्यो राक्षसेभ्यश् च घोरम्
त्वदाज्ञया रक्षितपुण्यदेशो
न विद्यते तपसा ते समानः
110.m: There is no fear here, O brahmin, / none terrible from the Dānavas and Rākṣasas; / by your command the sacred region is protected; / none is equal to you in ascetic power.

110.s:
jitārayo brahmavidāṃ variṣṭhaṃ
vayaṃ ca pūrvaṃ nihatā daityasaṃghāḥ
astrair alaṃ bhārabhūtaiḥ kṛtārthaiḥ
sthāpyaṃ sthānaṃ te samīpe munīśa
110.d:
जितारयो ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठं
वयं च पूर्वं निहता दैत्यसंघाः
अस्त्रैर् अलं भारभूतैः कृतार्थैः
स्थाप्यं स्थानं ते समीपे मुनीश
110.m: Our enemies have been conquered, O best of knowers of the Veda, / and earlier the hordes of Daityas were slain by us; / enough with the weapons that have accomplished their purpose and become a burden! / The place to deposit them is near you, O lord of sages.

110.s:
divyān bhogān kāminībhiḥ sametān
devodyāne nandane saṃbhajāmaḥ
tato yāmaḥ kṛtakāryāḥ sahendrāḥ
svaṃ svaṃ sthānaṃ cāyudhānāṃ ca rakṣā
110.d:
दिव्यान् भोगान् कामिनीभिः समेतान्
देवोद्याने नन्दने संभजामः
ततो यामः कृतकार्याः सहेन्द्राः
स्वं स्वं स्थानं चायुधानां च रक्षा
110.m: Let us enjoy divine pleasures together with lovely women / in the Nandana garden of the gods; / then, having accomplished our business, we together with Indra will go / each to our own abode, and let there be protection of the weapons.

110.s:
brahmovāca
tadvākyam ākarṇya dadhīcir evaṃ
vākyaṃ jagau vibudhān evam astu
nivāryamāṇaḥ priyaśīlayā striyā
kiṃ devakāryeṇa viruddhakāriṇā
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद्वाक्यम् आकर्ण्य दधीचिर् एवं
वाक्यं जगौ विबुधान् एवम् अस्तु
निवार्यमाणः प्रियशीलया स्त्रिया
किं देवकार्येण विरुद्धकारिणा
110.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing their speech, Dadhīci spoke thus / to the gods: "So be it," / even while being dissuaded by his wife of affectionate disposition: / "What is the use of the gods' business that brings about opposition?

110.s:
ye jñātaśāstrāḥ paramārthaniṣṭhāḥ
saṃsāraceṣṭāsu gatānurāgāḥ
teṣāṃ parārthavyasanena kiṃ mune
yenātra vāmutra sukhaṃ na kiṃcit
110.d:
ये ज्ञातशास्त्राः परमार्थनिष्ठाः
संसारचेष्टासु गतानुरागाः
तेषां परार्थव्यसनेन किं मुने
येनात्र वामुत्र सुखं न किंचित्
110.m: Those who know the scriptures, intent on the supreme reality, / whose attachment to worldly activities has departed— / what is the use of trouble for others' sake to them, O sage, / by which there is no happiness whatsoever here or in the hereafter?

110.s:
devadviṣo dveṣam anuprayānti
datte sthāne vipravarya śṛṇuṣva
naṣṭe hṛte cāyudhānāṃ munīśa
kupyanti devā ripavas te bhavanti
110.d:
देवद्विषो द्वेषम् अनुप्रयान्ति
दत्ते स्थाने विप्रवर्य शृणुष्व
नष्टे हृते चायुधानां मुनीश
कुप्यन्ति देवा रिपवस् ते भवन्ति
110.m: The enemies of the gods will pursue their enmity / once a place has been given, O best of brahmins, listen! / If [the weapons] are lost or stolen, O lord of sages, / the gods become angry and become your enemies.

110.s:
tasmān nedaṃ vedavidāṃ variṣṭha
yuktaṃ dravye parakīye mamatvam
tāvac ca maitrī dravyabhāvaś ca tāvan
naṣṭe hṛte ripavas te bhavanti
110.d:
तस्मान् नेदं वेदविदां वरिष्ठ
युक्तं द्रव्ये परकीये ममत्वम्
तावच् च मैत्री द्रव्यभावश् च तावन्
नष्टे हृते रिपवस् ते भवन्ति
110.m: Therefore, O best of the knowers of the Veda, this / sense of 'mine' toward another's property is not proper; / friendship lasts only as long as the property exists; / if it is lost or stolen, they become your enemies.

110.s:
ced asti śaktir dravyadāne tatas te
dātavyam evārthine kiṃ vicāryam
no cet santaḥ parakāryāṇi kuryur
vāgbhir manobhiḥ kṛtibhis tathaiva
110.d:
चेद् अस्ति शक्तिर् द्रव्यदाने ततस् ते
दातव्यम् एवार्थिने किं विचार्यम्
नो चेत् सन्तः परकार्याणि कुर्युर्
वाग्भिर् मनोभिः कृतिभिस् तथैव
110.m: If there is the power to give property, then indeed / it should be given to a supplicant—what is there to consider? / If not, good people should perform others' tasks / through words, minds, and deeds likewise."

110.s:
brahmovāca dadhīcir uvāca brahmovāca
śrutveritaṃ patyur iti priyāyāṃ
daivaṃ vinānyan na nṛṇāṃ samartham
tūṣṇīṃ sthitāyāṃ surasattamās te
saṃsthāpya cāstrāṇy atidīptimanti
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच दधीचिर् उवाच ब्रह्मोवाच
श्रुत्वेरितं पत्युर् इति प्रियायां
दैवं विनान्यन् न नृणां समर्थम्
तूष्णीं स्थितायां सुरसत्तमास् ते
संस्थाप्य चास्त्राण्य् अतिदीप्तिमन्ति
110.m:
Brahmā said:
When his beloved, having heard her husband speak thus,
remained silent, [knowing] that nothing avails men without destiny,
those best of the gods, having laid down their blazing weapons,

110.s:
natvā munīndraṃ yayur eva lokān
daityadviṣo nyastaśastrāḥ kṛtārthāḥ
gateṣu deveṣu munipravaryo
hṛṣṭo 'vasad bhāryayā dharmayuktaḥ
110.d:
नत्वा मुनीन्द्रं ययुर् एव लोकान्
दैत्यद्विषो न्यस्तशस्त्राः कृतार्थाः
गतेषु देवेषु मुनिप्रवर्यो
हृष्टो ऽवसद् भार्यया धर्मयुक्तः
110.m: and bowed to the lord of sages, went indeed to their realms, / the enemies of the Daityas, having laid down their arms and accomplished their goal. / When the gods had gone, the foremost among sages, / full of joy and accompanied by his wife, lived in accordance with dharma.

110.s:
gate ca kāle hy ativiprayukte
daive varṣe saṃkhyayā vai sahasre
na te surā āyudhānāṃ munīśa
vācaṃ manaś cāpi tathaiva cakruḥ
110.d:
गते च काले ह्य् अतिविप्रयुक्ते
दैवे वर्षे संख्यया वै सहस्रे
न ते सुरा आयुधानां मुनीश
वाचं मनश् चापि तथैव चक्रुः
110.m: And when a long period of time had elapsed, / a thousand celestial years in number, / those gods did not speak a word nor even turn their mind / toward the weapons, O lord of sages.

110.s:
dadhīcir apy āha gabhastim ojasā
devārayo māṃ dviṣatīha bhadre
na te surā netukāmā bhavanti
saṃsthāpitāny atra vadasva yuktam
110.d:
दधीचिर् अप्य् आह गभस्तिम् ओजसा
देवारयो मां द्विषतीह भद्रे
न ते सुरा नेतुकामा भवन्ति
संस्थापितान्य् अत्र वदस्व युक्तम्
110.m: Then Dadhīci with vigor spoke to Gabhastinī: / "The enemies of the gods hate me here, O auspicious one; / those gods have no desire to take back / what was deposited here; tell me what is proper!"

110.s:
sā cāha kāntaṃ vinayād uktam eva
tvaṃ jānīṣe nātha yad atra yuktam
daityā hariṣyanti mahāpravṛddhās
tapoyuktā balinaḥ svāyudhāni
110.d:
सा चाह कान्तं विनयाद् उक्तम् एव
त्वं जानीषे नाथ यद् अत्र युक्तम्
दैत्या हरिष्यन्ति महाप्रवृद्धास्
तपोयुक्ता बलिनः स्वायुधानि
110.m: And she spoke to her beloved out of modesty what had already been said: / "You know, O lord, whatever is proper in this matter; / the Daityas, greatly grown in power, / endowed with tapas and strong, will carry off their weapons."

110.s:
tadastrarakṣārtham idaṃ sa cakre
mantrais tu saṃkṣālya jalaiś ca puṇyaiḥ
tad vāri sarvāstramayaṃ supuṇyaṃ
tejoyuktaṃ tac ca papau dadhīciḥ
110.d:
तदस्त्ररक्षार्थम् इदं स चक्रे
मन्त्रैस् तु संक्षाल्य जलैश् च पुण्यैः
तद् वारि सर्वास्त्रमयं सुपुण्यं
तेजोयुक्तं तच् च पपौ दधीचिः
110.m:
for the preservation of those divine weapons he did this:
having cleansed them with mantras and sacred waters,
Dadhīci drank that highly sacred, splendorous water
which contained all the divine weapons.

110.s:
nirvīryarūpāṇi tadāyudhāni
kṣayaṃ jagmuḥ kramaśaḥ kālayogāt
surāḥ samāgatya dadhīcim ūcur
mahābhayaṃ hy āgataṃ śātravaṃ naḥ
110.d:
निर्वीर्यरूपाणि तदायुधानि
क्षयं जग्मुः क्रमशः कालयोगात्
सुराः समागत्य दधीचिम् ऊचुर्
महाभयं ह्य् आगतं शात्रवं नः
110.m:
Those weapons, made devoid of their power,
gradually diminished under the influence of time.
The gods approached and said to Dadhīci:
"A great danger from our enemies has indeed arrived!

110.s:
dadasva cāstrāṇi munipravīra
yāni tvadante nihitāni devaiḥ
dadhīcir apy āha surāribhītyā
anāgatyā bhavatāṃ cācireṇa
110.d:
ददस्व चास्त्राणि मुनिप्रवीर
यानि त्वदन्ते निहितानि देवैः
दधीचिर् अप्य् आह सुरारिभीत्या
अनागत्या भवतां चाचिरेण
110.m:
Bestow the divine weapons, O foremost among sages,
which were deposited with you by the gods!"
Dadhīci, too, said: "Out of fear of the enemies of the gods,
since you did not arrive for a long time,

110.s:
astrāṇi pītāni śarīrasaṃsthāny
uktāni yuktaṃ mama tad vadantu
śrutvā taduktaṃ vacanaṃ tu devāḥ
procus tam itthaṃ vinayāvanamrāḥ
110.d:
अस्त्राणि पीतानि शरीरसंस्थान्य्
उक्तानि युक्तं मम तद् वदन्तु
श्रुत्वा तदुक्तं वचनं तु देवाः
प्रोचुस् तम् इत्थं विनयावनम्राः
110.m: "The weapons have been consumed and remain within my body, / as was told; let them tell me what is proper." / Having heard the word he spoke, the gods / answered him, bowed low in reverence:

110.s:
astrāṇi dehīti ca vaktum etac
chakyaṃ na vānyat prativaktuṃ munīndra
vinā ca taiḥ paribhūyema nityaṃ
puṣṭārayaḥ kva prayāmo munīśa
110.d:
अस्त्राणि देहीति च वक्तुम् एतच्
छक्यं न वान्यत् प्रतिवक्तुं मुनीन्द्र
विना च तैः परिभूयेम नित्यं
पुष्टारयः क्व प्रयामो मुनीश
110.m: "Neither can we say 'Give us the weapons', / nor can we answer otherwise, O lord of sages. / Yet without them we would be perpetually overthrown; / with our enemies strengthened, where shall we go, O lord among sages?

110.s:
na martyaloke na tale na nāke
vāsaḥ surāṇāṃ bhavitādya tāta
tvaṃ vipravaryas tapasā caiva yukto
nānyad vaktuṃ yujyate te purastāt
110.d:
न मर्त्यलोके न तले न नाके
वासः सुराणां भविताद्य तात
त्वं विप्रवर्यस् तपसा चैव युक्तो
नान्यद् वक्तुं युज्यते ते पुरस्तात्
110.m: Neither in the mortal world, nor in the underworld, nor in heaven / can there be a dwelling for the gods today, father. / You are the best among the twice-born, endowed with austerity; / it is not fitting to speak anything else before you."

110.s:
vipras tadovāca madasthisaṃsthāny
astrāṇi gṛhṇantu na saṃśayo 'tra
devās tam apy āhur anena kiṃ no hy
astrair hīnāḥ strītvam āptāḥ surendrāḥ
110.d:
विप्रस् तदोवाच मदस्थिसंस्थान्य्
अस्त्राणि गृह्णन्तु न संशयो ऽत्र
देवास् तम् अप्य् आहुर् अनेन किं नो ह्य्
अस्त्रैर् हीनाः स्त्रीत्वम् आप्ताः सुरेन्द्राः
110.m: The brahmin then said: "Let them take the weapons / that reside in my bones, of this there is no doubt." / But the gods said to him: "What good is this to us? / Deprived of our weapons, the lords of the gods have attained womanhood."

110.s:
punas tadā cāha munipravīras
tyakṣye jīvān daihikān yogayuktaḥ
astrāṇi kurvantu madasthibhūtāny
anuttamāny uttamarūpavanti
110.d:
पुनस् तदा चाह मुनिप्रवीरस्
त्यक्ष्ये जीवान् दैहिकान् योगयुक्तः
अस्त्राणि कुर्वन्तु मदस्थिभूतान्य्
अनुत्तमान्य् उत्तमरूपवन्ति
110.m: Then the heroic sage spoke once again: / "I shall cast off the bodily vital breaths, absorbed in yoga; / let them fashion weapons from my bones, / unexcelled and possessed of supreme forms."

110.s:
kuruṣva cety āhur adīnasattvaṃ
dadhīcim ity uttaram agnikalpam
tadā tu tasya priyam īrayantī
na sāṃnidhye prātitheyī munīśa
110.d:
कुरुष्व चेत्य् आहुर् अदीनसत्त्वं
दधीचिम् इत्य् उत्तरम् अग्निकल्पम्
तदा तु तस्य प्रियम् ईरयन्ती
न सांनिध्ये प्रातिथेयी मुनीश
110.m: "Do so!" they replied to Dadhīci of undaunted spirit, / who was equal to fire, with this answer. / At that time, Prātitheyī, who spoke what was dear to him, / was not present, O lord of sages.

110.s:
te cāpi devās tām adṛṣṭvaiva śīghraṃ
tasyā bhītā vipram ūcuḥ kuruṣva
tatyāja jīvān dustyajān prītiyukto
yathāsukhaṃ deham imaṃ juṣadhvam
110.d:
ते चापि देवास् ताम् अदृष्ट्वैव शीघ्रं
तस्या भीता विप्रम् ऊचुः कुरुष्व
तत्याज जीवान् दुस्त्यजान् प्रीतियुक्तो
यथासुखं देहम् इमं जुषध्वम्
110.m: And not seeing her, the gods quickly, / afraid of her, said to the brahmin: "Do it!" / Filled with love, he gave up the vital breaths that are hard to abandon, [saying]: / "Enjoy this body as you please!"

110.s:
brahmovāca
ity uktvāsau baddhapadmāsanastho
nāsāgradattākṣiprakāśaprasannaḥ
vāyuṃ savahniṃ madhyamodghāṭayogān
nītvā śanair daharākāśagarbham
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वासौ बद्धपद्मासनस्थो
नासाग्रदत्ताक्षिप्रकाशप्रसन्नः
वायुं सवह्निं मध्यमोद्घाटयोगान्
नीत्वा शनैर् दहराकाशगर्भम्
110.m:
Brahmā said:
Having spoken thus, sitting in the bound lotus posture, / serene, his gaze fixed on the tip of his nose, / by the yoga of opening the central channel, slowly leading the breath / together with the fire into the hollow of the heart,

110.s:
yad aprameyaṃ paramaṃ padaṃ yad
yad brahmarūpaṃ yad upāsitavyam
tatraiva vinyasya dhiyaṃ mahātmā
sāyujyatāṃ brahmaṇo 'sau jagāma
110.d:
यद् अप्रमेयं परमं पदं यद्
यद् ब्रह्मरूपं यद् उपासितव्यम्
तत्रैव विन्यस्य धियं महात्मा
सायुज्यतां ब्रह्मणो ऽसौ जगाम
110.m: and fixing his thought on that which is immeasurable, / which is the supreme abode, which is of the nature of Brahman, which is to be meditated upon, / that great-souled one attained communion with Brahman.

110.s:
nirjīvatāṃ prāptam abhīkṣya devāḥ
kalevaraṃ tasya surāś ca samyak
tvaṣṭāram apy ūcur atitvarantaḥ
kuruṣva cāstrāṇi bahūni sadyaḥ
110.d:
निर्जीवतां प्राप्तम् अभीक्ष्य देवाः
कलेवरं तस्य सुराश् च सम्यक्
त्वष्टारम् अप्य् ऊचुर् अतित्वरन्तः
कुरुष्व चास्त्राणि बहूनि सद्यः
110.m: Observing that his body had become lifeless, / the deities and gods, in great haste, / spoke even to Tvaṣṭṛ: / "Fashion many weapons at once!"

110.s:
sa cāpi tān āha kathaṃ nu kāryaṃ
kalevaraṃ brāhmaṇasyeha devāḥ
bibhemi kartuṃ dāruṇaṃ cākṣamo 'haṃ
vidāritāny āyudhāny uttamāni
110.d:
स चापि तान् आह कथं नु कार्यं
कलेवरं ब्राह्मणस्येह देवाः
बिभेमि कर्तुं दारुणं चाक्षमो ऽहं
विदारितान्य् आयुधान्य् उत्तमानि
110.m: He too said to them: "How should this be done / to the body of a brahmin here, O gods? / I am afraid to do something cruel, and I am unable / to fashion excellent weapons from what has been torn apart."

110.s:
devā ūcuḥ
vajraṃ mukhaṃ vaḥ kriyate hitārthaṃ
gāvo devair āyudhārthaṃ kṣaṇena
dadhīcidehaṃ tu vidārya yūyam
asthīni śuddhāni prayacchatādya
110.d:
देवा ऊचुः
वज्रं मुखं वः क्रियते हितार्थं
गावो देवैर् आयुधार्थं क्षणेन
दधीचिदेहं तु विदार्य यूयम्
अस्थीनि शुद्धानि प्रयच्छताद्य
110.m:
The gods said:
"Your mouth is made into a thunderbolt for the sake of benefit; / the cows were created by the gods in an instant for the sake of weapons. / Tearing apart Dadhīci's body, / do you provide clean bones today."

110.s:
brahmovāca
tā devavākyāc ca tathaiva cakruḥ
saṃlihya cāsthīni daduḥ surāṇām
surās tvarā jagmur adīnasattvāḥ
svam ālayaṃ cāpi tathaiva gāvaḥ
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ता देववाक्याच् च तथैव चक्रुः
संलिह्य चास्थीनि ददुः सुराणाम्
सुरास् त्वरा जग्मुर् अदीनसत्त्वाः
स्वम् आलयं चापि तथैव गावः
110.m:
Brahmā said:
At the word of the gods, they did just so; / licking the bones clean, they gave them to the gods. / With minds relieved, the gods departed in haste, / and the cows likewise went to their own dwelling.

110.s:
kṛtvā tathāstrāṇi ca devatānāṃ
tvaṣṭā jagāmātha surājñayā tadā
tataś cirāc chīlavatī subhadrā
bhartuḥ priyā bālagarbhā tvarantī
110.d:
कृत्वा तथास्त्राणि च देवतानां
त्वष्टा जगामाथ सुराज्ञया तदा
ततश् चिराच् छीलवती सुभद्रा
भर्तुः प्रिया बालगर्भा त्वरन्ती
110.m: Having fashioned the weapons for the deities, / Tvaṣṭṛ then departed at the gods' command. / Then after a long time, the virtuous and auspicious one, / beloved of her husband and pregnant with a child, hurried along,

110.s:
kare gṛhītvā kalaśaṃ vāripūrṇam
umāṃ natvā phalapuṣpaiḥ sametya
agniṃ ca bhartāram athāśramaṃ ca
saṃdraṣṭukāmā hy ājagāmātha śīghram
110.d:
करे गृहीत्वा कलशं वारिपूर्णम्
उमां नत्वा फलपुष्पैः समेत्य
अग्निं च भर्तारम् अथाश्रमं च
संद्रष्टुकामा ह्य् आजगामाथ शीघ्रम्
110.m: carrying in her hand a pitcher filled with water, / having bowed to Umā, returning with fruits and flowers, / desiring to see the fire, her husband, and the hermitage; / indeed she arrived quickly.

110.s:
āgacchantīṃ tāṃ prātitheyīṃ tadānīṃ
nivārayām āsa tadolkapātaḥ
sā saṃbhramād āgatā cāśramaṃ svaṃ
naivāpaśyat tatra bhartāram agre
110.d:
आगच्छन्तीं तां प्रातिथेयीं तदानीं
निवारयाम् आस तदोल्कपातः
सा संभ्रमाद् आगता चाश्रमं स्वं
नैवापश्यत् तत्र भर्तारम् अग्रे
110.m: As Prātitheyī was coming at that time, / the fall of a meteor restrained her then. / Confused, she arrived at her hermitage / and did not see her husband before her.

110.s:
kva vā gataś ceti savismayā sā
papraccha cāgniṃ prātitheyī tadānīm
agnis tadovāca savistaraṃ tāṃ
devāgamaṃ yācanaṃ vai śarīre
110.d:
क्व वा गतश् चेति सविस्मया सा
पप्रच्छ चाग्निं प्रातिथेयी तदानीम्
अग्निस् तदोवाच सविस्तरं तां
देवागमं याचनं वै शरीरे
110.m: Perplexed, Prātitheyī then asked the fire: / "Where has he gone?" / The fire then told her in detail / of the gods' arrival, their begging for the body,

110.s:
asthnām upādānam atha prayāṇaṃ
śrutvā sarvaṃ duḥkhitā sā babhūva
duḥkhodvegāt sā papātātha pṛthvyāṃ
mandaṃ mandaṃ vahnināśvāsitā ca
110.d:
अस्थ्नाम् उपादानम् अथ प्रयाणं
श्रुत्वा सर्वं दुःखिता सा बभूव
दुःखोद्वेगात् सा पपाताथ पृथ्व्यां
मन्दं मन्दं वह्निनाश्वासिता च
110.m: the taking of the bones, and their departure. / Hearing everything, she was filled with sorrow; / from the agitation of grief, she fell to the ground, / and was slowly consoled by the fire.

110.s:
prātitheyy uvāca brahmovāca prātitheyy uvāca
utpadyate yat tu vināśi sarvaṃ
na śocyam astīti manuṣyaloke
govipradevārtham iha tyajanti
prāṇān priyān puṇyabhājo manuṣyāḥ
110.d:
प्रातिथेय्य् उवाच ब्रह्मोवाच प्रातिथेय्य् उवाच
उत्पद्यते यत् तु विनाशि सर्वं
न शोच्यम् अस्तीति मनुष्यलोके
गोविप्रदेवार्थम् इह त्यजन्ति
प्राणान् प्रियान् पुण्यभाजो मनुष्याः
110.m:
Prātitheyī said:
Whatever is born is all perishable;
there is nothing to be mourned in the world of men.
In this world, meritorious men surrender their dear lives
for the sake of cows, brāhmaṇas, and the gods.

110.s:
saṃsāracakre parivartamāne
dehaṃ samarthaṃ dharmayuktaṃ tv avāpya
priyān prāṇān devaviprārthahetos
te vai dhanyāḥ prāṇino ye tyajanti
110.d:
संसारचक्रे परिवर्तमाने
देहं समर्थं धर्मयुक्तं त्व् अवाप्य
प्रियान् प्राणान् देवविप्रार्थहेतोस्
ते वै धन्याः प्राणिनो ये त्यजन्ति
110.m: As the wheel of saṃsāra turns, / having obtained an able body endowed with dharma, / fortunate indeed are those living beings who surrender / their beloved lives for the sake of gods and brahmins.

110.s:
prāṇāḥ sarve 'syāpi dehānvitasya
yātāro vai nātra saṃdehaleśaḥ
evaṃ jñātvā vipragodevadīnādy
arthaṃ cainān utsṛjantīśvarās te
110.d:
प्राणाः सर्वे ऽस्यापि देहान्वितस्य
यातारो वै नात्र संदेहलेशः
एवं ज्ञात्वा विप्रगोदेवदीनाद्य्
अर्थं चैनान् उत्सृजन्तीश्वरास् ते
110.m: All the vital breaths of this embodied one / will surely depart; there is not the slightest doubt of this. / Knowing this, those lords give them up / for the sake of brahmins, cows, gods, and the destitute.

110.s:
nivāryamāṇo 'pi mayā prapannayā
cakāra devāstraparigrahaṃ saḥ
manogataṃ vetty athavā vidhātuḥ
ko martyalokātigaceṣṭitasya
110.d:
निवार्यमाणो ऽपि मया प्रपन्नया
चकार देवास्त्रपरिग्रहं सः
मनोगतं वेत्त्य् अथवा विधातुः
को मर्त्यलोकातिगचेष्टितस्य
110.m: Though restrained by me, who took refuge in him, / he took upon himself the weapons of the gods. / Or who knows the intention of the Ordainer, / whose deeds transcend the mortal world?"

110.s:
brahmovāca
ity evam uktvāpūjya cāgnīn yathāvad
bhartus tvacā lomabhiḥ sā viveśa
garbhasthitaṃ bālakaṃ prātitheyī
kukṣiṃ vidāryātha kare gṛhītvā
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् एवम् उक्त्वापूज्य चाग्नीन् यथावद्
भर्तुस् त्वचा लोमभिः सा विवेश
गर्भस्थितं बालकं प्रातिथेयी
कुक्षिं विदार्याथ करे गृहीत्वा
110.m:
Brahmā said:
Having spoken thus and properly worshipped the fires, / she entered [the fire] along with her husband's skin and hair. / Slitting her abdomen, Prātitheyī / took in her hand the boy resting in the womb.

110.s:
prātitheyy uvāca
pitrā hīno bandhubhir gotrajaiś ca
mātrā hīno bālakaḥ sarva eva
rakṣantu sarve 'pi ca bhūtasaṃghās
tathauṣadhyo bālakaṃ lokapālāḥ
110.d:
प्रातिथेय्य् उवाच
पित्रा हीनो बन्धुभिर् गोत्रजैश् च
मात्रा हीनो बालकः सर्व एव
रक्षन्तु सर्वे ऽपि च भूतसंघास्
तथौषध्यो बालकं लोकपालाः
110.m:
Prātitheyī said:
"Bereft of father, kinsmen, and agnates, / this child is completely bereft of mother. / Let all the hosts of beings, the herbs, / and the guardians of the world protect the child!

110.s:
ye bālakaṃ mātṛpitṛprahīṇaṃ
sanirviśeṣaṃ svatanuprarūḍhaiḥ
paśyanti rakṣanti ta eva nūnaṃ
brahmādikānām api vandanīyāḥ
110.d:
ये बालकं मातृपितृप्रहीणं
सनिर्विशेषं स्वतनुप्ररूढैः
पश्यन्ति रक्षन्ति त एव नूनं
ब्रह्मादिकानाम् अपि वन्दनीयाः
110.m: Those who look upon and protect a child / bereft of mother and father / without distinction from those sprung from their own body / are truly worthy of worship even by Brahmā and the others."

110.s:
brahmovāca
ity uktvā cātyajad bālaṃ bhartṛcittaparāyaṇā
pippalānāṃ samīpe tu nyasya bālaṃ namasya ca //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा चात्यजद् बालं भर्तृचित्तपरायणा
पिप्पलानां समीपे तु न्यस्य बालं नमस्य च ॥
110.m:
Brahmā said:
Having spoken thus, she, devoted in heart to her husband, abandoned the boy, / placing the boy near the pippala trees and bowing down to him.

110.s:
agniṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yajñapātrasamanvitā
viveśāgniṃ prātitheyī bhartrā saha divaṃ yayau //
110.d:
अग्निं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य यज्ञपात्रसमन्विता
विवेशाग्निं प्रातिथेयी भर्त्रा सह दिवं ययौ ॥
110.m: Circumambulating the fire, equipped with the sacrificial vessels, / Prātitheyī entered the fire and went to heaven with her husband.

110.s:
ruruduś cāśramasthā ye vṛkṣāś ca vanavāsinaḥ
putravat poṣitā yena ṛṣiṇā ca dadhīcinā //
110.d:
रुरुदुश् चाश्रमस्था ये वृक्षाश् च वनवासिनः
पुत्रवत् पोषिता येन ऋषिणा च दधीचिना ॥
110.m: And the trees standing in the hermitage, the dwellers in the forest, / who had been nurtured like sons by the sage Dadhīci, wept.

110.s:
vinā tena na jīvāmas tayā mātrā vinā tathā
mṛgāś ca pakṣiṇaḥ sarve vṛkṣāḥ procuḥ parasparam //
110.d:
विना तेन न जीवामस् तया मात्रा विना तथा
मृगाश् च पक्षिणः सर्वे वृक्षाः प्रोचुः परस्परम् ॥
110.m: "Without him we cannot live, nor without that mother," / so said all the beasts, the birds, and the trees to one another.

110.s:
vṛkṣā ūcuḥ
svargam āseduṣoḥ pitros tadapatyeṣv akṛtrimam
ye kurvanty aniśaṃ snehaṃ ta eva kṛtino narāḥ //
110.d:
वृक्षा ऊचुः
स्वर्गम् आसेदुषोः पित्रोस् तदपत्येष्व् अकृत्रिमम्
ये कुर्वन्त्य् अनिशं स्नेहं त एव कृतिनो नराः ॥
110.m:
The trees said:
"Those men are truly accomplished who continuously show unfeigned love / towards the offspring of their parents when they have reached heaven.

110.s:
dadhīciḥ prātitheyī vā vīkṣate 'smān yathā purā
tathā pitā na mātā vā dhig asmān pāpino vayam //
110.d:
दधीचिः प्रातिथेयी वा वीक्षते ऽस्मान् यथा पुरा
तथा पिता न माता वा धिग् अस्मान् पापिनो वयम् ॥
110.m: Neither our father nor our mother looks upon us / as Dadhīci or Prātitheyī did in the past; shame on us, we are sinners!

110.s:
asmākam api sarveṣām ataḥ prabhṛti niścitam
bālo dadhīciḥ prātitheyī bālo dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ //
110.d:
अस्माकम् अपि सर्वेषाम् अतः प्रभृति निश्चितम्
बालो दधीचिः प्रातिथेयी बालो धर्मः सनातनः ॥
110.m: Henceforth, it is decided for all of us as well: / the boy is Dadhīci, Prātitheyī; the boy is eternal dharma."

110.s:
brahmovāca
evam uktvā tadauṣadhyo vanaspatisamanvitāḥ
somaṃ rājānam abhyetya yācire 'mṛtam uttamam //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् उक्त्वा तदौषध्यो वनस्पतिसमन्विताः
सोमं राजानम् अभ्येत्य याचिरे ऽमृतम् उत्तमम् ॥
110.m:
Brahmā said:
Having spoken thus, the medicinal herbs along with the lords of the forest / approached King Soma and begged for the excellent nectar.

110.s:
sa cāpi dattavāṃs tebhyaḥ somo 'mṛtam anuttamam
dadur bālāya te cāpi amṛtaṃ suravallabham //
110.d:
स चापि दत्तवांस् तेभ्यः सोमो ऽमृतम् अनुत्तमम्
ददुर् बालाय ते चापि अमृतं सुरवल्लभम् ॥
110.m: And Soma gave them the unexcelled nectar; / and they gave the nectar dear to the gods to the boy.

110.s:
sa tena tṛpto vavṛdhe śuklapakṣe yathā śaśī
pippalaiḥ pālito yasmāt pippalādaḥ sa bālakaḥ
pravṛddhaḥ pippalān evam uvāca tv ativismitaḥ //
110.d:
स तेन तृप्तो ववृधे शुक्लपक्षे यथा शशी
पिप्पलैः पालितो यस्मात् पिप्पलादः स बालकः
प्रवृद्धः पिप्पलान् एवम् उवाच त्व् अतिविस्मितः ॥
110.m: Nourished by that, he grew like the moon in the bright fortnight. / Because he was protected by the pippala trees, that boy was named Pippalāda; / having grown up, he spoke thus to the pippala trees in great wonder:

110.s:
pippalāda uvāca
mānuṣebhyo mānuṣās tu jāyante pakṣibhiḥ khagāḥ
bījebhyo vīrudho loke vaiṣamyaṃ naiva dṛśyate
vārkṣas tv ahaṃ kathaṃ jāto hastapādādijīvavān //
110.d:
पिप्पलाद उवाच
मानुषेभ्यो मानुषास् तु जायन्ते पक्षिभिः खगाः
बीजेभ्यो वीरुधो लोके वैषम्यं नैव दृश्यते
वार्क्षस् त्व् अहं कथं जातो हस्तपादादिजीववान् ॥
110.m:
Pippalāda said:
"From human beings humans are born; from birds come fowl; / from seeds come climbing plants in the world; no anomaly is seen. / But being born of trees, how am I a living being with hands, feet, and the rest?"

110.s:
brahmovāca
vṛkṣās tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sarvam ūcur yathākramam
dadhīcer maraṇaṃ sādhvyās tathā cāgnipraveśanam //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
वृक्षास् तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वम् ऊचुर् यथाक्रमम्
दधीचेर् मरणं साध्व्यास् तथा चाग्निप्रवेशनम् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing his words, the trees told him everything in order: / the death of Dadhīci and the virtuous woman's entry into the fire,

110.s:
asthnāṃ saṃharaṇaṃ devair etat sarvaṃ savistaram
śrutvā duḥkhasamāviṣṭo nipapāta tadā bhuvi //
110.d:
अस्थ्नां संहरणं देवैर् एतत् सर्वं सविस्तरम्
श्रुत्वा दुःखसमाविष्टो निपपात तदा भुवि ॥
110.m: and the gathering of the bones by the gods—all this in detail. / Hearing it, overwhelmed with sorrow, he fell to the earth.

110.s:
āśvāsitaḥ punar vṛkṣair vākyair dharmārthasaṃhitaiḥ
āśvastaḥ sa punaḥ prāha tadauṣadhivanaspatīn //
110.d:
आश्वासितः पुनर् वृक्षैर् वाक्यैर् धर्मार्थसंहितैः
आश्वस्तः स पुनः प्राह तदौषधिवनस्पतीन् ॥
110.m: Consoled again by the trees with words endowed with dharma and purpose, / reassured, he then spoke once more to the herbs and lords of the forest:

110.s:
pippalāda uvāca
pitṛhantṝn haniṣye 'haṃ nānyathā jīvituṃ kṣamaḥ
pitur mitrāṇi śatrūṃś ca tathā putro 'nuvartate //
110.d:
पिप्पलाद उवाच
पितृहन्तॄन् हनिष्ये ऽहं नान्यथा जीवितुं क्षमः
पितुर् मित्राणि शत्रूंश् च तथा पुत्रो ऽनुवर्तते ॥
110.m: Pippalāda said: / "I shall kill the murderers of my parents; I am unable to live otherwise. / A son follows his father's friends and enemies alike.

110.s:
sa eva putro yo 'nyas tu putrarūpo ripuḥ smṛtaḥ
vadanti pitṛmitrāṇi tārayanty ahitān api //
110.d:
स एव पुत्रो यो ऽन्यस् तु पुत्ररूपो रिपुः स्मृतः
वदन्ति पितृमित्राणि तारयन्त्य् अहितान् अपि ॥
110.m: He alone is a son; another who merely takes the form of a son is considered an enemy. / They say that a father's friends deliver even those who are hostile."

110.s:
brahmovāca
vṛkṣās taṃ bālam ādāya somāntikam athāyayuḥ
bālavākyaṃ tu te vṛkṣāḥ somāyātha nyavedayan
śrutvā somo 'pi taṃ bālaṃ pippalādam abhāṣata //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
वृक्षास् तं बालम् आदाय सोमान्तिकम् अथाययुः
बालवाक्यं तु ते वृक्षाः सोमायाथ न्यवेदयन्
श्रुत्वा सोमो ऽपि तं बालं पिप्पलादम् अभाषत ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Taking the boy with them, the trees then approached Soma. / Those trees reported the boy's words to Soma. / Having heard them, Soma also spoke to the boy Pippalāda:

110.s:
soma uvāca
gṛhāṇa vidyāṃ vidhivat samagrāṃ
tapaḥsamṛddhiṃ ca śubhāṃ ca vācam
śauryaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca balaṃ ca buddhiṃ
saṃprāpsyase putra madājñayā tvam
110.d:
सोम उवाच
गृहाण विद्यां विधिवत् समग्रां
तपःसमृद्धिं च शुभां च वाचम्
शौर्यं च रूपं च बलं च बुद्धिं
संप्राप्स्यसे पुत्र मदाज्ञया त्वम्
110.m: Soma said: / "Accept complete knowledge according to the rules, / the prosperity of austerity, and auspicious speech. / Heroism, beauty, strength, and intellect / you shall obtain by my command, my son."

110.s:
brahmovāca
pippalādas tam apy āha oṣadhīśaṃ vinītavat //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पिप्पलादस् तम् अप्य् आह ओषधीशं विनीतवत् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Pippalāda also spoke humbly to that lord of plants:

110.s:
pippalāda uvāca
sarvam etad vṛthā manye pitṛhantṛviniṣkṛtim
na karomy atra yāvac ca tasmāt tat prathamaṃ vada //
110.d:
पिप्पलाद उवाच
सर्वम् एतद् वृथा मन्ये पितृहन्तृविनिष्कृतिम्
न करोम्य् अत्र यावच् च तस्मात् तत् प्रथमं वद ॥
110.m: Pippalāda said: / "I consider all this useless as long as I do not / take vengeance upon the murderers of my parents here; therefore, tell me about that first:

110.s:
yasmin deśe yatra kāle yasmin deve ca mantrake
yatra tīrthe ca sidhyeta matsaṃkalpaḥ surottama //
110.d:
यस्मिन् देशे यत्र काले यस्मिन् देवे च मन्त्रके
यत्र तीर्थे च सिध्येत मत्संकल्पः सुरोत्तम ॥
110.m: in what land, at what time, through which deity and which mantra, / and at which tīrtha my resolve may succeed, O best of gods?"

110.s:
brahmovāca
candraḥ prāha ciraṃ dhyātvā bhuktir vā muktir eva vā
sarvaṃ maheśvarād devāj jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
चन्द्रः प्राह चिरं ध्यात्वा भुक्तिर् वा मुक्तिर् एव वा
सर्वं महेश्वराद् देवाज् जायते नात्र संशयः ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / After contemplating for a long time, the Moon said: "Whether worldly enjoyment or liberation, / everything arises from the god Maheśvara; there is no doubt about this."

110.s:
sa somaṃ punar apy āha kathaṃ drakṣye maheśvaram
bālo 'haṃ bālabuddhiś ca na sāmarthyaṃ tapas tathā //
110.d:
स सोमं पुनर् अप्य् आह कथं द्रक्ष्ये महेश्वरम्
बालो ऽहं बालबुद्धिश् च न सामर्थ्यं तपस् तथा ॥
110.m: He spoke once more to Soma: "How shall I behold Maheśvara? / I am a boy with a child's understanding; I have neither power nor austerity."

110.s:
candra uvāca
gautamīṃ gaccha bhadra tvaṃ stuhi cakreśvaraṃ haram
prasannas tu taveśāno hy alpāyāsena vatsaka //
110.d:
चन्द्र उवाच
गौतमीं गच्छ भद्र त्वं स्तुहि चक्रेश्वरं हरम्
प्रसन्नस् तु तवेशानो ह्य् अल्पायासेन वत्सक ॥
110.m: The Moon said: / "Go to the Gautamī, auspicious boy, and praise Hara, the lord of the discus. / For the Lord will be gracious to you with little effort, little one.

110.s:
prīto bhaven mahādevaḥ sākṣāt kāruṇikaḥ śivaḥ
āste sākṣātkṛtaḥ śaṃbhur viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā //
110.d:
प्रीतो भवेन् महादेवः साक्षात् कारुणिकः शिवः
आस्ते साक्षात्कृतः शंभुर् विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ॥
110.m: Mahādeva, Śiva himself, full of compassion, will be pleased. / Śambhu abides there, made manifest by Viṣṇu the almighty.

110.s:
varaṃ ca dattavān viṣṇoś cakraṃ ca tridaśārcitam
gaccha tatra mahābuddhe daṇḍake gautamīṃ nadīm //
110.d:
वरं च दत्तवान् विष्णोश् चक्रं च त्रिदशार्चितम्
गच्छ तत्र महाबुद्धे दण्डके गौतमीं नदीम् ॥
110.m: And he granted a boon and the discus worshipped by the thirty [gods] to Viṣṇu. / Go there, O highly intelligent one, to the Gautamī river in the Daṇḍaka [Forest].

110.s:
cakreśvaraṃ nāma tīrthaṃ jānanty oṣadhayas tu tat
taṃ gatvā stuhi deveśaṃ sarvabhāvena śaṃkaram
sa te prītamanās tāta sarvān kāmān pradāsyati //
110.d:
चक्रेश्वरं नाम तीर्थं जानन्त्य् ओषधयस् तु तत्
तं गत्वा स्तुहि देवेशं सर्वभावेन शंकरम्
स ते प्रीतमनास् तात सर्वान् कामान् प्रदास्यति ॥
110.m: The herbs know that tīrtha named Cakreśvara. / Go there and praise the lord of gods, Śaṅkara, with all your being; / he, pleased in his heart, my dear, will grant all your desires."

110.s:
brahmovāca
tad rājavacanād brahman pippalādo mahāmuniḥ
ājagāma jagannātho yatra rudraḥ sa cakradaḥ //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् राजवचनाद् ब्रह्मन् पिप्पलादो महामुनिः
आजगाम जगन्नाथो यत्र रुद्रः स चक्रदः ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / At the word of that king [of the stars], O brahmin, the great sage Pippalāda, / the master of the world, went to the place where that Rudra, giver of the discus, resided.

110.s:
taṃ bālaṃ kṛpayāviṣṭāḥ pippalāḥ svāśramān yayuḥ
godāvaryāṃ tataḥ snātvā natvā tribhuvaneśvaram
tuṣṭāva sarvabhāvena pippalādaḥ śivaṃ śuciḥ //
110.d:
तं बालं कृपयाविष्टाः पिप्पलाः स्वाश्रमान् ययुः
गोदावर्यां ततः स्नात्वा नत्वा त्रिभुवनेश्वरम्
तुष्टाव सर्वभावेन पिप्पलादः शिवं शुचिः ॥
110.m: Filled with compassion for the boy, the pippala trees returned to their hermitages. / Then, having bathed in the Godāvarī and bowed down to the lord of the three worlds, / Pippalāda, purified, praised Śiva with all his being:

110.s:
pippalāda uvāca
sarvāṇi karmāṇi vihāya dhīrās
tyaktaiṣaṇā nirjitacittavātāḥ
yaṃ yānti muktyai śaraṇaṃ prayatnāt
tam ādidevaṃ praṇamāmi śaṃbhum
110.d:
पिप्पलाद उवाच
सर्वाणि कर्माणि विहाय धीरास्
त्यक्तैषणा निर्जितचित्तवाताः
यं यान्ति मुक्त्यै शरणं प्रयत्नात्
तम् आदिदेवं प्रणमामि शंभुम्
110.m: Pippalāda said: / "Abandoning all rituals, having cast off cravings, their breath and thoughts subdued, / the steadfast take refuge in him with effort for liberation— / to that primordial god, Śambhu, I bow.

110.s:
yaḥ sarvasākṣī sakalāntarātmā
sarveśvaraḥ sarvakalānidhānam
vijñāya maccittagataṃ samastaṃ
sa me smarāriḥ karuṇāṃ karotu
110.d:
यः सर्वसाक्षी सकलान्तरात्मा
सर्वेश्वरः सर्वकलानिधानम्
विज्ञाय मच्चित्तगतं समस्तं
स मे स्मरारिः करुणां करोतु
110.m: He who is the witness of all, the inner self of all things, / the lord of all, the repository of all arts— / having perceived everything dwelling within my heart, / may that enemy of Smara show compassion to me.

110.s:
digīśvarāñ jitya surārcitasya
kailāsam āndolayataḥ purāreḥ
aṅguṣṭhakṛtyaiva rasātalād adho
gatasya tasyaiva daśānanasya
110.d:
दिगीश्वराञ् जित्य सुरार्चितस्य
कैलासम् आन्दोलयतः पुरारेः
अङ्गुष्ठकृत्यैव रसातलाद् अधो
गतस्य तस्यैव दशाननस्य
110.m: When the ten-necked [Rāvaṇa], having conquered the regents of the directions, / shook Kailāsa, the seat of the enemy of Pura worshipped by the gods, / by merely pressing down your toe, he went / down beneath the underworld.

110.s:
ālūnakāyasya giraṃ niśamya
vihasya devyā saha dattam iṣṭam
tasmai prasannaḥ kupito 'pi tadvad
ayuktadātāsi maheśvara tvam
110.d:
आलूनकायस्य गिरं निशम्य
विहस्य देव्या सह दत्तम् इष्टम्
तस्मै प्रसन्नः कुपितो ऽपि तद्वद्
अयुक्तदातासि महेश्वर त्वम्
110.m: Hearing the cry of him whose body was mutilated, / you smiled with the Goddess and granted him his desire; / pleased with him, though previously angered in that manner, / you are the giver of the unearned, O Maheśvara!

110.s:
sautrāmaṇīm ṛddhim adhaḥ sa cakre
yo 'rcāṃ harau nityam atīva kṛtvā
bāṇaḥ praśasyaḥ kṛtavān uccapūjāṃ
ramyāṃ manojñāṃ śaśikhaṇḍamauleḥ
110.d:
सौत्रामणीम् ऋद्धिम् अधः स चक्रे
यो ऽर्चां हरौ नित्यम् अतीव कृत्वा
बाणः प्रशस्यः कृतवान् उच्चपूजां
रम्यां मनोज्ञां शशिखण्डमौलेः
110.m: Praised is Bāṇa, who placed below him the prosperity of Sautrāmaṇī, / who, constantly making immense worship of Hara, / performed exalted, beautiful, and pleasing worship / of the one whose crest is a crescent moon.

110.s:
jitvā ripūn devagaṇān prapūjya
guruṃ namaskartum agād viśākhaḥ
cukopa dṛṣṭvā gaṇanātham ūḍham
aṅke tam āropya jahāsa somaḥ
110.d:
जित्वा रिपून् देवगणान् प्रपूज्य
गुरुं नमस्कर्तुम् अगाद् विशाखः
चुकोप दृष्ट्वा गणनाथम् ऊढम्
अङ्के तम् आरोप्य जहास सोमः
110.m: Having conquered his enemies and worshipped the hosts of gods, / Viśākha went to bow down to his father. / Seeing the lord of gaṇas already seated [there], he grew angry; / lifting him onto his lap, Soma laughed.

110.s:
īśāṅkarūḍho 'pi śiśusvabhāvān
na mātur aṅkaṃ pramumoca bālaḥ
kruddhaṃ sutaṃ bodhitum apy aśaktas
tato 'rdhanāritvam avāpa somaḥ
110.d:
ईशाङ्करूढो ऽपि शिशुस्वभावान्
न मातुर् अङ्कं प्रमुमोच बालः
क्रुद्धं सुतं बोधितुम् अप्य् अशक्तस्
ततो ऽर्धनारित्वम् अवाप सोमः
110.m: Even while seated on the Lord's lap, by a child's nature, / the boy did not leave his mother's lap. / Unable to appease his angry son, / Soma then assumed the form of half-woman."

110.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ svayaṃbhūḥ suprītaḥ pippalādam abhāṣata //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः स्वयंभूः सुप्रीतः पिप्पलादम् अभाषत ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Then Svayambhū, deeply pleased, spoke to Pippalāda:

110.s:
śiva uvāca
varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te pippalāda yathepsitam //
110.d:
शिव उवाच
वरं वरय भद्रं ते पिप्पलाद यथेप्सितम् ॥
110.m: Śiva said: / "Choose a boon as you desire, Pippalāda; may it be well with you!"

110.s:
pippalāda uvāca
hato devair mahādeva pitā mama mahāyaśāḥ
adāmbhikaḥ satyavādī tathā mātā pativratā //
110.d:
पिप्पलाद उवाच
हतो देवैर् महादेव पिता मम महायशाः
अदाम्भिकः सत्यवादी तथा माता पतिव्रता ॥
110.m: Pippalāda said: / "O Mahādeva, my renowned father, / unpretentious and truthful, was slain by the gods, and so was my faithful mother.

110.s:
devebhyaś ca tayor nāśaṃ śrutvā nātha savistaram
duḥkhakopasamāviṣṭo nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe //
110.d:
देवेभ्यश् च तयोर् नाशं श्रुत्वा नाथ सविस्तरम्
दुःखकोपसमाविष्टो नाहं जीवितुम् उत्सहे ॥
110.m: Hearing in detail of their destruction caused by the gods, O Lord, / I am filled with grief and anger, and I have no desire to live.

110.s:
tasmān me dehi sāmarthyaṃ nāśayeyaṃ surān yathā
avadhyasevyas trailokye tvam eva śaśiśekhara //
110.d:
तस्मान् मे देहि सामर्थ्यं नाशयेयं सुरान् यथा
अवध्यसेव्यस् त्रैलोक्ये त्वम् एव शशिशेखर ॥
110.m: Therefore, grant me the power so that I may destroy the gods; / you alone, crowned with the crescent moon, are to be served by those who are unslayable in the three worlds."

110.s:
īśvara uvāca
tṛtīyaṃ nayanaṃ draṣṭuṃ yadi śaknoṣi me 'nagha
tataḥ samartho bhavitā devāṃś chedayituṃ bhavān //
110.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
तृतीयं नयनं द्रष्टुं यदि शक्नोषि मे ऽनघ
ततः समर्थो भविता देवांश् छेदयितुं भवान् ॥
110.m: The Lord said: / "If you are able to behold my third eye, O sinless one, / then you will become capable of destroying the gods."

110.s:
brahmovāca
tato draṣṭuṃ manaś cakre tṛtīyaṃ locanaṃ vibhoḥ
na śaśāka tadovāca na śakto 'smīti śaṃkaram //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो द्रष्टुं मनश् चक्रे तृतीयं लोचनं विभोः
न शशाक तदोवाच न शक्तो ऽस्मीति शंकरम् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Then he resolved to behold the third eye of the omnipresent Lord; / he was not able, and then he said to Śaṅkara: 'I am not able.'

110.s:
īśvara uvāca
kiṃcit kuru tapo bāla yadā drakṣyasi locanam
tṛtīyaṃ tvaṃ tadābhīṣṭaṃ prāpsyase nātra saṃśayaḥ //
110.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
किंचित् कुरु तपो बाल यदा द्रक्ष्यसि लोचनम्
तृतीयं त्वं तदाभीष्टं प्राप्स्यसे नात्र संशयः ॥
110.m: The Lord said: / "Perform a little austerity, child. When you behold / the third eye, then you will obtain your desire; of this there is no doubt."

110.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutveśānavākyaṃ tapase kṛtaniścayaḥ
dadhīcisūnur dharmātmā tatraiva bahulāḥ samāḥ //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वेशानवाक्यं तपसे कृतनिश्चयः
दधीचिसूनुर् धर्मात्मा तत्रैव बहुलाः समाः ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard these words of the Lord, resolved upon austerity, / the righteous son of Dadhīci spent many years right there.

110.s:
śivadhyānaikanirato bālo 'pi balavān iva
pratyahaṃ prātar utthāya snātvā natvā gurūn kramāt //
110.d:
शिवध्यानैकनिरतो बालो ऽपि बलवान् इव
प्रत्यहं प्रातर् उत्थाय स्नात्वा नत्वा गुरून् क्रमात् ॥
110.m: Wholly devoted to meditation on Śiva, though a boy, as if strong, / rising daily at dawn, bathing, and bowing to his teachers in order,

110.s:
sukhāsīno manaḥ kṛtvā suṣumnāyām ananyadhīḥ
hastasvastikam āropya nābhau vismṛtasaṃsṛtiḥ //
110.d:
सुखासीनो मनः कृत्वा सुषुम्नायाम् अनन्यधीः
हस्तस्वस्तिकम् आरोप्य नाभौ विस्मृतसंसृतिः ॥
110.m: comfortably seated, focusing his mind on the suṣumṇā with single-pointed thought, / placing his crossed hands at the navel, forgetting transmigration,

110.s:
sthānāt sthānāntarotkarṣān vidadhyau śāṃbhavaṃ mahaḥ
dadarśa cakṣur devasya tṛtīyaṃ pippalāśanaḥ
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā vinīta idam abravīt //
110.d:
स्थानात् स्थानान्तरोत्कर्षान् विदध्यौ शांभवं महः
ददर्श चक्षुर् देवस्य तृतीयं पिप्पलाशनः
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा विनीत इदम् अब्रवीत् ॥
110.m: he meditated on the splendor of Śambhu through the elevation from stage to stage; / and that eater of pippala berries saw the third eye of the god. / Folding his hands in reverence, he spoke humbly as follows:

110.s:
pippalāda uvāca
śaṃbhunā devadevena varo dattaḥ purā mama
tārtīyacakṣuṣo jyotir yadā paśyasi tatkṣaṇāt //
110.d:
पिप्पलाद उवाच
शंभुना देवदेवेन वरो दत्तः पुरा मम
तार्तीयचक्षुषो ज्योतिर् यदा पश्यसि तत्क्षणात् ॥
110.m: Pippalāda said: / "A boon was granted to me formerly by Śambhu, the god of gods: / 'From the moment you behold the splendor of the third eye,

110.s:
sarvaṃ te prārthitaṃ sidhyed ity āha tridaśeśvaraḥ
tasmād ripuvināśāya hetubhūtāṃ prayaccha me //
110.d:
सर्वं ते प्रार्थितं सिध्येद् इत्य् आह त्रिदशेश्वरः
तस्माद् रिपुविनाशाय हेतुभूतां प्रयच्छ मे ॥
110.m: all that you request shall be accomplished'—so said the lord of the thirty [gods]. / Therefore, grant me that which will serve as the cause for the destruction of my enemies."

110.s:
tadaiva pippalāḥ procur vaḍavāpi mahādyute
mātā tava prātitheyī vadanty evaṃ divaṃ gatā //
110.d:
तदैव पिप्पलाः प्रोचुर् वडवापि महाद्युते
माता तव प्रातिथेयी वदन्त्य् एवं दिवं गता ॥
110.m: Just then the pippala trees said: "Even as a mare, O you of great splendor, / your mother, Prātitheyī, saying thus, went to heaven:

110.s:
parābhidrohaniratā vismṛtātmahitā narāḥ
itas tato bhrāntacittāḥ patanti narakāvaṭe //
110.d:
पराभिद्रोहनिरता विस्मृतात्महिता नराः
इतस् ततो भ्रान्तचित्ताः पतन्ति नरकावटे ॥
110.m: 'Men devoted to injuring others, having forgotten their own welfare, / their minds wandering here and there, fall into the pit of hell.'"

110.s:
tan mātṛvacanaṃ śrutvā kupitaḥ pippalāśanaḥ
abhimāne jvalaty antaḥ sādhuvādo nirarthakaḥ //
110.d:
तन् मातृवचनं श्रुत्वा कुपितः पिप्पलाशनः
अभिमाने ज्वलत्य् अन्तः साधुवादो निरर्थकः ॥
110.m: Hearing those words of his mother, the eater of pippala berries was enraged; / when pride burns within, good counsel is of no avail.

110.s:
dehi dehīti taṃ prāha kṛtyā netravinirgatā
vaḍaveti smaran vipraḥ kṛtyāpi vaḍavākṛtiḥ //
110.d:
देहि देहीति तं प्राह कृत्या नेत्रविनिर्गता
वडवेति स्मरन् विप्रः कृत्यापि वडवाकृतिः ॥
110.m: "Give! Give!" said to him the kṛtyā that had come forth from his eye. / Thinking of a mare, the vipra [meditated], and the kṛtyā too took the form of a mare.

110.s:
sarvasattvavināśāya prabhūtānalagarbhiṇī
gabhastinī bālagarbhā yā mātā pippalāśinaḥ //
110.d:
सर्वसत्त्वविनाशाय प्रभूतानलगर्भिणी
गभस्तिनी बालगर्भा या माता पिप्पलाशिनः ॥
110.m: Carrying vast fire within her womb for the destruction of all creatures, / radiant, pregnant with a child, she who was the mother of the consumer of pippala berries (Pippalāda)—

110.s:
taddhyānayogāt tu jātā kṛtyā sānalagarbhiṇī
utpannā sā mahāraudrā mṛtyujihveva bhīṣaṇā //
110.d:
तद्ध्यानयोगात् तु जाता कृत्या सानलगर्भिणी
उत्पन्ना सा महारौद्रा मृत्युजिह्वेव भीषणा ॥
110.m: from the yoga of his meditation upon her was born that kṛtyā bearing fire in her womb; / exceedingly fierce she arose, terrifying like the tongue of Death.

110.s:
avocat pippalādaṃ taṃ kiṃ kṛtyaṃ me vadasva tat
pippalādo 'pi tāṃ prāha devān khāda ripūn mama //
110.d:
अवोचत् पिप्पलादं तं किं कृत्यं मे वदस्व तत्
पिप्पलादो ऽपि तां प्राह देवान् खाद रिपून् मम ॥
110.m: She said to that Pippalāda: "Tell me, what is my task?" / And Pippalāda said to her: "Devour the gods, my enemies!"

110.s:
jagrāha sā tathety uktvā pippalādaṃ purasthitam
sa prāha kim idaṃ kṛtye sā cāpy āha tvayoditam //
110.d:
जग्राह सा तथेत्य् उक्त्वा पिप्पलादं पुरस्थितम्
स प्राह किम् इदं कृत्ये सा चाप्य् आह त्वयोदितम् ॥
110.m: Saying "So be it," she seized Pippalāda as he stood before her. / He said: "What is this, kṛtyā?" and she replied: "It was spoken by you—

110.s:
devaiś ca nirmitaṃ dehaṃ tato bhītaḥ śivaṃ yayau
tuṣṭāva devaṃ sa muniḥ kṛtyāṃ prāha tadā śivaḥ //
110.d:
देवैश् च निर्मितं देहं ततो भीतः शिवं ययौ
तुष्टाव देवं स मुनिः कृत्यां प्राह तदा शिवः ॥
110.m: and the body was fashioned by the gods." Thereupon, terrified, he went to Śiva. / The sage praised the god; then Śiva spoke to the kṛtyā:

110.s:
śiva uvāca
yojanāntaḥsthitāñ jīvān na gṛhāṇa madājñayā
tasmād yāhi tato dūraṃ kṛtye kṛtyaṃ tataḥ kuru //
110.d:
शिव उवाच
योजनान्तःस्थिताञ् जीवान् न गृहाण मदाज्ञया
तस्माद् याहि ततो दूरं कृत्ये कृत्यं ततः कुरु ॥
110.m: Śiva said: / "By my command, do not seize living beings situated within a yojana. / Therefore go far from here, kṛtyā, and then do your deed."

110.s:
brahmovāca
tīrthāt tu pippalāt pūrvaṃ yāvad yojanasaṃkhyayā
prātiṣṭhad vaḍavārūpā kṛtyā sā ṛṣinirmitā //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तीर्थात् तु पिप्पलात् पूर्वं यावद् योजनसंख्यया
प्रातिष्ठद् वडवारूपा कृत्या सा ऋषिनिर्मिता ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / But to the east of the Pippala tīrtha, as far as the measure of a yojana, / stood that kṛtyā produced by the ṛṣi, in the form of a mare.

110.s:
tasyāṃ jāto mahān agnir lokasaṃharaṇakṣamaḥ
taṃ dṛṣṭvā vibudhāḥ sarve trastāḥ śaṃbhum upāgaman //
110.d:
तस्यां जातो महान् अग्निर् लोकसंहरणक्षमः
तं दृष्ट्वा विबुधाः सर्वे त्रस्ताः शंभुम् उपागमन् ॥
110.m: From her arose a great fire capable of destroying the worlds. / Seeing it, all the gods were terrified and approached Śaṃbhu.

110.s:
cakreśvaraṃ pippaleśaṃ pippalādena toṣitam
stuvanto bhītamanasaḥ śaṃbhum ūcur divaukasaḥ //
110.d:
चक्रेश्वरं पिप्पलेशं पिप्पलादेन तोषितम्
स्तुवन्तो भीतमनसः शंभुम् ऊचुर् दिवौकसः ॥
110.m: Praising Cakreśvara, Pippaleśa, who had been propitiated by Pippalāda, / the heaven-dwellers, their minds filled with fear, spoke to Śaṃbhu:

110.s:
devā ūcuḥ
rakṣasva śaṃbho kṛtyāsmān bādhate tadbhavānalaḥ
śaraṇaṃ bhava sarveśa bhītānām abhayaprada //
110.d:
देवा ऊचुः
रक्षस्व शंभो कृत्यास्मान् बाधते तद्भवानलः
शरणं भव सर्वेश भीतानाम् अभयप्रद ॥
110.m: The gods said: / "Protect [us], O Śaṃbhu! The kṛtyā afflicts us; the fire arising from her [threatens us]. / Become a refuge, O lord of all, granter of fearlessness to the frightened!

110.s:
sarvataḥ paribhūtānām ārtānāṃ śrāntacetasām
sarveṣām eva jantūnāṃ tvam eva śaraṇaṃ śiva //
110.d:
सर्वतः परिभूतानाम् आर्तानां श्रान्तचेतसाम्
सर्वेषाम् एव जन्तूनां त्वम् एव शरणं शिव ॥
110.m: For those humiliated from every side, distressed, their minds exhausted— / for all creatures whatsoever, you alone are the refuge, O Śiva!

110.s:
ṛṣiṇābhyarthitā kṛtyā tvaccakṣurvahninirgatā
sā jighāṃsati lokāṃs trīṃs tvaṃ nas trātā na cetaraḥ //
110.d:
ऋषिणाभ्यर्थिता कृत्या त्वच्चक्षुर्वह्निनिर्गता
सा जिघांसति लोकांस् त्रींस् त्वं नस् त्राता न चेतरः ॥
110.m: Entreated by the ṛṣi, the kṛtyā has come forth from the fire of your eye; / she desires to destroy the three worlds. You are our protector, and no other!"

110.s:
brahmovāca
tān abravīj jagannātho yojanāntarnivāsinaḥ
na bādhate tv asau kṛtyā tasmād yūyam aharniśam
ihaivāsadhvam amarās tasyā vo na bhayaṃ bhavet //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तान् अब्रवीज् जगन्नाथो योजनान्तर्निवासिनः
न बाधते त्व् असौ कृत्या तस्माद् यूयम् अहर्निशम्
इहैवासध्वम् अमरास् तस्या वो न भयं भवेत् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / The lord of the universe spoke to them: "Those who dwell within a yojana / this kṛtyā does not torment. Therefore, O immortals, / dwell day and night right here; you will have no fear of her."

110.s:
brahmovāca
punar ūcuḥ sureśānaṃ tvayā dattaṃ triviṣṭapam
tat tyaktvātra kathaṃ nātha vatsyāmas tridaśārcita //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुनर् ऊचुः सुरेशानं त्वया दत्तं त्रिविष्टपम्
तत् त्यक्त्वात्र कथं नाथ वत्स्यामस् त्रिदशार्चित ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / They spoke again to the lord of the gods: "The triple heaven was granted by you. / Abandoning that, how shall we dwell here, O lord worshipped by the thirty [gods]?"

110.s:
brahmovāca
devānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā śivo vākyam athābravīt //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
देवानां वचनं श्रुत्वा शिवो वाक्यम् अथाब्रवीत् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard the words of the gods, Śiva then spoke [these] words:

110.s:
śiva uvāca
devo 'sau viśvataścakṣur yo devo viśvatomukhaḥ
yo raśmibhis tu dhamate nityaṃ yo janako mataḥ //
110.d:
शिव उवाच
देवो ऽसौ विश्वतश्चक्षुर् यो देवो विश्वतोमुखः
यो रश्मिभिस् तु धमते नित्यं यो जनको मतः ॥
110.m: Śiva said: / "That god whose eye is everywhere, that god whose face is on all sides, / who radiates heat with his rays, who is considered the eternal progenitor—

110.s:
sa sūrya eka evātra sākṣād rūpeṇa sarvadā
sthitiṃ karotu tanmūrtau bhaviṣyanty akhilāḥ sthitāḥ //
110.d:
स सूर्य एक एवात्र साक्षाद् रूपेण सर्वदा
स्थितिं करोतु तन्मूर्तौ भविष्यन्त्य् अखिलाः स्थिताः ॥
110.m: let that Sūrya alone constantly make his abode here in visible form; / in his form, all will abide firmly established."

110.s:
brahmovāca
tatheti śaṃbhuvacanāt pārijātataros tadā
devā divākaraṃ cakrus tvaṣṭā bhāskaram abravīt //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेति शंभुवचनात् पारिजाततरोस् तदा
देवा दिवाकरं चक्रुस् त्वष्टा भास्करम् अब्रवीत् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Saying "So be it" at Śaṃbhu's word, out of a pārijāta tree / the gods then fashioned the Sun. Tvaṣṭṛ spoke to the Sun:

110.s:
tvaṣṭovāca
ihaivāssva jagatsvāmin rakṣemān vibudhān svayam
svāṃśaiś ca vayam apy atra tiṣṭhāmaḥ śaṃbhusaṃnidhau //
110.d:
त्वष्टोवाच
इहैवास्स्व जगत्स्वामिन् रक्षेमान् विबुधान् स्वयम्
स्वांशैश् च वयम् अप्य् अत्र तिष्ठामः शंभुसंनिधौ ॥
110.m: Tvaṣṭṛ said: / "Dwell right here, O master of the universe, and protect these gods yourself; / and we too, through our portions, will dwell here in the presence of Śaṃbhu."

110.s:
cakreśvarasya parito yāvad yojanasaṃkhyayā
gaṅgāyā ubhayaṃ tīram āsādyāsan surottamāḥ //
110.d:
चक्रेश्वरस्य परितो यावद् योजनसंख्यया
गङ्गाया उभयं तीरम् आसाद्यासन् सुरोत्तमाः ॥
110.m: Around Cakreśvara, as far as the measure of a yojana, / reaching both banks of the Gaṅgā, the foremost of the gods settled.

110.s:
aṅgulyardhārdhamātraṃ tu gaṅgātīraṃ samāśritāḥ
tisraḥ koṭyas tathā pañca śatāni munisattama
tīrthānāṃ tatra vyuṣṭiṃ ca kaḥ śṛṇoti bravīti vā //
110.d:
अङ्गुल्यर्धार्धमात्रं तु गङ्गातीरं समाश्रिताः
तिस्रः कोट्यस् तथा पञ्च शतानि मुनिसत्तम
तीर्थानां तत्र व्युष्टिं च कः शृणोति ब्रवीति वा ॥
110.m: Resorting to the bank of the Gaṅgā by merely a quarter of a finger's width, / [there were] thirty million and five hundred [tīrthas], O best of sages; / and who can hear or tell the efficacy of the tīrthas there?

110.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve vinītāḥ śivam abruvan //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः सुरगणाः सर्वे विनीताः शिवम् अब्रुवन् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Then all the hosts of gods, humble, spoke to Śiva:

110.s:
devā ūcuḥ
pippalādaṃ sureśāna śamaṃ naya jaganmaya //
110.d:
देवा ऊचुः
पिप्पलादं सुरेशान शमं नय जगन्मय ॥
110.m: The gods said: / "O lord of the gods, O you who consist of the universe, bring Pippalāda to peace!"

110.s:
brahmovāca
om ity uktvā jagannāthaḥ pippalādam avocata //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ओम् इत्य् उक्त्वा जगन्नाथः पिप्पलादम् अवोचत ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Saying "Om," the lord of the universe spoke to Pippalāda:

110.s:
śiva uvāca
nāśiteṣv api deveṣu pitā te nāgamiṣyati
dattāḥ pitrā tava prāṇā devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye //
110.d:
शिव उवाच
नाशितेष्व् अपि देवेषु पिता ते नागमिष्यति
दत्ताः पित्रा तव प्राणा देवानां कार्यसिद्धये ॥
110.m: Śiva said: / "Even if the gods are destroyed, your father will not return. / Your father gave his life for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose.

110.s:
dīnārtakaruṇābandhuḥ ko hi tādṛgbhave bhavet
tathā yātā divaṃ tāta tava mātā pativratā //
110.d:
दीनार्तकरुणाबन्धुः को हि तादृग्भवे भवेत्
तथा याता दिवं तात तव माता पतिव्रता ॥
110.m: Who indeed in this world could be such a friend in compassion to the wretched and afflicted? / Likewise, dear boy, your chaste mother has gone to heaven.

110.s:
samā kāpy atra matayā lopāmudrāpy arundhatī
yad asthibhiḥ surāḥ sarve jayinaḥ sukhinaḥ sadā //
110.d:
समा काप्य् अत्र मतया लोपामुद्राप्य् अरुन्धती
यद् अस्थिभिः सुराः सर्वे जयिनः सुखिनः सदा ॥
110.m: In intelligence she is equal to anyone here, even to Lopāmudrā or Arundhatī. / Since by his bones all the gods are always victorious and happy,

110.s:
tenāvāptaṃ yaśaḥ sphītaṃ tava mātrākṣayaṃ kṛtam
tvayā putreṇa sarvatra nātaḥ parataraṃ kṛtam //
110.d:
तेनावाप्तं यशः स्फीतं तव मात्राक्षयं कृतम्
त्वया पुत्रेण सर्वत्र नातः परतरं कृतम् ॥
110.m: abundant fame was attained by him, and it was made imperishable by your mother. / By you, his son, nothing greater than this has been done anywhere.

110.s:
tvatpratāpabhayāt svargāc cyutāṃs tvaṃ pātum arhasi
kāṃdiśīkāṃs tava bhayād amarāṃs trātum arhasi
nārtatrāṇād abhyadhikaṃ sukṛtaṃ kvāpi vidyate //
110.d:
त्वत्प्रतापभयात् स्वर्गाच् च्युतांस् त्वं पातुम् अर्हसि
कांदिशीकांस् तव भयाद् अमरांस् त्रातुम् अर्हसि
नार्तत्राणाद् अभ्यधिकं सुकृतं क्वापि विद्यते ॥
110.m: You ought to protect those fallen from heaven out of fear of your power; / you ought to protect the immortals fleeing in all directions from fear of you. / Nowhere is there any merit superior to the protection of the distressed.

110.s:
yāvad yaśaḥ sphurati cāru manuṣyaloke
ahāni tāvanti divaṃ gatasya
dine dine varṣasaṃkhyā parasmiṃl
loke vāso jāyate nirvikāraḥ
110.d:
यावद् यशः स्फुरति चारु मनुष्यलोके
अहानि तावन्ति दिवं गतस्य
दिने दिने वर्षसंख्या परस्मिंल्
लोके वासो जायते निर्विकारः
110.m: As long as lovely renown shines in the mortal world, / for that many days does one who has gone to heaven / find day after day a changeless dwelling in the higher world, / counted in years.

110.s:
mṛtās ta evātra yaśo na yeṣām
andhās ta eva śrutavarjitā ye
ye dānaśīlā na napuṃsakās te
ye dharmaśīlā na ta eva śocyāḥ
110.d:
मृतास् त एवात्र यशो न येषाम्
अन्धास् त एव श्रुतवर्जिता ये
ये दानशीला न नपुंसकास् ते
ये धर्मशीला न त एव शोच्याः
110.m: Only they who have no renown are truly dead here; / only they who are bereft of learning are truly blind; / only they who are not generous are truly eunuchs; / only they who are devoted to dharma are not to be pitied."

110.s:
brahmovāca
bhāṣitaṃ devadevasya śrutvā śānto 'bhavan muniḥ
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā natvā nātham athābravīt //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
भाषितं देवदेवस्य श्रुत्वा शान्तो ऽभवन् मुनिः
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा नत्वा नाथम् अथाब्रवीत् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing the speech of the god of gods, the sage became peaceful. / Folding his hands in supplication and bowing to the lord, he then spoke:

110.s:
pippalāda uvāca
vāgbhir manobhiḥ kṛtibhiḥ kadācin
mamopakurvanti hite ratā ye
tebhyo hitārthaṃ tv iha cāpareṣāṃ
somaṃ namasyāmi surādipūjyam
110.d:
पिप्पलाद उवाच
वाग्भिर् मनोभिः कृतिभिः कदाचिन्
ममोपकुर्वन्ति हिते रता ये
तेभ्यो हितार्थं त्व् इह चापरेषां
सोमं नमस्यामि सुरादिपूज्यम्
110.m: Pippalāda said: / "To those who, devoted to my welfare, ever assist me / with words, thoughts, and deeds, / and for the sake of their welfare and that of others here, / I bow to Soma, who is worshipped by gods and others.

110.s:
saṃrakṣito yair abhivardhitaś ca
samānagotraś ca samānadharmā
teṣām abhīṣṭāni śivaḥ karotu
bālendumauliṃ praṇato 'smi nityam
110.d:
संरक्षितो यैर् अभिवर्धितश् च
समानगोत्रश् च समानधर्मा
तेषाम् अभीष्टानि शिवः करोतु
बालेन्दुमौलिं प्रणतो ऽस्मि नित्यम्
110.m: May Śiva grant the desires of those by whom I was protected / and brought up, of the same lineage and of the same dharma; / I bow down constantly to the one who wears the crescent moon on his diadem.

110.s:
yair ahaṃ vardhito nityaṃ mātṛvat pitṛvat prabho
tannāmnā jāyatāṃ tīrthaṃ devadeva jagattraye //
110.d:
यैर् अहं वर्धितो नित्यं मातृवत् पितृवत् प्रभो
तन्नाम्ना जायतां तीर्थं देवदेव जगत्त्रये ॥
110.m: By whom I was constantly raised like a mother and like a father, O lord, / let a tīrtha be formed in their name in the three worlds, O god of gods!

110.s:
yaśas tu teṣāṃ bhavitā tebhyo 'ham anṛṇas tataḥ
yāni kṣetrāṇi devānāṃ yāni tīrthāni bhūtale //
110.d:
यशस् तु तेषां भविता तेभ्यो ऽहम् अनृणस् ततः
यानि क्षेत्राणि देवानां यानि तीर्थानि भूतले ॥
110.m: Then there will be fame for them, and from that I will be free of debt to them. / Whatever sacred sites of the gods and whatever tīrthas there are upon the surface of the earth,

110.s:
tebhyo yad idam adhikam anumanyantu devatāḥ
tataḥ kṣame 'haṃ devānām aparādhaṃ nirañjanaḥ //
110.d:
तेभ्यो यद् इदम् अधिकम् अनुमन्यन्तु देवताः
ततः क्षमे ऽहं देवानाम् अपराधं निरञ्जनः ॥
110.m: let the deities agree that this [place] is superior to them. / Then, spotless, I will forgive the offense of the gods."

110.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ samakṣaṃ surasākṣarāṃ giraṃ
sahasracakṣuḥpramukhāṃs tathāgrataḥ
uvāca devā api menire vaco
dadhīciputroditam ādareṇa
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः समक्षं सुरसाक्षरां गिरं
सहस्रचक्षुःप्रमुखांस् तथाग्रतः
उवाच देवा अपि मेनिरे वचो
दधीचिपुत्रोदितम् आदरेण
110.m: Brahmā said: / Then before him he uttered this charming speech in plain words / before the thousand-eyed one [Indra] and the other [gods]; / and the gods also accepted with respect the words / spoken by the son of Dadhīci.

110.s:
bālasya buddhiṃ vinayaṃ ca vidyāṃ
śauryaṃ balaṃ sāhasaṃ satyavācam
pitror bhaktiṃ bhāvaśuddhiṃ viditvā
tadāvādīc chaṃkaraḥ pippalādam
110.d:
बालस्य बुद्धिं विनयं च विद्यां
शौर्यं बलं साहसं सत्यवाचम्
पित्रोर् भक्तिं भावशुद्धिं विदित्वा
तदावादीच् छंकरः पिप्पलादम्
110.m: Recognizing the boy's intellect, modesty, learning, / valour, strength, daring, truthfulness of speech, / devotion to his parents, and purity of heart, / Śaṅkara then said to Pippalāda:

110.s:
śaṃkara uvāca
vatsa yad vai priyaṃ kāmaṃ yac cāpi suravallabham
prāpsyase vada kalyāṇaṃ nānyathā tvaṃ manaḥ kṛthāḥ //
110.d:
शंकर उवाच
वत्स यद् वै प्रियं कामं यच् चापि सुरवल्लभम्
प्राप्स्यसे वद कल्याणं नान्यथा त्वं मनः कृथाः ॥
110.m: Śaṅkara said: / "Dear child, whatever is pleasing and desired, and whatever is dear to the gods, / you shall obtain; state your blessing; do not think otherwise!"

110.s:
pippalāda uvāca
ye gaṅgāyām āplutā dharmaniṣṭhāḥ
saṃpaśyanti tvatpadābjaṃ maheśa
sarvān kāmān āpnuvantu prasahya
dehānte te padam āyāntu śaivam
110.d:
पिप्पलाद उवाच
ये गङ्गायाम् आप्लुता धर्मनिष्ठाः
संपश्यन्ति त्वत्पदाब्जं महेश
सर्वान् कामान् आप्नुवन्तु प्रसह्य
देहान्ते ते पदम् आयान्तु शैवम्
110.m: Pippalāda said: / "Those who, bathed in the Gaṅgā and steadfast in dharma, / behold your lotus feet, O Maheśa, / may they forcefully attain all their desires, / and at the end of their bodies may they go to the abode of Śiva!

110.s:
tātaḥ prāptas tvatpadaṃ cāmbikā me
nātha prāptā pippalaś cāmarāś ca
sukhaṃ prāptā nāthanāthaṃ vilokya
tvāṃ paśyeyus tvatpadaṃ te prayāntu
110.d:
तातः प्राप्तस् त्वत्पदं चाम्बिका मे
नाथ प्राप्ता पिप्पलश् चामराश् च
सुखं प्राप्ता नाथनाथं विलोक्य
त्वां पश्येयुस् त्वत्पदं ते प्रयान्तु
110.m: My father has reached your abode, and my mother, / O lord, has reached it, and the pippala tree and the immortals / have attained happiness having seen the lord of lords; / may they behold you, and may they go to your abode!"

110.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā pippalādaṃ devadevo maheśvaraḥ
abhinandya ca taṃ devaiḥ sārdhaṃ vākyam athābravīt //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा पिप्पलादं देवदेवो महेश्वरः
अभिनन्द्य च तं देवैः सार्धं वाक्यम् अथाब्रवीत् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Having said, “So be it,” to Pippalāda, the god of gods, Maheśvara, / after congratulating him, spoke these words together with the gods:

110.s:
devā api mudā yuktā nirbhayās tatkṛtād bhayāt
idam ūcuḥ sarva eva dādhīcaṃ śivasaṃnidhau //
110.d:
देवा अपि मुदा युक्ता निर्भयास् तत्कृताद् भयात्
इदम् ऊचुः सर्व एव दाधीचं शिवसंनिधौ ॥
110.m: The gods too, filled with joy and freed from fear of the peril he had caused, / all said this to the son of Dadhīci in the presence of Śiva.

110.s:
devā ūcuḥ
surāṇāṃ yad abhīṣṭaṃ ca tvayā kṛtam asaṃśayam
pālitā devadevasya ājñā trailokyamaṇḍanī //
110.d:
देवा ऊचुः
सुराणां यद् अभीष्टं च त्वया कृतम् असंशयम्
पालिता देवदेवस्य आज्ञा त्रैलोक्यमण्डनी ॥
110.m: The gods said: / What was desired by the gods has undoubtedly been done by you; / the command of the god of gods, which adorns the three worlds, has been obeyed.

110.s:
yācitaṃ ca tvayā pūrvaṃ parārthaṃ nātmane dvija
tasmād anyatamaṃ brūhi kiṃcid dāsyāmahe vayam //
110.d:
याचितं च त्वया पूर्वं परार्थं नात्मने द्विज
तस्माद् अन्यतमं ब्रूहि किंचिद् दास्यामहे वयम् ॥
110.m: And what you asked for earlier, O twice-born, was for the sake of others, not for yourself. / Therefore, ask for something else, and we will grant it.

110.s:
brahmovāca
punaḥ punas tad evocuḥ surasaṃghā dvijottamam
kṛtāñjalipuṭaḥ pūrvaṃ natvā śaṃbhusurān idam
uvāca pippalādaś ca umāṃ natvā ca pippalān //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुनः पुनस् तद् एवोचुः सुरसंघा द्विजोत्तमम्
कृताञ्जलिपुटः पूर्वं नत्वा शंभुसुरान् इदम्
उवाच पिप्पलादश् च उमां नत्वा च पिप्पलान् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Again and again the hosts of gods said just that to the best of the twice-born. / With folded hands, having first bowed to Śaṃbhu and the gods, / Pippalāda, having bowed to Umā and to the pippala trees, said this:

110.s:
pippalāda uvāca
pitarau draṣṭukāmo 'smi sadā me śabdagocarau
te dhanyāḥ prāṇino loke mātāpitror vaśe sthitāḥ //
110.d:
पिप्पलाद उवाच
पितरौ द्रष्टुकामो ऽस्मि सदा मे शब्दगोचरौ
ते धन्याः प्राणिनो लोके मातापित्रोर् वशे स्थिताः ॥
110.m: Pippalāda said: / I desire to see my parents, who are always within the realm of words for me. / Blessed are those living beings in the world who abide under the control of their mother and father,

110.s:
śuśrūṣaṇaparā nityaṃ tatpādājñāpratīkṣakāḥ
indriyāṇi śarīraṃ ca kulaṃ śaktiṃ dhiyaṃ vapuḥ //
110.d:
शुश्रूषणपरा नित्यं तत्पादाज्ञाप्रतीक्षकाः
इन्द्रियाणि शरीरं च कुलं शक्तिं धियं वपुः ॥
110.m: constantly devoted to serving them, awaiting the command of their feet! / Having obtained sense-faculties, a body, family, strength, intellect, and physical form,

110.s:
parilabhya tayoḥ kṛtye kṛtakṛtyo bhavet svayam
paśūnāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ cāpi sulabhaṃ mātṛdarśanam //
110.d:
परिलभ्य तयोः कृत्ये कृतकृत्यो भवेत् स्वयम्
पशूनां पक्षिणां चापि सुलभं मातृदर्शनम् ॥
110.m: one would become truly fulfilled by acting on their behalf. / The sight of a mother is easily available even to beasts and birds;

110.s:
durlabhaṃ mama tac cāpi pṛcche pāpaphalaṃ nu kim
durlabhaṃ ca tathā cet syāt sarveṣāṃ yasya kasyacit //
110.d:
दुर्लभं मम तच् चापि पृच्छे पापफलं नु किम्
दुर्लभं च तथा चेत् स्यात् सर्वेषां यस्य कस्यचित् ॥
110.m: yet it is difficult for me to obtain. I ask: is this the fruit of my sin? / If it were so difficult to obtain, for anyone whomsoever,

110.s:
nopapadyeta sulabhaṃ matto nānyo 'sti pāpakṛt
tayor darśanamātraṃ ca yadi prāpsye surottamāḥ //
110.d:
नोपपद्येत सुलभं मत्तो नान्यो ऽस्ति पापकृत्
तयोर् दर्शनमात्रं च यदि प्राप्स्ये सुरोत्तमाः ॥
110.m: it would not be so easily available; there is no wrongdoer other than me! / O best of gods, if only I might attain the sight of them both,

110.s:
manovākkāyakarmabhyaḥ phalaṃ prāptaṃ bhaviṣyati
pitarau ye na paśyanti samutpannā na saṃsṛtau
teṣāṃ mahāpātakānāṃ kaḥ saṃkhyāṃ kartum īśvaraḥ //
110.d:
मनोवाक्कायकर्मभ्यः फलं प्राप्तं भविष्यति
पितरौ ये न पश्यन्ति समुत्पन्ना न संसृतौ
तेषां महापातकानां कः संख्यां कर्तुम् ईश्वरः ॥
110.m: the fruit of actions of mind, speech, and body will have been achieved. / Who is capable of counting the great sins / of those who, having been born into worldly existence, do not see their parents?

110.s:
brahmovāca
tad ṛṣer vacanaṃ śrutvā mithaḥ saṃmantrya te surāḥ
vimānavaram ārūḍhau pitarau daṃpatī śubhau //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् ऋषेर् वचनं श्रुत्वा मिथः संमन्त्र्य ते सुराः
विमानवरम् आरूढौ पितरौ दंपती शुभौ ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard those words of the sage, those gods consulted among themselves, [and said:] / “Mounted upon an excellent celestial chariot, your parents, an auspicious couple,

110.s:
tava saṃdarśanākāṅkṣau drakṣyase vādya niścitam
viṣādaṃ lobhamohau ca tyaktvā cittaṃ śamaṃ naya //
110.d:
तव संदर्शनाकाङ्क्षौ द्रक्ष्यसे वाद्य निश्चितम्
विषादं लोभमोहौ च त्यक्त्वा चित्तं शमं नय ॥
110.m: longing to see you, you will certainly see today. / Abandoning dejection, greed, and delusion, lead your mind to peace.

110.s:
paśya paśyeti taṃ prāhur dādhīcaṃ surasattamāḥ
vimānavaram ārūḍhau svargiṇau svarṇabhūṣaṇau //
110.d:
पश्य पश्येति तं प्राहुर् दाधीचं सुरसत्तमाः
विमानवरम् आरूढौ स्वर्गिणौ स्वर्णभूषणौ ॥
110.m: Behold! Behold!” the best of gods said to that son of Dadhīci. / Mounted upon an excellent celestial chariot, dwellers of heaven adorned with gold,

110.s:
tava saṃdarśanākāṅkṣau pitarau daṃpatī śubhau
vījyamānau surastrībhiḥ stūyamānau ca kiṃnaraiḥ //
110.d:
तव संदर्शनाकाङ्क्षौ पितरौ दंपती शुभौ
वीज्यमानौ सुरस्त्रीभिः स्तूयमानौ च किंनरैः ॥
110.m: longing to see you, an auspicious couple, your parents, / being fanned by celestial women and praised by kiṃnaras!

110.s:
dṛṣṭvā sa mātāpitarau nanāma śivasaṃnidhau
harṣabāṣpāśrunayanau sa kathaṃcid uvāca tau //
110.d:
दृष्ट्वा स मातापितरौ ननाम शिवसंनिधौ
हर्षबाष्पाश्रुनयनौ स कथंचिद् उवाच तौ ॥
110.m: Seeing his mother and father, he bowed down in the presence of Śiva; / with tears of joy in his eyes, he somehow spoke to them both.

110.s:
putra uvāca
tārayanty eva pitarāv anye putrāḥ kulodvahāḥ
ahaṃ tu mātur udare kevalaṃ bhedakāraṇam
evaṃbhūto 'pi tau mohāt paśyeyam atidurmatiḥ //
110.d:
पुत्र उवाच
तारयन्त्य् एव पितराव् अन्ये पुत्राः कुलोद्वहाः
अहं तु मातुर् उदरे केवलं भेदकारणम्
एवंभूतो ऽपि तौ मोहात् पश्येयम् अतिदुर्मतिः ॥
110.m: The son said: / Other sons who carry forward the lineage deliver their parents; / but I was merely the cause of tearing apart my mother’s womb. / Even being such a one, through delusion might I, utterly wicked, behold them both?

110.s:
brahmovāca
tāv ālokya tato duḥkhād vaktuṃ naiva śaśāka saḥ
devāś ca mātāpitarau pippalādam athābruvan //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ताव् आलोक्य ततो दुःखाद् वक्तुं नैव शशाक सः
देवाश् च मातापितरौ पिप्पलादम् अथाब्रुवन् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Beholding them both, he was then unable to speak out of grief. / And the gods and his mother and father then said to Pippalāda:

110.s:
dhanyas tvaṃ putra lokeṣu yasya kīrtir gatā divam
sākṣātkṛtas tvayā tryakṣo devāś cāśvāsitās tvayā
tvayā putreṇa sallokā na kṣīyante kadācana //
110.d:
धन्यस् त्वं पुत्र लोकेषु यस्य कीर्तिर् गता दिवम्
साक्षात्कृतस् त्वया त्र्यक्षो देवाश् चाश्वासितास् त्वया
त्वया पुत्रेण सल्लोका न क्षीयन्ते कदाचन ॥
110.m: “Blessed are you, O son, in the worlds, whose fame has reached heaven! / The three-eyed one has been seen directly by you, and the gods have been comforted by you; / by you as a son, the good worlds never perish.”

110.s:
brahmovāca
puṣpavṛṣṭis tadā svargāt papāta tasya mūrdhani
jayaśabdaḥ surair uktaḥ prādurbhūto mahāmune //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुष्पवृष्टिस् तदा स्वर्गात् पपात तस्य मूर्धनि
जयशब्दः सुरैर् उक्तः प्रादुर्भूतो महामुने ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / A shower of flowers then fell from heaven upon his head; / a cry of victory uttered by the gods arose, O great sage.

110.s:
āśiṣaṃ tu sute dattvā dadhīciḥ saha bhāryayā
śaṃbhuṃ gaṅgāṃ surān natvā putraṃ vākyam athābravīt //
110.d:
आशिषं तु सुते दत्त्वा दधीचिः सह भार्यया
शंभुं गङ्गां सुरान् नत्वा पुत्रं वाक्यम् अथाब्रवीत् ॥
110.m: Having bestowed a blessing upon his son, Dadhīci together with his wife, / having bowed to Śaṃbhu, the Gaṅgā, and the gods, then spoke these words to his son:

110.s:
dadhīcir uvāca
prāpya bhāryāṃ śive bhaktiṃ kuru gaṅgāṃ ca sevaya
putrān utpādya vidhivad yajñān iṣṭvā sadakṣiṇān
kṛtakṛtyas tato vatsa ākramasva ciraṃ divam //
110.d:
दधीचिर् उवाच
प्राप्य भार्यां शिवे भक्तिं कुरु गङ्गां च सेवय
पुत्रान् उत्पाद्य विधिवद् यज्ञान् इष्ट्वा सदक्षिणान्
कृतकृत्यस् ततो वत्स आक्रमस्व चिरं दिवम् ॥
110.m: Dadhīci said: / Having obtained a wife, practice devotion to Śiva and serve the Gaṅgā. / Having fathered sons according to rule and performed sacrifices with priestly fees, / having achieved your purpose, my child, enter heaven for a long time.

110.s:
brahmovāca
karomy evam iti prāha dadhīciṃ pippalāśanaḥ
dadhīciḥ putram āśvāsya bhāryayā ca punaḥ punaḥ //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
करोम्य् एवम् इति प्राह दधीचिं पिप्पलाशनः
दधीचिः पुत्रम् आश्वास्य भार्यया च पुनः पुनः ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Pippalāda said to Dadhīci, “I will do so.” / Having comforted his son along with his wife again and again,

110.s:
anujñātaḥ suragaṇaiḥ punaḥ sa divam ākramat
devā apy ūcire sarve pippalādaṃ sasaṃbhramāḥ //
110.d:
अनुज्ञातः सुरगणैः पुनः स दिवम् आक्रमत्
देवा अप्य् ऊचिरे सर्वे पिप्पलादं ससंभ्रमाः ॥
110.m: permitted by the hosts of gods, he entered heaven once more. / All the gods, too, agitated with urgency, said to Pippalāda:

110.s:
devā ūcuḥ
kṛtyāṃ śamaya bhadraṃ te tad utpannaṃ mahānalam //
110.d:
देवा ऊचुः
कृत्यां शमय भद्रं ते तद् उत्पन्नं महानलम् ॥
110.m: The gods said: / Quench the destructive spirit, may good betide you, and the great fire that arose from her!

110.s:
brahmovāca
pippalādas tu tān āha na śakto 'haṃ nivāraṇe
asatyaṃ naiva vaktāhaṃ yūyaṃ kṛtyāṃ tu brūta tām //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पिप्पलादस् तु तान् आह न शक्तो ऽहं निवारणे
असत्यं नैव वक्ताहं यूयं कृत्यां तु ब्रूत ताम् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Pippalāda, however, said to them, “I am not able to ward them off. / I will never speak an untruth; speak yourselves to that destructive spirit.

110.s:
māṃ dṛṣṭvā sā mahāraudrā viparītaṃ kariṣyati
tām eva gatvā vibudhāḥ procus te śāntikāraṇam //
110.d:
मां दृष्ट्वा सा महारौद्रा विपरीतं करिष्यति
ताम् एव गत्वा विबुधाः प्रोचुस् ते शान्तिकारणम् ॥
110.m: Seeing me, she, intensely fierce, will do the opposite.” / Going to her, the gods spoke for the sake of pacification.

110.s:
analaṃ ca yathāprīti te ubhe nety avocatām
sarveṣāṃ bhakṣaṇāyaiva sṛṣṭā cāhaṃ dvijanmanā //
110.d:
अनलं च यथाप्रीति ते उभे नेत्य् अवोचताम्
सर्वेषां भक्षणायैव सृष्टा चाहं द्विजन्मना ॥
110.m: And to the fire, as kindly as possible, but both of them said, “No. / I was created by the twice-born specifically to devour everyone,

110.s:
tathā ca matprasūto 'gnir anyathā tat kathaṃ bhavet
mahābhūtāni pañcāpi sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ tathā //
110.d:
तथा च मत्प्रसूतो ऽग्निर् अन्यथा तत् कथं भवेत्
महाभूतानि पञ्चापि स्थावरं जङ्गमं तथा ॥
110.m: and the fire was born from me; how could it be otherwise? / Even the five gross elements, both the stationary and the moving,

110.s:
sarvam asmanmukhe vidyād vaktavyaṃ nāvaśiṣyate
mayā saṃmantrya te devāḥ punar ūcur ubhāv api //
110.d:
सर्वम् अस्मन्मुखे विद्याद् वक्तव्यं नावशिष्यते
मया संमन्त्र्य ते देवाः पुनर् ऊचुर् उभाव् अपि ॥
110.m: one should know to be entirely in our mouth; nothing remains to be said.” / Having consulted with me, those gods spoke again to both of them:

110.s:
bhakṣayetām ubhau sarvaṃ yathānukramatas tathā
vaḍavāpi surān evam uvāca śṛṇu nārada //
110.d:
भक्षयेताम् उभौ सर्वं यथानुक्रमतस् तथा
वडवापि सुरान् एवम् उवाच शृणु नारद ॥
110.m: “Let both of you devour everything in proper order.” / Hear, O Nārada, what Vaḍavā too said to the gods.

110.s:
vaḍavovāca
bhavatām icchayā sarvaṃ bhakṣyaṃ me surasattamāḥ //
110.d:
वडवोवाच
भवताम् इच्छया सर्वं भक्ष्यं मे सुरसत्तमाः ॥
110.m: Vaḍavā said: / In accordance with your wish, everything shall be devoured by me, O best of gods.

110.s:
brahmovāca
vaḍavā sā nadī jātā gaṅgayā saṃgatā mune
tadbhavas tu mahān agnir ya āsīd atibhīṣaṇaḥ
tam āhur amarā vahniṃ bhūtānām ādito viduḥ //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
वडवा सा नदी जाता गङ्गया संगता मुने
तद्भवस् तु महान् अग्निर् य आसीद् अतिभीषणः
तम् आहुर् अमरा वह्निं भूतानाम् आदितो विदुः ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / That Vaḍavā became a river and joined with the Gaṅgā, O sage; / and the great fire that was born from her, which was extremely terrifying, / the immortals called the fire that exists from the beginning of all beings.

110.s:
surā ūcuḥ
āpo jyeṣṭhatamā jñeyās tathaiva prathamaṃ bhavān
tatrāpy apāṃpatiṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ samudram aśanaṃ kuru
yathaiva tu vayaṃ brūmo gaccha bhuṅkṣva yathāsukham //
110.d:
सुरा ऊचुः
आपो ज्येष्ठतमा ज्ञेयास् तथैव प्रथमं भवान्
तत्राप्य् अपांपतिं ज्येष्ठं समुद्रम् अशनं कुरु
यथैव तु वयं ब्रूमो गच्छ भुङ्क्ष्व यथासुखम् ॥
110.m: The gods said: / Waters should be known as the eldest of all, and likewise you are the first. / Even there, make the ocean, the eldest lord of the waters, your food. / Just as we say, go and consume it at your pleasure.

110.s:
brahmovāca
analas tv amarān āha āpas tatra kathaṃ tv aham
vrajeyaṃ yadi māṃ tatra prāpayanty udakaṃ mahat //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अनलस् त्व् अमरान् आह आपस् तत्र कथं त्व् अहम्
व्रजेयं यदि मां तत्र प्रापयन्त्य् उदकं महत् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / The fire said to the immortals, “The waters are there; but how / could I go unless you take me there to the great water?”

110.s:
bhavanta eva te 'py āhuḥ kathaṃ te 'gne gatir bhavet
agnir apy āha tān devān kanyā māṃ guṇaśālinī //
110.d:
भवन्त एव ते ऽप्य् आहुः कथं ते ऽग्ने गतिर् भवेत्
अग्निर् अप्य् आह तान् देवान् कन्या मां गुणशालिनी ॥
110.m: They too said, “How could your going take place, O fire?” / The fire also said to those gods, “An accomplished maiden,

110.s:
hiraṇyakalaśe sthāpya nayed yatra gatir mama
tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kanyām ūcuḥ sarasvatīm //
110.d:
हिरण्यकलशे स्थाप्य नयेद् यत्र गतिर् मम
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा कन्याम् ऊचुः सरस्वतीम् ॥
110.m: having placed me in a golden pot, should take me to where my destination is.” / Having heard his words, they spoke to the maiden Sarasvatī.

110.s:
devā ūcuḥ
nayainam analaṃ śīghraṃ śirasā varuṇālayam //
110.d:
देवा ऊचुः
नयैनम् अनलं शीघ्रं शिरसा वरुणालयम् ॥
110.m: The gods said: / Take this fire quickly upon your head to the abode of Varuṇa!

110.s:
brahmovāca
sarasvatī surān āha naikā śaktā ca dhāraṇe
yuktā catasṛbhiḥ śīghraṃ vaheyaṃ varuṇālayam //
110.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सरस्वती सुरान् आह नैका शक्ता च धारणे
युक्ता चतसृभिः शीघ्रं वहेयं वरुणालयम् ॥
110.m: Brahmā said: / Sarasvatī said to the gods, “Alone I am not able to hold him; / accompanied by four [others], I would quickly carry him to the abode of Varuṇa.”

110.s:
sarasvatyā vacaḥ śrutvā gaṅgāṃ ca yamunāṃ tathā
narmadāṃ tapatīṃ caiva surāḥ procuḥ pṛthak pṛthak //
110.d:
सरस्वत्या वचः श्रुत्वा गङ्गां च यमुनां तथा
नर्मदां तपतीं चैव सुराः प्रोचुः पृथक् पृथक् ॥
110.m: Having heard the words of Sarasvatī, the gods spoke individually / to Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Narmadā, and Tapatī.

110.s:
tābhiḥ samanvitovāha hiraṇyakalaśe 'nalam
saṃsthāpya śirasādhārya tā jagmur varuṇālayam //
110.d:
ताभिः समन्वितोवाह हिरण्यकलशे ऽनलम्
संस्थाप्य शिरसाधार्य ता जग्मुर् वरुणालयम् ॥
110.m: Accompanied by them, having placed the fire in a golden pot / and bearing it upon their heads, they carried it and went to the abode of Varuṇa,

110.s:
saṃsthāpya yatra deveśaḥ somanātho jagatpatiḥ
adhyāste vibudhaiḥ sārdhaṃ prabhāse śaśibhūṣaṇaḥ //
110.d:
संस्थाप्य यत्र देवेशः सोमनाथो जगत्पतिः
अध्यास्ते विबुधैः सार्धं प्रभासे शशिभूषणः ॥
110.m: depositing it where the lord of the gods, Somanātha, the lord of the world, / adorned with the crescent moon, resides together with the gods at Prabhāsa.

110.s:
prāpayām āsur analaṃ pañcanadyaḥ sarasvatī
adhyāste ca mahān agniḥ piban vāri śanaiḥ śanaiḥ //
110.d:
प्रापयाम् आसुर् अनलं पञ्चनद्यः सरस्वती
अध्यास्ते च महान् अग्निः पिबन् वारि शनैः शनैः ॥
110.m: The five rivers, led by Sarasvatī, brought the fire there; / and the great fire resides there, drinking the water little by little.

110.s: tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve śivam ūcuḥ surottamam //
110.d: ततः सुरगणाः सर्वे शिवम् ऊचुः सुरोत्तमम् ॥
110.m: Then all the hosts of gods spoke to Śiva, the best of the gods.

110.s:
devā ūcuḥ
