कृत्यां च वडवां तत्र देवाश् च ऋषयो ऽमलाः ॥
116.m: Brahmā said: / From then on, the rākṣasas became the enemies of the gods. / And there the gods and the stainless sages [placed] the Kṛtyā as a mare (Vaḍavā).

116.s:
mṛtyor bhāryā bhava tvaṃ tām ity uktvā te 'bhyaṣecayan
abhiṣekodakaṃ yat tu sā nadī vaḍavābhavat //
116.d:
मृत्योर् भार्या भव त्वं ताम् इत्य् उक्त्वा ते ऽभ्यषेचयन्
अभिषेकोदकं यत् तु सा नदी वडवाभवत् ॥
116.m: "Become the wife of Death," saying this to her, they consecrated her. / The water of consecration indeed became the river Vaḍavā.

116.s:
mṛtyunā sthāpitaṃ liṅgaṃ mahānalam iti śrutam
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ vaḍavāsaṃgamaṃ viduḥ //
116.d:
मृत्युना स्थापितं लिङ्गं महानलम् इति श्रुतम्
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं वडवासंगमं विदुः ॥
116.m: The liṅga installed by Death is renowned as Mahānala. / From that time onward, the wise know that tīrtha as Vaḍavāsaṃgama.

116.s:
mahānalo yatra devas tat tīrthaṃ bhuktimuktidam
sahasraṃ tatra tīrthānāṃ sarvābhīṣṭapradāyinām
ubhayos tīrayos tatra smaraṇād aghaghātinām //
116.d:
महानलो यत्र देवस् तत् तीर्थं भुक्तिमुक्तिदम्
सहस्रं तत्र तीर्थानां सर्वाभीष्टप्रदायिनाम्
उभयोस् तीरयोस् तत्र स्मरणाद् अघघातिनाम् ॥
116.m: Where God Mahānala is present, that tīrtha bestows enjoyment and liberation. / There are a thousand tīrthas there that grant all desires / on both its banks, destroying sins upon mere remembrance.

117.s:
brahmovāca
ātmatīrtham iti khyātaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ nṛṇām
tasya prabhāvaṃ vakṣyāmi yatra jñāneśvaraḥ śivaḥ //
117.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
आत्मतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं नृणाम्
तस्य प्रभावं वक्ष्यामि यत्र ज्ञानेश्वरः शिवः ॥
117.m: Brahmā said: / Known as Ātmatīrtha, it bestows enjoyment and liberation upon men. / I shall tell of its power, where Śiva is the Lord of Wisdom.

117.s:
datta ity api vikhyātaḥ so 'triputro harapriyaḥ
durvāsasaḥ priyo bhrātā sarvajñānaviśāradaḥ
sa gatvā pitaraṃ prāha vinayena praṇamya ca //
117.d:
दत्त इत्य् अपि विख्यातः सो ऽत्रिपुत्रो हरप्रियः
दुर्वाससः प्रियो भ्राता सर्वज्ञानविशारदः
स गत्वा पितरं प्राह विनयेन प्रणम्य च ॥
117.m: Famous by the name Datta, that son of Atri, dear to Hara, / beloved brother of Durvāsas, skilled in all knowledge, / went to his father and, bowing with humility, spoke:

117.s:
datta uvāca
brahmajñānaṃ kathaṃ me syāt kaṃ pṛcchāmi kva yāmi ca //
117.d:
दत्त उवाच
ब्रह्मज्ञानं कथं मे स्यात् कं पृच्छामि क्व यामि च ॥
117.m: Datta said: / How may I attain knowledge of Brahman? Whom should I ask, and where should I go?

117.s:
brahmovāca
tac chrutvātriḥ putravākyaṃ dhyātvā vacanam abravīt //
117.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तच् छ्रुत्वात्रिः पुत्रवाक्यं ध्यात्वा वचनम् अब्रवीत् ॥
117.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of his son, Atri meditated and spoke these words:

117.s:
atrir uvāca
gautamīṃ putra gaccha tvaṃ tatra stuhi maheśvaram
sa tu prīto yadaiva syāt tadā jñānam avāpsyasi //
117.d:
अत्रिर् उवाच
गौतमीं पुत्र गच्छ त्वं तत्र स्तुहि महेश्वरम्
स तु प्रीतो यदैव स्यात् तदा ज्ञानम् अवाप्स्यसि ॥
117.m: Atri said: / Go to the Gautamī, my son, and praise Maheśvara there. / Only when he is pleased will you attain knowledge.

117.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā tadātreyo gaṅgāṃ gatvā śucir yataḥ
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā bhaktyā tuṣṭāva śaṃkaram //
117.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा तदात्रेयो गङ्गां गत्वा शुचिर् यतः
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा भक्त्या तुष्टाव शंकरम् ॥
117.m: Brahmā said: / Saying "So be it," the son of Atri then went to the Gaṅgā, pure and restrained; / folding his hands in reverence, he praised Śaṅkara with devotion:

117.s:
datta uvāca
saṃsārakūpe patito 'smi daivān
mohena gupto bhavaduḥkhapaṅke
ajñānanāmnā tamasāvṛto 'haṃ
paraṃ na vindāmi surādhinātha
117.d:
दत्त उवाच
संसारकूपे पतितो ऽस्मि दैवान्
मोहेन गुप्तो भवदुःखपङ्के
अज्ञाननाम्ना तमसावृतो ऽहं
परं न विन्दामि सुराधिनाथ
117.m: Datta said: / I have fallen by fate into the well of saṃsāra, / enveloped by delusion in the mire of worldly suffering. / Shrouded in the darkness named ignorance, / I do not find the Supreme, O lord of the gods!

117.s:
bhinnas triśūlena balīyasāhaṃ
pāpena cintākṣurapāṭitaś ca
tapto 'smi pañcendriyatīvratāpaiḥ
śrānto 'smi saṃtāraya somanātha
117.d:
भिन्नस् त्रिशूलेन बलीयसाहं
पापेन चिन्ताक्षुरपाटितश् च
तप्तो ऽस्मि पञ्चेन्द्रियतीव्रतापैः
श्रान्तो ऽस्मि संतारय सोमनाथ
117.m: I am pierced by the mighty trident of sin, / and cleft by the razor of anxious thought; / I am burned by the fierce torments of the five senses; / I am exhausted—ferry me across, O lord of Soma!

117.s:
baddho 'smi dāridryamayaiś ca bandhair
hato 'smi rogānalatīvratāpaiḥ
krānto 'smy ahaṃ mṛtyubhujaṃgamena
bhīto bhṛśaṃ kiṃ karavāṇi śaṃbho
117.d:
बद्धो ऽस्मि दारिद्र्यमयैश् च बन्धैर्
हतो ऽस्मि रोगानलतीव्रतापैः
क्रान्तो ऽस्म्य् अहं मृत्युभुजंगमेन
भीतो भृशं किं करवाणि शंभो
117.m: I am bound by fetters made of poverty; / I am struck by the fierce heats of the fire of disease; / I am overcome by the serpent of death; / I am utterly terrified—what shall I do, O Śambhu?

117.s:
bhavābhavābhyām atipīḍito 'haṃ
tṛṣṇākṣudhābhyāṃ ca rajastamobhyām
īdṛkṣayā jarayā cābhibhūtaḥ
paśyāvasthāṃ kṛpayā me 'dya nātha
117.d:
भवाभवाभ्याम् अतिपीडितो ऽहं
तृष्णाक्षुधाभ्यां च रजस्तमोभ्याम्
ईदृक्षया जरया चाभिभूतः
पश्यावस्थां कृपया मे ऽद्य नाथ
117.m: I am sorely tormented by existence and non-existence, / by thirst and hunger, and by passion and darkness; / overpowered by old age of such kind, / behold my condition with mercy today, O Lord!

117.s:
kāmena kopena ca matsareṇa
dambhena darpādibhir apy anekaiḥ
ekaikaśaḥ kaṣṭagato 'smi viddhas
tvaṃ nāthavad vāraya nātha śatrūn
117.d:
कामेन कोपेन च मत्सरेण
दम्भेन दर्पादिभिर् अप्य् अनेकैः
एकैकशः कष्टगतो ऽस्मि विद्धस्
त्वं नाथवद् वारय नाथ शत्रून्
117.m: By desire, by anger, by malice, / by deceit, and by many faults like arrogance, / pierced one by one, I have fallen into distress; / like a true protector, O Lord, drive away these enemies!

117.s:
kasyāpi kaścit patitasya puṃso
duḥkhapraṇodī bhavatīti satyam
vinā bhavantaṃ mama somanātha
kutrāpi kāruṇyavaco 'pi nāsti
117.d:
कस्यापि कश्चित् पतितस्य पुंसो
दुःखप्रणोदी भवतीति सत्यम्
विना भवन्तं मम सोमनाथ
कुत्रापि कारुण्यवचो ऽपि नास्ति
117.m: It is true that for some fallen man, / someone exists to dispel his sorrow; / yet without you, O lord of Soma, / there is not even a word of compassion for me anywhere.

117.s:
tāvat sa kopo bhayamohaduḥkhāny
ajñānadāridryarujas tathaiva
kāmādayo mṛtyur apīha yāvan
namaḥ śivāyeti na vacmi vākyam
117.d:
तावत् स कोपो भयमोहदुःखान्य्
अज्ञानदारिद्र्यरुजस् तथैव
कामादयो मृत्युर् अपीह यावन्
नमः शिवायेति न वच्मि वाक्यम्
117.m: Anger, fear, delusion, and sorrow persist, / as do ignorance, poverty, and diseases, / desire and the rest, and death itself in this world, / only so long as I do not utter the words: "Homage to Śiva!"

117.s:
na me 'sti dharmo na ca me 'sti bhaktir
nāhaṃ vivekī karuṇā kuto me
dātāsi tenāśu śaraṇya citte
nidhehi someti padaṃ madīye
117.d:
न मे ऽस्ति धर्मो न च मे ऽस्ति भक्तिर्
नाहं विवेकी करुणा कुतो मे
दातासि तेनाशु शरण्य चित्ते
निधेहि सोमेति पदं मदीये
117.m: I have no dharma and no devotion; / I have no discernment—whence would compassion come to me? / You are the giver; therefore, O refuge, swiftly / place the word "Soma" in my heart!

117.s:
yāce na cāhaṃ surabhūpatitvaṃ
hṛtpadmamadhye mama somanātha
śrīsomapādāmbujasaṃnidhānaṃ
yāce vicāryaiva ca tat kuruṣva
117.d:
याचे न चाहं सुरभूपतित्वं
हृत्पद्ममध्ये मम सोमनाथ
श्रीसोमपादाम्बुजसंनिधानं
याचे विचार्यैव च तत् कुरुष्व
117.m: I do not ask for dominion over the gods or the earth; / in the center of the lotus of my heart, O lord of Soma, / I ask for the presence of the lotus feet of auspicious Soma; / consider this and grant it!

117.s:
yathā tavāhaṃ vidito 'smi pāpas
tathāpi vijñāpanam āśṛṇuṣva
saṃśrūyate yatra vacaḥ śiveti
tatra sthitiḥ syān mama somanātha
117.d:
यथा तवाहं विदितो ऽस्मि पापस्
तथापि विज्ञापनम् आशृणुष्व
संश्रूयते यत्र वचः शिवेति
तत्र स्थितिः स्यान् मम सोमनाथ
117.m: Though I am known to you as a sinner, / listen nonetheless to my supplication: / Wherever the word "Śiva" is heard, / may my dwelling be there, O lord of Soma!

117.s:
gaurīpate śaṃkara somanātha
viśveśa kāruṇyanidhe 'khilātman
saṃstūyate yatra sadeti tatra
keṣām api syāt kṛtināṃ nivāsaḥ
117.d:
गौरीपते शंकर सोमनाथ
विश्वेश कारुण्यनिधे ऽखिलात्मन्
संस्तूयते यत्र सदेति तत्र
केषाम् अपि स्यात् कृतिनां निवासः
117.m: O lord of Gaurī, O Śaṅkara, O lord of Soma, / O Lord of the Universe, ocean of compassion, Self of all! / Where you are ever praised, / there may the dwelling of some fortunate souls be.

117.s:
brahmovāca
ity ātreyastutiṃ śrutvā tutoṣa bhagavān haraḥ
varado 'smīti taṃ prāha yoginaṃ viśvakṛd bhavaḥ //
117.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् आत्रेयस्तुतिं श्रुत्वा तुतोष भगवान् हरः
वरदो ऽस्मीति तं प्राह योगिनं विश्वकृद् भवः ॥
117.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing this hymn of praise by the son of Atri, the blessed Hara was pleased. / "I grant a boon," said Bhava, maker of the universe, to that yogin.

117.s:
ātreya uvāca
ātmajñānaṃ ca muktiṃ ca bhuktiṃ ca vipulāṃ tvayi
tīrthasyāpi ca māhātmyaṃ varo 'yaṃ tridaśārcita //
117.d:
आत्रेय उवाच
आत्मज्ञानं च मुक्तिं च भुक्तिं च विपुलां त्वयि
तीर्थस्यापि च माहात्म्यं वरो ऽयं त्रिदशार्चित ॥
117.m: The son of Atri said: / Knowledge of the Self, liberation, and abundant enjoyment in you, / as well as the greatness of this tīrtha—this is the boon [I ask], O worshiped of the thirty [gods]!

117.s:
brahmovāca
evam astv iti taṃ śaṃbhur uktvā cāntaradhīyata
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrtham ātmatīrthaṃ vidur budhāḥ
tatra snānena dānena muktiḥ syād iha nārada //
117.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् अस्त्व् इति तं शंभुर् उक्त्वा चान्तरधीयत
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थम् आत्मतीर्थं विदुर् बुधाः
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन मुक्तिः स्याद् इह नारद ॥
117.m: Brahmā said: / Saying "May it be so" to him, Śambhu vanished. / From that time onward, the wise know that tīrtha as Ātmatīrtha. / By bathing and giving gifts there, liberation is attained in this world, O Nārada.

118.s:
brahmovāca
aśvatthatīrtham ākhyātaṃ pippalaṃ ca tataḥ param
uttare mandatīrthaṃ tu tatra vyuṣṭim itaḥ śṛṇu //
118.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अश्वत्थतीर्थम् आख्यातं पिप्पलं च ततः परम्
उत्तरे मन्दतीर्थं तु तत्र व्युष्टिम् इतः शृणु ॥
118.m: Brahmā said: / Aśvatthatīrtha is declared, and Pippala after that; / to the north is Mandatīrtha—hear now the reward there.

118.s:
purā tv agastyo bhagavān dakṣiṇāśāpatiḥ prabhuḥ
devais tu preritaḥ pūrvaṃ vindhyasya prārthanaṃ prati //
118.d:
पुरा त्व् अगस्त्यो भगवान् दक्षिणाशापतिः प्रभुः
देवैस् तु प्रेरितः पूर्वं विन्ध्यस्य प्रार्थनं प्रति ॥
118.m: Formerly, the blessed and powerful Agastya, lord of the southern quarter, / was dispatched earlier by the gods / to make a request of the Vindhya mountain.

118.s:
sa śanair vindhyam abhyāgāt sahasramunibhir vṛtaḥ
tam āgatya nagaśreṣṭhaṃ bahuvṛkṣasamākulam //
118.d:
स शनैर् विन्ध्यम् अभ्यागात् सहस्रमुनिभिर् वृतः
तम् आगत्य नगश्रेष्ठं बहुवृक्षसमाकुलम् ॥
118.m: Accompanied by a thousand sages, he slowly approached the Vindhya. / Reaching that best of mountains, filled with many trees,

118.s:
spardhinaṃ merubhānubhyāṃ vindhyaṃ śṛṅgaśatair vṛtam
atyunnataṃ nagaṃ dhīro lopāmudrāpatir muniḥ //
118.d:
स्पर्धिनं मेरुभानुभ्यां विन्ध्यं शृङ्गशतैर् वृतम्
अत्युन्नतं नगं धीरो लोपामुद्रापतिर् मुनिः ॥
118.m: rivaling Meru and the sun, covered with hundreds of peaks, / an exceedingly lofty mountain, that wise sage, the husband of Lopāmudrā,

118.s:
kṛtātithyo dvijaiḥ sārdhaṃ praśasya ca nagaṃ punaḥ
idam āha muniśreṣṭho devakāryārthasiddhaye //
118.d:
कृतातिथ्यो द्विजैः सार्धं प्रशस्य च नगं पुनः
इदम् आह मुनिश्रेष्ठो देवकार्यार्थसिद्धये ॥
118.m: having received hospitality alongside the twice-born and having praised the mountain again, / that best of sages spoke thus to accomplish the mission of the gods:

118.s:
agastya uvāca
ahaṃ yāmi nagaśreṣṭha munibhis tattvadarśibhiḥ
tīrthayātrāṃ karomīti dakṣiṇāśāṃ vrajāmy aham //
118.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
अहं यामि नगश्रेष्ठ मुनिभिस् तत्त्वदर्शिभिः
तीर्थयात्रां करोमीति दक्षिणाशां व्रजाम्य् अहम् ॥
118.m: Agastya said: / I am going, O best of mountains, with sages who see the truth; / I am undertaking a pilgrimage to sacred waters, and going to the southern quarter.

118.s:
dehi mārgaṃ nagapate ātithyaṃ dehi yācate
yāvad āgamanaṃ me syāt sthātavyaṃ tāvad eva hi //
118.d:
देहि मार्गं नगपते आतिथ्यं देहि याचते
यावद् आगमनं मे स्यात् स्थातव्यं तावद् एव हि ॥
118.m: Grant a passage, O lord of mountains; grant hospitality to one who asks! / You must remain just as you are until my return;

118.s:
nānyathā bhavitavyaṃ te tathety āha nagottamaḥ
ākrāman dakṣiṇām āśāṃ tair vṛto munibhir muniḥ //
118.d:
नान्यथा भवितव्यं ते तथेत्य् आह नगोत्तमः
आक्रामन् दक्षिणाम् आशां तैर् वृतो मुनिभिर् मुनिः ॥
118.m: it must not be otherwise for you! The best of mountains said, "So be it." / Traversing the southern quarter, surrounded by those sages, the sage

118.s:
śanaiḥ sa gautamīm āgāt sattrayāgāya dīkṣitaḥ
yāvat saṃvatsaraṃ sattram akarod ṛṣibhir vṛtaḥ //
118.d:
शनैः स गौतमीम् आगात् सत्त्रयागाय दीक्षितः
यावत् संवत्सरं सत्त्रम् अकरोद् ऋषिभिर् वृतः ॥
118.m: gradually reached the Gautamī, consecrated for a sacrificial session. / Surrounded by the sages, he performed a sacrificial session for a full year.

118.s:
kaiṭabhasya sutau pāpau rākṣasau dharmakaṇṭakau
aśvatthaḥ pippalaś ceti vikhyātau tridaśālaye //
118.d:
कैटभस्य सुतौ पापौ राक्षसौ धर्मकण्टकौ
अश्वत्थः पिप्पलश् चेति विख्यातौ त्रिदशालये ॥
118.m: There were two wicked rākṣasas, the sons of Kaiṭabha, thorns to dharma, / renowned in the abode of the thirty [gods] as Aśvattha and Pippala.

118.s:
aśvattho 'śvattharūpeṇa pippalo brahmarūpadhṛk
tāv ubhāv antaraṃ prepsū yajñavidhvaṃsanāya tu //
118.d:
अश्वत्थो ऽश्वत्थरूपेण पिप्पलो ब्रह्मरूपधृक्
ताव् उभाव् अन्तरं प्रेप्सू यज्ञविध्वंसनाय तु ॥
118.m: Aśvattha assumed the form of an aśvattha tree, and Pippala took the form of a brāhmaṇa. / Both seeking an opportunity to ruin the sacrifice,

118.s:
kurutāṃ kāṅkṣitaṃ rūpaṃ dānavau pāpacetasau
aśvattho vṛkṣarūpeṇa pippalo brāhmaṇākṛtiḥ //
118.d:
कुरुतां काङ्क्षितं रूपं दानवौ पापचेतसौ
अश्वत्थो वृक्षरूपेण पिप्पलो ब्राह्मणाकृतिः ॥
118.m: those two evil-minded dānavas assumed the desired forms: / Aśvattha in the form of a tree, and Pippala in the guise of a brāhmaṇa.

118.s:
ubhau tau brāhmaṇān nityaṃ pīḍayetāṃ tapodhana
ālabhante ca ye 'śvatthaṃ tāṃs tān aśnāty asau taruḥ //
118.d:
उभौ तौ ब्राह्मणान् नित्यं पीडयेतां तपोधन
आलभन्ते च ये ऽश्वत्थं तांस् तान् अश्नात्य् असौ तरुः ॥
118.m: Both of them constantly harassed brāhmaṇas, O rich in asceticism! / Whoever touched the aśvattha, that tree devoured them.

118.s:
pippalaḥ sāmago bhūtvā śiṣyān aśnāti rākṣasaḥ
tasmād adyāpi vipreṣu sāmago 'tīva niṣkṛpaḥ //
118.d:
पिप्पलः सामगो भूत्वा शिष्यान् अश्नाति राक्षसः
तस्माद् अद्यापि विप्रेषु सामगो ऽतीव निष्कृपः ॥
118.m: Assuming the guise of a chanter of the Sāmaveda, the rākṣasa Pippala devoured his disciples. / Therefore, even today among the brahmins, a chanter of the Sāmaveda is utterly pitiless.

118.s:
kṣīyamāṇān dvijān dṛṣṭvā munayo rākṣasāv imau
iti buddhvā mahāprājñā dakṣiṇaṃ tīram āśritam //
118.d:
क्षीयमाणान् द्विजान् दृष्ट्वा मुनयो राक्षसाव् इमौ
इति बुद्ध्वा महाप्राज्ञा दक्षिणं तीरम् आश्रितम् ॥
118.m: Seeing the twice-born being diminished, the very wise sages, / realizing, "These two are rākṣasas," resorted to the southern bank.

118.s:
sauriṃ śanaiścaraṃ mandaṃ tapasyantaṃ dhṛtavratam
gatvā munigaṇāḥ sarve rakṣaḥkarma nyavedayan //
118.d:
सौरिं शनैश्चरं मन्दं तपस्यन्तं धृतव्रतम्
गत्वा मुनिगणाः सर्वे रक्षःकर्म न्यवेदयन् ॥
118.m: Approaching Sauri, Śanaiścara, Manda, who was practicing austerities and observing vows, / all the hosts of sages reported the deeds of the rākṣasas.

118.s:
saurir munigaṇān āha pūrṇe tapasi me dvijāḥ
rākṣasau hanmy apūrṇe tu tapasy akṣama eva hi //
118.d:
सौरिर् मुनिगणान् आह पूर्णे तपसि मे द्विजाः
राक्षसौ हन्म्य् अपूर्णे तु तपस्य् अक्षम एव हि ॥
118.m: Sauri said to the hosts of sages: "O twice-born, when my austerity is complete, / I shall slay the two rākṣasas; while my austerity is incomplete, I am incapable."

118.s:
punaḥ procur munigaṇā dāsyāmas te tapo mahat
ity ukto brāhmaṇaiḥ sauriḥ kṛtam ity āha tān api //
118.d:
पुनः प्रोचुर् मुनिगणा दास्यामस् ते तपो महत्
इत्य् उक्तो ब्राह्मणैः सौरिः कृतम् इत्य् आह तान् अपि ॥
118.m: Again the hosts of sages said: "We will give you great austerity." / Thus addressed by the brāhmaṇas, Sauri said to them, "It is done."

118.s:
saurir brāhmaṇaveṣeṇa prāyād aśvattharūpiṇam
rākṣasaṃ brāhmaṇo bhūtvā pradakṣiṇam athākarot //
118.d:
सौरिर् ब्राह्मणवेषेण प्रायाद् अश्वत्थरूपिणम्
राक्षसं ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा प्रदक्षिणम् अथाकरोत् ॥
118.m: Disguised as a brāhmaṇa, the son of Sūrya approached the demon who had taken the form of an aśvattha tree, and becoming a brāhmaṇa, he circumambulated him.

118.s:
pradakṣiṇaṃ tu kurvāṇaṃ mene brāhmaṇam eva tam
nityavad rākṣasaḥ pāpo bhakṣayām āsa māyayā //
118.d:
प्रदक्षिणं तु कुर्वाणं मेने ब्राह्मणम् एव तम्
नित्यवद् राक्षसः पापो भक्षयाम् आस मायया ॥
118.m: Believing him who was performing the circumambulation to be merely a brāhmaṇa, the evil demon swallowed him through illusory power, as he always did.

118.s:
tasya kāyaṃ samāviśya cakṣuṣāntrāṇy apaśyata
dṛṣṭaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ pāpo mandena ravisūnunā //
118.d:
तस्य कायं समाविश्य चक्षुषान्त्राण्य् अपश्यत
दृष्टः स राक्षसः पापो मन्देन रविसूनुना ॥
118.m: Having entered his body, he looked at his entrails with his eye; that evil demon was seen by the slow-moving son of the sun.

118.s:
bhasmībhūtaḥ kṣaṇenaiva girir vajrahato yathā
aśvatthaṃ bhasmasāt kṛtvā anyaṃ brāhmaṇarūpiṇam //
118.d:
भस्मीभूतः क्षणेनैव गिरिर् वज्रहतो यथा
अश्वत्थं भस्मसात् कृत्वा अन्यं ब्राह्मणरूपिणम् ॥
118.m: In an instant, [the demon] was reduced to ashes, like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt. Having reduced the aśvattha to ashes, [he went] to the other [demon] who had taken the form of a brāhmaṇa.

118.s:
rākṣasaṃ pāpanilayam eka eva tam abhyagāt
adhīyāno vipra iva śiṣyarūpo vinītavat //
118.d:
राक्षसं पापनिलयम् एक एव तम् अभ्यगात्
अधीयानो विप्र इव शिष्यरूपो विनीतवत् ॥
118.m: Alone he approached that demon, an abode of evil, like a student-brāhmaṇa studying, appearing humble in the form of a disciple.

118.s:
pippalaḥ pūrvavac cāpi bhakṣayām āsa bhānujam
sa bhakṣitaḥ pūrvavac ca kukṣāv antrāṇy avaikṣata //
118.d:
पिप्पलः पूर्ववच् चापि भक्षयाम् आस भानुजम्
स भक्षितः पूर्ववच् च कुक्षाव् अन्त्राण्य् अवैक्षत ॥
118.m: Pippala, just as before, swallowed the son of the sun. He, swallowed just as before, looked at the entrails in the belly.

118.s:
tenālokitamātro 'sau rākṣaso bhasmasād abhūt
ubhau hatvā bhānusutaḥ kiṃ kṛtyaṃ me vadantv atha //
118.d:
तेनालोकितमात्रो ऽसौ राक्षसो भस्मसाद् अभूत्
उभौ हत्वा भानुसुतः किं कृत्यं मे वदन्त्व् अथ ॥
118.m: As soon as he was looked at by him, that demon turned to ashes. Having slain them both, the son of the sun said: "Now tell me, what should be done by me?"

118.s:
munayo jātasaṃharṣāḥ sarva eva tapasvinaḥ
tataḥ prasannā hy abhavann ṛṣayo 'gastyapūrvakāḥ //
118.d:
मुनयो जातसंहर्षाः सर्व एव तपस्विनः
ततः प्रसन्ना ह्य् अभवन्न् ऋषयो ऽगस्त्यपूर्वकाः ॥
118.m: The sages, all the ascetics, were filled with delight. Then the ṛṣis, headed by Agastya, were indeed pleased.

118.s:
varān dadur yathākāmaṃ sauraye mandagāmine
sa prīto brāhmaṇān āha śaniḥ sūryasuto balī //
118.d:
वरान् ददुर् यथाकामं सौरये मन्दगामिने
स प्रीतो ब्राह्मणान् आह शनिः सूर्यसुतो बली ॥
118.m: They granted boons according to his desire to the son of Sūrya, the slow-moving one. Pleased, the mighty Śani, the son of Sūrya, said to the brāhmaṇas:

118.s:
saurir uvāca
maddvāre niyatā ye ca kurvanty aśvatthalambhanam
teṣāṃ sarvāṇi kāryāṇi syuḥ pīḍā madbhavā na ca //
118.d:
सौरिर् उवाच
मद्द्वारे नियता ये च कुर्वन्त्य् अश्वत्थलम्भनम्
तेषां सर्वाणि कार्याणि स्युः पीडा मद्भवा न च ॥
118.m:
The son of Sūrya said:
Those who, restrained, touch the aśvattha tree on my day—all their undertakings will succeed, and they will suffer no affliction born of me.

118.s:
tīrthe cāśvatthasaṃjñe vai snānaṃ kurvanti ye narāḥ
teṣāṃ sarvāṇi kāryāṇi bhaveyur aparo varaḥ //
118.d:
तीर्थे चाश्वत्थसंज्ञे वै स्नानं कुर्वन्ति ये नराः
तेषां सर्वाणि कार्याणि भवेयुर् अपरो वरः ॥
118.m: And the people who bathe at the tīrtha named Aśvattha—all their undertakings will succeed; this is another boon.

118.s:
mandavāre tu ye 'śvatthaṃ prātar utthāya mānavāḥ
ālabhante ca teṣāṃ vai grahapīḍā vyapohatu //
118.d:
मन्दवारे तु ये ऽश्वत्थं प्रातर् उत्थाय मानवाः
आलभन्ते च तेषां वै ग्रहपीडा व्यपोहतु ॥
118.m: The people who, having arisen in the morning on Saturday, touch the aśvattha tree—may the affliction caused by planets indeed be removed for them!

118.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrtham aśvatthaṃ pippalaṃ viduḥ
tīrthaṃ śanaiścaraṃ tatra tatrāgastyaṃ ca sāttrikam //
118.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थम् अश्वत्थं पिप्पलं विदुः
तीर्थं शनैश्चरं तत्र तत्रागस्त्यं च सात्त्रिकम् ॥
118.m:
Brahmā said:
From that time on, they know that tīrtha as Aśvattha and Pippala. There is the Śanaiścara tīrtha there, and there the Āgastya and the Sāttrika [tīrthas],

118.s:
yājñikaṃ cāpi tat tīrthaṃ sāmagaṃ tīrtham eva ca
ityādyaṣṭottarāṇy āsan sahasrāṇy atha ṣoḍaśa
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca sattrayāgaphalapradam //
118.d:
याज्ञिकं चापि तत् तीर्थं सामगं तीर्थम् एव च
इत्याद्यष्टोत्तराण्य् आसन् सहस्राण्य् अथ षोडश
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च सत्त्रयागफलप्रदम् ॥
118.m:
as well as that Yājñika tīrtha, and the Sāmaga tīrtha. Thus, beginning with these, there were sixteen thousand and eight [tīrthas];
bathing and giving gifts at them grants the fruit of a sacrificial session.

119.s:
brahmovāca
somatīrtham iti khyātaṃ tad apy uktaṃ mahātmabhiḥ
tatra snānena dānena somapānaphalaṃ labhet //
119.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सोमतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं तद् अप्य् उक्तं महात्मभिः
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन सोमपानफलं लभेत् ॥

119.s:
jagatāṃ mātaraḥ pūrvam oṣadhyo jīvasaṃmatāḥ
mamāpi mātaro devyaḥ pūrvāsāṃ pūrvavattarāḥ //
119.d:
जगतां मातरः पूर्वम् ओषध्यो जीवसंमताः
ममापि मातरो देव्यः पूर्वासां पूर्ववत्तराः ॥
119.m:
Formerly, the medicinal plants, regarded as the life of creatures, were the mothers of the worlds,
and the goddesses were mothers even to me, ancient ones older than the ancient.

119.s:
āsu pratiṣṭhito dharmaḥ svādhyāyo yajñakarma ca
ābhir eva dhṛtaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram //
119.d:
आसु प्रतिष्ठितो धर्मः स्वाध्यायो यज्ञकर्म च
आभिर् एव धृतं सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
119.m:
On them is established dharma, the recitation of sacred texts, and sacrificial rites;
by them alone is this entire threefold world, moving and unmoving, sustained.

119.s:
aśeṣarogopaśamo bhavaty ābhir asaṃśayam
annam etābhir eva syād aśeṣaprāṇarakṣaṇam
atrauṣadhyo jagadvandyā mām ūcur anahaṃkṛtāḥ //
119.d:
अशेषरोगोपशमो भवत्य् आभिर् असंशयम्
अन्नम् एताभिर् एव स्याद् अशेषप्राणरक्षणम्
अत्रौषध्यो जगद्वन्द्या माम् ऊचुर् अनहंकृताः ॥

119.s:
oṣadhya ūcuḥ
asmākaṃ tvaṃ patiṃ dehi rājānaṃ surasattama //
119.d:
ओषध्य ऊचुः
अस्माकं त्वं पतिं देहि राजानं सुरसत्तम ॥
119.m:
The medicinal plants said:
Grant us a lord, a king, O best of gods!

119.s:
brahmovāca
tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tāsāṃ mayoktā oṣadhīr idam
patiṃ prāpsyatha sarvāś ca rājānaṃ prītivardhanam //
119.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तच् छ्रुत्वा वचनं तासां मयोक्ता ओषधीर् इदम्
पतिं प्राप्स्यथ सर्वाश् च राजानं प्रीतिवर्धनम् ॥
119.m:
Brahmā said:
Having heard those words of theirs, I said this to the medicinal plants:
"You all shall obtain a lord, a king who increases delight."

119.s:
rājānam iti tac chrutvā tā mām ūcuḥ punar mune
gantavyaṃ kva punaś coktā gautamīṃ yāntu mātaraḥ //
119.d:
राजानम् इति तच् छ्रुत्वा ता माम् ऊचुः पुनर् मुने
गन्तव्यं क्व पुनश् चोक्ता गौतमीं यान्तु मातरः ॥
119.m:
Having heard that—[the word] "king"—they said to me again, O sage: "Where should we go?"
And they were told: "Let the mothers go to the Gautamī.

119.s:
tuṣṭāyām atha tasyāṃ vo rājā syāl lokapūjitaḥ
tāś ca gatvā muniśreṣṭha tuṣṭuvur gautamīṃ nadīm //
119.d:
तुष्टायाम् अथ तस्यां वो राजा स्याल् लोकपूजितः
ताश् च गत्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठ तुष्टुवुर् गौतमीं नदीम् ॥
119.m:
When she is pleased with you, there will be a king worshipped by the world."
And having gone, O best of sages, they praised the river Gautamī.

119.s:
oṣadhya ūcuḥ
kiṃ vākariṣyan bhavavartino janā
nānāghasaṃghābhibhavāc ca duḥkhitāḥ
na cāgamiṣyad bhavatī bhuvaṃ cet
puṇyodake gautami śaṃbhukānte
119.d:
ओषध्य ऊचुः
किं वाकरिष्यन् भववर्तिनो जना
नानाघसंघाभिभवाच् च दुःखिताः
न चागमिष्यद् भवती भुवं चेत्
पुण्योदके गौतमि शंभुकान्ते
119.m:
The medicinal plants said:
What would the people dwelling in worldly existence do,
afflicted by being overcome by hosts of various sins,
if you had not come to earth,
O Gautamī of holy waters, beloved of Śambhu?

119.s:
ko vetti bhāgyaṃ naradehabhājāṃ
mahīgatānāṃ saritām adhīśe
eṣāṃ mahāpātakasaṃghahantrī
tvam amba gaṅge sulabhā sadaiva
119.d:
को वेत्ति भाग्यं नरदेहभाजां
महीगतानां सरिताम् अधीशे
एषां महापातकसंघहन्त्री
त्वम् अम्ब गङ्गे सुलभा सदैव
119.m:
Who knows the fortune of those who possess human bodies,
who have come to earth, O sovereign of rivers?
You, O mother Gaṅgā, slayer of the host of great sins,
are always easily attainable to them.

119.s:
na te vibhūtiṃ nanu vetti ko 'pi
trailokyavandye jagadamba gaṅge
gaurīsamāliṅgitavigraho 'pi
dhatte smarāriḥ śirasāpi yat tvām
119.d:
न ते विभूतिं ननु वेत्ति को ऽपि
त्रैलोक्यवन्द्ये जगदम्ब गङ्गे
गौरीसमालिङ्गितविग्रहो ऽपि
धत्ते स्मरारिः शिरसापि यत् त्वाम्
119.m:
Indeed, no one knows your majestic power,
O mother of the world, Gaṅgā, revered by the three worlds,
since the enemy of Smara, even while his body is embraced by Gaurī,
holds you upon his head!

119.s:
namo 'stu te mātar abhīṣṭadāyini
namo 'stu te brahmamaye 'ghanāśini
namo 'stu te viṣṇupadābjaniḥsṛte
namo 'stu te śaṃbhujaṭāviniḥsṛte
119.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते मातर् अभीष्टदायिनि
नमो ऽस्तु ते ब्रह्ममये ऽघनाशिनि
नमो ऽस्तु ते विष्णुपदाब्जनिःसृते
नमो ऽस्तु ते शंभुजटाविनिःसृते
119.m:
Homage to you, O mother who grants desired wishes!
Homage to you who are made of brahman, destroyer of sins!
Homage to you who flow forth from the lotus foot of Viṣṇu!
Homage to you who flow forth from the matted locks of Śambhu!

119.s:
brahmovāca
ity evaṃ stuvatām īśā kiṃ dadāmīty avocata //
119.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् एवं स्तुवताम् ईशा किं ददामीत्य् अवोचत ॥
119.m:
Brahmā said:
To those praising her in this manner, the sovereign [river] said: "What shall I give?"

119.s:
oṣadhya ūcuḥ
patiṃ dehi jaganmātā rājānam atitejasam //
119.d:
ओषध्य ऊचुः
पतिं देहि जगन्माता राजानम् अतितेजसम् ॥
119.m:
The medicinal plants said:
O mother of the world, give us a lord, a king of immense splendor!

119.s:
brahmovāca
tadovāca nadī gaṅgā oṣadhīs tā idaṃ vacaḥ //
119.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तदोवाच नदी गङ्गा ओषधीस् ता इदं वचः ॥
119.m:
Brahmā said:
Then the river Gaṅgā spoke these words to the medicinal plants:

119.s:
gaṅgovāca
ahaṃ cāmṛtarūpāsmi oṣadhyo mātaro 'mṛtāḥ
tādṛśaṃ cāmṛtātmānaṃ patiṃ somaṃ dadāmi vaḥ //
119.d:
गङ्गोवाच
अहं चामृतरूपास्मि ओषध्यो मातरो ऽमृताः
तादृशं चामृतात्मानं पतिं सोमं ददामि वः ॥
119.m:
Gaṅgā said:
I am of the nature of nectar, and you, medicinal plants, are immortal mothers.
I give to you such a lord of nectar-nature, Soma.

119.s:
brahmovāca
devāś ca ṛṣayo vākyaṃ menire soma eva ca
oṣadhyaś cāpi tad vākyaṃ tato jagmuḥ svam ālayam //
119.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
देवाश् च ऋषयो वाक्यं मेनिरे सोम एव च
ओषध्यश् चापि तद् वाक्यं ततो जग्मुः स्वम् आलयम् ॥

119.s:
yatra cāpur mahauṣadhyo rājānam amṛtātmakam
somaṃ samastasaṃtāpapāpasaṃghanivārakam //
119.d:
यत्र चापुर् महौषध्यो राजानम् अमृतात्मकम्
सोमं समस्तसंतापपापसंघनिवारकम् ॥
119.m:
Where the great medicinal plants obtained a king of nectar-nature,
Soma, the remover of all torment and hosts of sins,

119.s:
somatīrthaṃ tu tat khyātaṃ somapānaphalapradam
tatra snānena dānena pitaraḥ svargam āpnuyuḥ //
119.d:
सोमतीर्थं तु तत् ख्यातं सोमपानफलप्रदम्
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन पितरः स्वर्गम् आप्नुयुः ॥
119.m:
that is known as Somatīrtha, granting the fruit of drinking soma;
by bathing and giving gifts there, ancestors attain heaven.

119.s:
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ paṭhed vā bhaktitaḥ smaret
dīrgham āyur avāpnoti sa putrī dhanavān bhavet //
119.d:
य इदं शृणुयान् नित्यं पठेद् वा भक्तितः स्मरेत्
दीर्घम् आयुर् अवाप्नोति स पुत्री धनवान् भवेत् ॥
119.m:
He who regularly hears this, reads it, or remembers it with devotion,
attains a long life; he will possess sons and wealth.

120.s:
brahmovāca
dhānyatīrtham iti khyātaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām
subhikṣaṃ kṣemadaṃ puṃsāṃ sarvāpadvinivāraṇam //
120.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
धान्यतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं सर्वकामप्रदं नृणाम्
सुभिक्षं क्षेमदं पुंसां सर्वापद्विनिवारणम् ॥
120.m:
Brahmā said:
There is that known as Dhānyatīrtha, granting all desires to mortals,
bestowing abundance and security to men, removing all misfortunes.

120.s:
oṣadhyaḥ somarājānaṃ patiṃ prāpya mudānvitāḥ
ūcuḥ sarvasya lokasya gaṅgāyāś cepsitaṃ vacaḥ //
120.d:
ओषध्यः सोमराजानं पतिं प्राप्य मुदान्विताः
ऊचुः सर्वस्य लोकस्य गङ्गायाश् चेप्सितं वचः ॥
120.m:
The medicinal plants, filled with joy upon obtaining King Soma as their lord,
spoke words desired by all the world and by Gaṅgā.

120.s:
oṣadhya ūcuḥ
vaidikī puṇyagāthāsti yāṃ vai vedavido viduḥ
bhūmiṃ sasyavatīṃ kaścin mātaraṃ mātṛsaṃmitām //
120.d:
ओषध्य ऊचुः
वैदिकी पुण्यगाथास्ति यां वै वेदविदो विदुः
भूमिं सस्यवतीं कश्चिन् मातरं मातृसंमिताम् ॥
120.m:
The medicinal plants said:
There is a sacred Vedic verse which those who know the Vedas know:
[If] anyone [gives] the earth, bearing crops, like a mother, equal to a mother,

120.s:
gaṅgāsamīpe yo dadyāt sarvakāmān avāpnuyāt
bhūmiṃ sasyavatīṃ gāś ca oṣadhīś ca mudānvitaḥ //
120.d:
गङ्गासमीपे यो दद्यात् सर्वकामान् अवाप्नुयात्
भूमिं सस्यवतीं गाश् च ओषधीश् च मुदान्वितः ॥
120.m:
he who gives it near the Gaṅgā shall attain all desires.
The earth bearing crops, and cows, and medicinal plants—he who, filled with joy,

120.s:
viṣṇubrahmeśarūpāya yo dadyād bhaktimān naraḥ
sarvaṃ tad akṣayaṃ vidyāt sarvakāmān avāpnuyāt //
120.d:
विष्णुब्रह्मेशरूपाय यो दद्याद् भक्तिमान् नरः
सर्वं तद् अक्षयं विद्यात् सर्वकामान् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
120.m:
a devoted man, gives them to one who embodies Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and the Lord—
he should know that all of it becomes imperishable; he will attain all desires.

120.s:
oṣadhyaḥ somarājanyāḥ somaś cāpy oṣadhīpatiḥ
iti jñātvā brahmavida oṣadhīr yaḥ pradāsyati //
120.d:
ओषध्यः सोमराजन्याः सोमश् चाप्य् ओषधीपतिः
इति ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मविद ओषधीर् यः प्रदास्यति ॥
120.m:
The medicinal plants have Soma as their king, and Soma is the lord of medicinal plants;
knowing this, he who gives medicinal plants to one who knows brahman

120.s:
sarvān kāmān avāpnoti brahmaloke mahīyate
tā eva somarājanyāḥ prītāḥ procuḥ punaḥ punaḥ //
120.d:
सर्वान् कामान् अवाप्नोति ब्रह्मलोके महीयते
ता एव सोमराजन्याः प्रीताः प्रोचुः पुनः पुनः ॥
120.m:
attains all desires and is glorified in the world of Brahmā.
Those very ones whose king is Soma, delighted, spoke repeatedly:

120.s:
oṣadhya ūcuḥ
yo 'smān dadāti gaṅgāyāṃ taṃ rājan pārayāmasi
tvam uttamaś cauṣadhīśa tvadadhīnaṃ carācaram //
120.d:
ओषध्य ऊचुः
यो ऽस्मान् ददाति गङ्गायां तं राजन् पारयामसि
त्वम् उत्तमश् चौषधीश त्वदधीनं चराचरम् ॥
120.m:
The medicinal plants said:
He who gives us at the Gaṅgā, him, O King, we bring across.
You are the supreme lord of medicinal plants; under your power is all that moves and does not move.

120.s:
oṣadhayaḥ saṃvadante somena saha rājñā
yo 'smān dadāti viprebhyas taṃ rājan pārayāmasi //
120.d:
ओषधयः संवदन्ते सोमेन सह राज्ञा
यो ऽस्मान् ददाति विप्रेभ्यस् तं राजन् पारयामसि ॥
120.m:
The medicinal plants converse together with King Soma:
"He who gives us to brāhmaṇas, him, O King, we bring across.

120.s:
vayaṃ ca brahmarūpiṇyaḥ prāṇarūpiṇya eva ca
yo 'smān dadāti viprebhyas taṃ rājan pārayāmasi //
120.d:
वयं च ब्रह्मरूपिण्यः प्राणरूपिण्य एव च
यो ऽस्मान् ददाति विप्रेभ्यस् तं राजन् पारयामसि ॥
120.m:
We are forms of brahman and forms of life-breath;
he who gives us to brāhmaṇas, him, O King, we bring across.

120.s:
asmān dadāti yo nityaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo jitavrataḥ
upāstir asti sāsmākaṃ taṃ rājan pārayāmasi //
120.d:
अस्मान् ददाति यो नित्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो जितव्रतः
उपास्तिर् अस्ति सास्माकं तं राजन् पारयामसि ॥
120.m:
He who continually gives us to brāhmaṇas, steadfast in his vow—
that is worship of us; him, O King, we bring across."

120.s:
sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ kiṃcid asmābhir vyāpṛtaṃ jagat
yo 'smān dadāti viprebhyas taṃ rājan pārayāmasi //
120.d:
स्थावरं जङ्गमं किंचिद् अस्माभिर् व्यापृतं जगत्
यो ऽस्मान् ददाति विप्रेभ्यस् तं राजन् पारयामसि ॥
120.m: Whatever is stationary or moving in the world is pervaded by us. / Whoever gives us to the twice-born, O king, him we carry across.

120.s:
havyaṃ kavyaṃ yad amṛtaṃ yat kiṃcid upabhujyate
tadgarīyaś ca yo dadyāt taṃ rājan pārayāmasi //
120.d:
हव्यं कव्यं यद् अमृतं यत् किंचिद् उपभुज्यते
तद्गरीयश् च यो दद्यात् तं राजन् पारयामसि ॥
120.m: Whatever oblations to the gods or ancestors, whatever nectar, whatever at all is consumed— / and whoever gives what is superior to that, O king, him we carry across.

120.s:
ity etāṃ vaidikīṃ gāthāṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti smareta vā
paṭhate bhaktim āpannas taṃ rājan pārayāmasi //
120.d:
इत्य् एतां वैदिकीं गाथां यः शृणोति स्मरेत वा
पठते भक्तिम् आपन्नस् तं राजन् पारयामसि ॥
120.m: Whoever, having attained devotion, hears, remembers, / or recites this Vedic hymn, O king, him we carry across.

120.s:
brahmovāca
yatraiṣā paṭhitā gāthā somena saha rājñā
gaṅgātīre cauṣadhībhir dhānyatīrthaṃ tad ucyate //
120.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यत्रैषा पठिता गाथा सोमेन सह राज्ञा
गङ्गातीरे चौषधीभिर् धान्यतीर्थं तद् उच्यते ॥
120.m: Brahmā said: / Where this hymn was recited by the king along with Soma / and the medicinal plants on the bank of the Gaṅgā, that is called Dhānyatīrtha.

120.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrtham auṣadhyaṃ saumyam eva ca
amṛtaṃ vedagāthaṃ ca mātṛtīrthaṃ tathaiva ca //
120.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थम् औषध्यं सौम्यम् एव च
अमृतं वेदगाथं च मातृतीर्थं तथैव च ॥
120.m: From then on, that sacred place is Auṣadhya, Saumya, / Amṛta, Vedagātha, and also Mātṛtīrtha.

120.s:
eṣu snānaṃ japo homo dānaṃ ca pitṛtarpaṇam
annadānaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt tad ānantyāya kalpate //
120.d:
एषु स्नानं जपो होमो दानं च पितृतर्पणम्
अन्नदानं तु यः कुर्यात् तद् आनन्त्याय कल्पते ॥
120.m: Whoever performs bathing, silent recitation, fire-offering, gift-giving, water-libations to the ancestors, / and the gift of food at these [places], that tends toward infinity.

120.s:
ṣaṭśatādhikasāhasraṃ tīrthānāṃ tīrayor dvayoḥ
sarvapāpanihantṝṇāṃ sarvasaṃpadvivardhanam //
120.d:
षट्शताधिकसाहस्रं तीर्थानां तीरयोर् द्वयोः
सर्वपापनिहन्तॄणां सर्वसंपद्विवर्धनम् ॥
120.m: On both banks there are one thousand and six hundred sacred places / that destroy all sins and increase all prosperity.

121.s:
brahmovāca
vidarbhāsaṃgamaṃ puṇyaṃ revatīsaṃgamaṃ tathā
tatra yad vṛttam ākhyāsye yat purāṇavido viduḥ //
121.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
विदर्भासंगमं पुण्यं रेवतीसंगमं तथा
तत्र यद् वृत्तम् आख्यास्ये यत् पुराणविदो विदुः ॥
121.m: Brahmā said: / There is the holy confluence of the Vidarbhā and likewise the confluence of the Revatī; / I shall relate what happened there, which those who know the Purāṇas know.

121.s:
bharadvāja iti khyāta ṛṣir āsīt tapodhikaḥ
tasya svasā revatīti kurūpā vikṛtasvarā //
121.d:
भरद्वाज इति ख्यात ऋषिर् आसीत् तपोधिकः
तस्य स्वसा रेवतीति कुरूपा विकृतस्वरा ॥
121.m: There was a sage celebrated as Bharadvāja, rich in austerities. / His sister, named Revatī, was deformed and had a discordant voice.

121.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṛtāṃ bhrātā bharadvājaḥ pratāpavān
cintayā parayā yukto gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe taṭe //
121.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा विकृतां भ्राता भरद्वाजः प्रतापवान्
चिन्तया परया युक्तो गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तटे ॥
121.m: Seeing her deformed, her brother, the glorious Bharadvāja, / was seized with great anxiety on the southern bank of the Gaṅgā:

121.s:
kasmai dadyām imāṃ kanyāṃ svasāraṃ bhīṣaṇākṛtim
na kaścit pratigṛhṇāti dātavyā ca svasā tathā //
121.d:
कस्मै दद्याम् इमां कन्यां स्वसारं भीषणाकृतिम्
न कश्चित् प्रतिगृह्णाति दातव्या च स्वसा तथा ॥
121.m: "To whom may I give this maiden, my sister of terrifying appearance? / No one accepts her, yet my sister must be given in marriage.

121.s:
aho bhūyān na kasyāpi kanyā duḥkhaikakāraṇam
maraṇaṃ jīvato 'py asya prāṇinas tu pade pade //
121.d:
अहो भूयान् न कस्यापि कन्या दुःखैककारणम्
मरणं जीवतो ऽप्य् अस्य प्राणिनस् तु पदे पदे ॥
121.m: Alas, may no one have a daughter, the sole cause of sorrow! / For this living creature, there is death at every step, even while alive."

121.s:
evaṃ vimṛśatas tasya svāśrame cātiśobhane
draṣṭuṃ munivaraḥ prāyād bharadvājaṃ yatavratam //
121.d:
एवं विमृशतस् तस्य स्वाश्रमे चातिशोभने
द्रष्टुं मुनिवरः प्रायाद् भरद्वाजं यतव्रतम् ॥
121.m: As he was pondering thus in his very lovely hermitage, / an excellent sage came to see Bharadvāja of restrained vows.

121.s:
dvyaṣṭavarṣaḥ śubhavapuḥ śānto dānto guṇākaraḥ
nāmnā kaṭha iti khyāto bharadvājaṃ nanāma saḥ //
121.d:
द्व्यष्टवर्षः शुभवपुः शान्तो दान्तो गुणाकरः
नाम्ना कठ इति ख्यातो भरद्वाजं ननाम सः ॥
121.m: He was sixteen years old, of auspicious body, calm, self-controlled, a mine of virtues, / renowned by the name Kaṭha; he bowed to Bharadvāja.

121.s:
vidhivat pūjya taṃ vipraṃ bharadvājaḥ kaṭhaṃ tadā
tasyāgamanakāryaṃ ca papraccha purataḥ sthitaḥ //
121.d:
विधिवत् पूज्य तं विप्रं भरद्वाजः कठं तदा
तस्यागमनकार्यं च पप्रच्छ पुरतः स्थितः ॥
121.m: Duly honoring that twice-born Kaṭha, / Bharadvāja then stood before him and asked the purpose of his arrival.

121.s:
kaṭho 'py āha bharadvājaṃ vidyārthy aham upāgataḥ
tathā ca darśanākāṅkṣī yad yuktaṃ tad vidhīyatām //
121.d:
कठो ऽप्य् आह भरद्वाजं विद्यार्थ्य् अहम् उपागतः
तथा च दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी यद् युक्तं तद् विधीयताम् ॥
121.m: Kaṭha too said to Bharadvāja, "I have come seeking knowledge / and desiring to see [you]; let that be done which is fitting."

121.s:
bharadvājaḥ kaṭhaṃ prāha adhīṣva yad abhīpsitam
purāṇaṃ smṛtayo vedā dharmasthānāny anekaśaḥ //
121.d:
भरद्वाजः कठं प्राह अधीष्व यद् अभीप्सितम्
पुराणं स्मृतयो वेदा धर्मस्थानान्य् अनेकशः ॥
121.m: Bharadvāja said to Kaṭha, "Study whatever is desired: / the Purāṇa, the Smṛtis, the Vedas, and numerous abodes of dharma.

121.s:
sarvaṃ vedmi mahāprājña ruciraṃ vada mā ciram
kulīno dharmanirato guruśuśrūṣaṇe rataḥ
abhimānī śrutadharaḥ śiṣyaḥ puṇyair avāpyate //
121.d:
सर्वं वेद्मि महाप्राज्ञ रुचिरं वद मा चिरम्
कुलीनो धर्मनिरतो गुरुशुश्रूषणे रतः
अभिमानी श्रुतधरः शिष्यः पुण्यैर् अवाप्यते ॥
121.m: I know everything, O highly wise one; speak your pleasure without delay. / A disciple who is high-born, devoted to dharma, devoted to serving the guru, / self-respecting, and able to retain what is heard is attained through merits."

121.s:
kaṭha uvāca
adhyāpayasva bho brahmañ śiṣyaṃ māṃ vītakalmaṣam
śuśrūṣaṇarataṃ bhaktaṃ kulīnaṃ satyavādinam //
121.d:
कठ उवाच
अध्यापयस्व भो ब्रह्मञ् शिष्यं मां वीतकल्मषम्
शुश्रूषणरतं भक्तं कुलीनं सत्यवादिनम् ॥
121.m: Kaṭha said: / "Instruct me, O holy one, as a disciple free from blemish, / devoted to your service, devoted, well-born, and truthful."

121.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā bharadvājaḥ prādād vidyām aśeṣataḥ
prāptavidyaḥ kaṭhaḥ prīto bharadvājam athābravīt //
121.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा भरद्वाजः प्रादाद् विद्याम् अशेषतः
प्राप्तविद्यः कठः प्रीतो भरद्वाजम् अथाब्रवीत् ॥
121.m: Brahmā said: / Saying 'So be it,' Bharadvāja imparted all knowledge without remainder. / Having acquired the knowledge, the delighted Kaṭha then said to Bharadvāja:

121.s:
kaṭha uvāca
iccheyaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dātuṃ guro tava manaḥpriyām
vadasva durlabhaṃ vāpi guro tubhyaṃ namo 'stu te //
121.d:
कठ उवाच
इच्छेयं दक्षिणां दातुं गुरो तव मनःप्रियाम्
वदस्व दुर्लभं वापि गुरो तुभ्यं नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
121.m: Kaṭha said: / "I wish to give a guru's fee pleasing to your mind, O guru; / speak, even if it is difficult to attain, O guru; reverence be to you!

121.s:
vidyāṃ prāpyāpi ye mohāt svaguroḥ pāritoṣikam
na prayacchanti nirayaṃ te yānty ācandratārakam //
121.d:
विद्यां प्राप्यापि ये मोहात् स्वगुरोः पारितोषिकम्
न प्रयच्छन्ति निरयं ते यान्त्य् आचन्द्रतारकम् ॥
121.m: Those who, even after receiving knowledge, through delusion do not grant / a recompense to their guru, go to hell as long as the moon and the stars endure."

121.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
gṛhāṇa kanyāṃ vidhivad bhāryāṃ kuru mama svasām
asyāṃ prītyā vartitavyaṃ yāceyaṃ dakṣiṇām imām //
121.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
गृहाण कन्यां विधिवद् भार्यां कुरु मम स्वसाम्
अस्यां प्रीत्या वर्तितव्यं याचेयं दक्षिणाम् इमाम् ॥
121.m: Bharadvāja said: / "Accept this maiden according to rule; make my sister your wife. / You must live with her in affection; this is the fee I ask."

121.s:
kaṭha uvāca
bhrātṛvat putravac cāpi śiṣyaḥ syāt tu guroḥ sadā
guruś ca pitṛvac ca syāt saṃbandho 'tra kathaṃ bhavet //
121.d:
कठ उवाच
भ्रातृवत् पुत्रवच् चापि शिष्यः स्यात् तु गुरोः सदा
गुरुश् च पितृवच् च स्यात् संबन्धो ऽत्र कथं भवेत् ॥
121.m: Kaṭha said: / "A disciple is always like a brother and like a son to the guru, / and the guru is like a father; how can there be a [marital] union here?"

121.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
madvākyaṃ kuru satyaṃ tvaṃ mamājñā tava dakṣiṇā
sarvaṃ smṛtvā kaṭhādya tvaṃ revatīṃ bhara tanmanāḥ //
121.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
मद्वाक्यं कुरु सत्यं त्वं ममाज्ञा तव दक्षिणा
सर्वं स्मृत्वा कठाद्य त्वं रेवतीं भर तन्मनाः ॥
121.m: Bharadvāja said: / "Make my word true; my command is your fee. / Remembering everything, O Kaṭha, today support Revatī with a focused mind."

121.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā guror vākyāt kaṭho jagrāha pāṇinā
revatīṃ vidhivad dattāṃ tāṃ samīkṣya kaṭhas tv atha //
121.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा गुरोर् वाक्यात् कठो जग्राह पाणिना
रेवतीं विधिवद् दत्तां तां समीक्ष्य कठस् त्व् अथ ॥
121.m: Brahmā said: / Saying 'So be it,' at the word of the guru, Kaṭha took by the hand / Revatī, who was given according to rule. But then, looking upon her, Kaṭha

121.s:
tatraiva pūjayām āsa deveśaṃ śaṃkaraṃ tadā
revatyā rūpasaṃpattyai śivaprītyai ca revatī //
121.d:
तत्रैव पूजयाम् आस देवेशं शंकरं तदा
रेवत्या रूपसंपत्त्यै शिवप्रीत्यै च रेवती ॥
121.m: worshiped Śaṅkara, the lord of gods, right there / for Revatī's acquisition of beauty and for the pleasure of Śiva; and Revatī,

121.s:
surūpā cārusarvāṅgī na rūpeṇopamīyate
abhiṣekodakaṃ tatra revatyā yad viniḥsṛtam //
121.d:
सुरूपा चारुसर्वाङ्गी न रूपेणोपमीयते
अभिषेकोदकं तत्र रेवत्या यद् विनिःसृतम् ॥
121.m: becoming beautiful, having lovely limbs all over, was beyond compare in beauty. / The consecration water that flowed from Revatī there

121.s:
sābhavat tatra gaṅgāyāṃ tasmāt tannāmato nadī
revatīti samākhyātā rūpasaubhāgyadāyinī //
121.d:
साभवत् तत्र गङ्गायां तस्मात् तन्नामतो नदी
रेवतीति समाख्याता रूपसौभाग्यदायिनी ॥
121.m: became a river there at the Gaṅgā; therefore, after her name, / it is known as Revatī, bestowing beauty and good fortune.

121.s:
punar darbhaiś ca vividhair abhiṣekaṃ cakāra saḥ
puṇyarūpatvasaṃsiddhyai vidarbhā tad abhūn nadī //
121.d:
पुनर् दर्भैश् च विविधैर् अभिषेकं चकार सः
पुण्यरूपत्वसंसिद्ध्यै विदर्भा तद् अभून् नदी ॥
121.m: Again, he performed a consecration with various darbha grasses / for the attainment of holy form; that became the river Vidarbhā.

121.s:
śraddhayā saṃgame snātvā revatīgaṅgayor naraḥ
sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇuloke mahīyate //
121.d:
श्रद्धया संगमे स्नात्वा रेवतीगङ्गयोर् नरः
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोके महीयते ॥
121.m: A man who bathes with faith at the confluence of the Revatī and the Gaṅgā / is freed from all sins and glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.

121.s:
tathā vidarbhāgautamyoḥ saṃgame śraddhayā mune
snānaṃ karoty asau yāti bhuktiṃ muktiṃ ca tatkṣaṇāt //
121.d:
तथा विदर्भागौतम्योः संगमे श्रद्धया मुने
स्नानं करोत्य् असौ याति भुक्तिं मुक्तिं च तत्क्षणात् ॥
121.m: Likewise, O sage, he who bathes with faith at the confluence of the Vidarbhā and the Gautamī / instantly attains enjoyment and liberation.

121.s:
ubhayos tīrayos tatra tīrthānāṃ śatam uttamam
sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam //
121.d:
उभयोस् तीरयोस् तत्र तीर्थानां शतम् उत्तमम्
सर्वपापक्षयकरं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकम् ॥
121.m: On both banks there are an excellent hundred sacred places, / bringing about the destruction of all sins and bestowing all perfections.

122.s:
brahmovāca
pūrṇatīrtham iti khyātaṃ gaṅgāyā uttare taṭe
tatra snātvā naro 'jñānāt tathāpi śubham āpnuyāt //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पूर्णतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं गङ्गाया उत्तरे तटे
तत्र स्नात्वा नरो ऽज्ञानात् तथापि शुभम् आप्नुयात् ॥
122.m: Brahmā said: / There is the renowned Pūrṇatīrtha on the northern bank of the Gaṅgā; / bathing there even through ignorance, a person nevertheless obtains good fortune.

122.s:
pūrṇatīrthasya māhātmyaṃ varṇyate kena jantunā
svayaṃ saṃsthīyate yatra cakriṇā ca pinākinā //
122.d:
पूर्णतीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं वर्ण्यते केन जन्तुना
स्वयं संस्थीयते यत्र चक्रिणा च पिनाकिना ॥
122.m: By what living being can the greatness of Pūrṇatīrtha be described, / where the wielder of the discus and the wielder of the Pināka bow dwell in person?

122.s:
purā dhanvantarir nāma kalpādāv āyuṣaḥ sutaḥ
iṣṭvā bahuvidhair yajñair aśvamedhapuraḥsaraiḥ //
122.d:
पुरा धन्वन्तरिर् नाम कल्पादाव् आयुषः सुतः
इष्ट्वा बहुविधैर् यज्ञैर् अश्वमेधपुरःसरैः ॥
122.m: Formerly, at the beginning of a kalpa, the son of Āyus named Dhanvantari, / having sacrificed with manifold sacrifices preceded by the horse-sacrifice,

122.s:
dattvā dānāny anekāni bhuktvā bhogāṃś ca puṣkalān
vijñāya bhogavaiṣamyaṃ paraṃ vairāgyam āśritaḥ //
122.d:
दत्त्वा दानान्य् अनेकानि भुक्त्वा भोगांश् च पुष्कलान्
विज्ञाय भोगवैषम्यं परं वैराग्यम् आश्रितः ॥
122.m: having given many gifts, and having enjoyed abundant pleasures, / realized the defectiveness of pleasures and resorted to supreme dispassion.

122.s:
giriśṛṅge 'mbudheḥ pāre tathā gaṅgānadītaṭe
śivaviṣṇvor gṛhe vāpi viśeṣāt puṇyasaṃgame //
122.d:
गिरिशृङ्गे ऽम्बुधेः पारे तथा गङ्गानदीतटे
शिवविष्ण्वोर् गृहे वापि विशेषात् पुण्यसंगमे ॥
122.m: On a mountain peak, on the shore of the ocean, or on the bank of the river Gaṅgā, / or in a temple of Śiva and Viṣṇu, especially at a holy confluence,

122.s:
taptaṃ hutaṃ ca japtaṃ ca sarvam akṣayatāṃ vrajet
dhanvantarir iti jñātvā tatra tepe tapo mahat //
122.d:
तप्तं हुतं च जप्तं च सर्वम् अक्षयतां व्रजेत्
धन्वन्तरिर् इति ज्ञात्वा तत्र तेपे तपो महत् ॥
122.m: austerity performed, oblations offered, and silent recitations muttered—all reach imperishability. / Knowing this, Dhanvantari performed great austerity there.

122.s:
jñānavairāgyasaṃpanno bhīmeśacaraṇāśrayaḥ
tapaś cakāra vipulaṃ gaṅgāsāgarasaṃgame //
122.d:
ज्ञानवैराग्यसंपन्नो भीमेशचरणाश्रयः
तपश् चकार विपुलं गङ्गासागरसंगमे ॥
122.m: Endowed with knowledge and dispassion, taking refuge at the feet of Bhīmeśa, / he performed extensive austerity at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean.

122.s:
purā ca nikṛto rājñā raṇaṃ hitvā mahāsuraḥ
sahasram ekaṃ varṣāṇāṃ samudraṃ prāviśad bhayāt //
122.d:
पुरा च निकृतो राज्ञा रणं हित्वा महासुरः
सहस्रम् एकं वर्षाणां समुद्रं प्राविशद् भयात् ॥
122.m: Formerly, a great asura, having been defeated by the king and abandoning the battle, / entered the ocean out of fear for a thousand years.

122.s:
dhanvantarau vanaṃ prāpte rājyaṃ prāpte tu tatsute
virāgaṃ ca gate rājñi tataḥ prāyād athārṇavāt //
122.d:
धन्वन्तरौ वनं प्राप्ते राज्यं प्राप्ते तु तत्सुते
विरागं च गते राज्ञि ततः प्रायाद् अथार्णवात् ॥
122.m: When Dhanvantari had gone to the forest, his son had attained the kingdom, / and the king had attained dispassion, he then came out of the ocean.

122.s:
tapasyantaṃ tamo nāma balavān asuro mune
gaṅgātīraṃ samāśritya rājā dhanvantarir yataḥ //
122.d:
तपस्यन्तं तमो नाम बलवान् असुरो मुने
गङ्गातीरं समाश्रित्य राजा धन्वन्तरिर् यतः ॥
122.m: A powerful asura named Tama, O sage, [sought] / the king Dhanvantari, who was practicing austerity, having resorted to the bank of the Gaṅgā,

122.s:
japahomarato nityaṃ brahmajñānaparāyaṇaḥ
taṃ ripuṃ nāśayāmīti tamaḥ prāyād athārṇavāt //
122.d:
जपहोमरतो नित्यं ब्रह्मज्ञानपरायणः
तं रिपुं नाशयामीति तमः प्रायाद् अथार्णवात् ॥
122.m: ever devoted to silent recitation and fire-offerings, intent on the knowledge of Brahman. / Thinking 'I shall destroy that enemy,' Tama then emerged from the ocean.

122.s:
nāśito bahuśo 'nena rājñā balavatā tv aham
taṃ ripuṃ nāśayāmīti tamaḥ prāyād athārṇavāt //
122.d:
नाशितो बहुशो ऽनेन राज्ञा बलवता त्व् अहम्
तं रिपुं नाशयामीति तमः प्रायाद् अथार्णवात् ॥
122.m: "Indeed, I was defeated many times by this powerful king; / I shall destroy that enemy!"—thinking thus, Tama came forth from the ocean.

122.s:
māyayā pramadārūpaṃ kṛtvā rājānam abhyagāt
nṛtyagītavatī subhrūr hasantī cārudarśanā //
122.d:
मायया प्रमदारूपं कृत्वा राजानम् अभ्यगात्
नृत्यगीतवती सुभ्रूर् हसन्ती चारुदर्शना ॥
122.m: By his illusory power, he assumed the form of a young woman and approached the king, / endowed with dance and song, fair-browed, smiling, and lovely to behold.

122.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā cārusarvāṅgīṃ bahukālaṃ nayānvitām
śāntām anuvratāṃ bhaktāṃ kṛpayā cābravīn nṛpaḥ //
122.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा चारुसर्वाङ्गीं बहुकालं नयान्विताम्
शान्ताम् अनुव्रतां भक्तां कृपया चाब्रवीन् नृपः ॥
122.m: Seeing her with all her limbs lovely, for a long time well-behaved, / peaceful, devoted, and faithful, the king spoke with compassion:

122.s:
nṛpa uvāca
kāsi tvaṃ kasya hetor vā vartase gahane vane
kaṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣasīva tvaṃ vada kalyāṇi pṛcchate //
122.d:
नृप उवाच
कासि त्वं कस्य हेतोर् वा वर्तसे गहने वने
कं दृष्ट्वा हर्षसीव त्वं वद कल्याणि पृच्छते ॥
122.m:
The king said:
"Who are you, or for what reason do you dwell in this dense forest? / Seeing whom do you seem to rejoice? Tell, auspicious woman, to one who asks!"

122.s:
brahmovāca
pramadā cāpi tadvākyaṃ śrutvā rājānam abravīt //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
प्रमदा चापि तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा राजानम् अब्रवीत् ॥
122.m:
Brahmā said:
Having heard his words, the woman spoke to the king:

122.s:
pramadovāca
tvayi tiṣṭhati ko loke hetur harṣasya me bhavet
aham indrasya yā lakṣmīs tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmasaṃbhṛtam //
122.d:
प्रमदोवाच
त्वयि तिष्ठति को लोके हेतुर् हर्षस्य मे भवेत्
अहम् इन्द्रस्य या लक्ष्मीस् त्वां दृष्ट्वा कामसंभृतम् ॥
122.m:
The woman said:
"While you are present, what reason in the world could there be for my joy? / I am the very Lakṣmī of Indra; having seen you filled with desire,

122.s:
harṣāc carāmi purato rājaṃs tava punaḥ punaḥ
agaṇyapuṇyavirahād ahaṃ sarvasya durlabhā //
122.d:
हर्षाच् चरामि पुरतो राजंस् तव पुनः पुनः
अगण्यपुण्यविरहाद् अहं सर्वस्य दुर्लभा ॥
122.m: I wander out of delight before you, O king, again and again. / In the absence of boundless merit, I am hard to attain for anyone."

122.s:
brahmovāca
etad vaco niśamyāśu tapas tyaktvā suduṣkaram
tām eva manasā dhyāyaṃs tanniṣṭhas tatparāyaṇaḥ //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतद् वचो निशम्याशु तपस् त्यक्त्वा सुदुष्करम्
ताम् एव मनसा ध्यायंस् तन्निष्ठस् तत्परायणः ॥
122.m:
Brahmā said:
Having heard these words, he immediately abandoned his exceedingly difficult penance. / Meditating upon her alone in his mind, intent on her, devoted to her,

122.s:
tadekaśaraṇo rājā babhūva sa yadā tamaḥ
antardhānaṃ gato brahman nāśayitvā tapo bṛhat //
122.d:
तदेकशरणो राजा बभूव स यदा तमः
अन्तर्धानं गतो ब्रह्मन् नाशयित्वा तपो बृहत् ॥
122.m: when the king became someone whose sole refuge was her, Tama, / having ruined his great penance, vanished, O brahmin.

122.s:
etasminn antare 'haṃ vai varān dātuṃ samabhyagām
taṃ dṛṣṭvā vihvalībhūtaṃ tapobhraṣṭaṃ yathā mṛtam //
122.d:
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे ऽहं वै वरान् दातुं समभ्यगाम्
तं दृष्ट्वा विह्वलीभूतं तपोभ्रष्टं यथा मृतम् ॥
122.m: In the meantime, I truly arrived to grant boons. / Seeing him bewildered, fallen from penance, as if dead,

122.s:
tam āśvāsyātha vividhair hetubhir nṛpasattamam
tava śatrus tamo nāma kṛtvā tāṃ tapasaś cyutim //
122.d:
तम् आश्वास्याथ विविधैर् हेतुभिर् नृपसत्तमम्
तव शत्रुस् तमो नाम कृत्वा तां तपसश् च्युतिम् ॥
122.m: and comforting that best of kings with various arguments, [I said]: / "Your enemy named Tama brought about that fall from penance,

122.s:
caritārtho gato rājan na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
ānandayanti pramadās tāpayanti ca mānavam //
122.d:
चरितार्थो गतो राजन् न त्वं शोचितुम् अर्हसि
आनन्दयन्ति प्रमदास् तापयन्ति च मानवम् ॥
122.m: and, having achieved his purpose, has gone, O king. You should not grieve. / Women bring joy and bring torment to a man—

122.s:
sarvā eva viśeṣeṇa kim u māyāmayī tu sā
tataḥ kṛtāñjalī rājā mām āha vigatabhramaḥ //
122.d:
सर्वा एव विशेषेण किम् उ मायामयी तु सा
ततः कृताञ्जली राजा माम् आह विगतभ्रमः ॥
122.m: all of them especially; how much more so one composed of illusory power?" / Then the king, with folded hands, his delusion gone, spoke to me:

122.s:
rājovāca
kiṃ karomi kathaṃ brahmaṃs tapasaḥ pāram āpnuyām //
122.d:
राजोवाच
किं करोमि कथं ब्रह्मंस् तपसः पारम् आप्नुयाम् ॥
122.m:
The king said:
"What shall I do? How, O Brahmā, may I attain the end of penance?"

122.s:
brahmovāca
tatas tasyottaraṃ prādāṃ devadevaṃ janārdanam
stuhi sarvaprayatnena tataḥ siddhim avāpsyasi //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततस् तस्योत्तरं प्रादां देवदेवं जनार्दनम्
स्तुहि सर्वप्रयत्नेन ततः सिद्धिम् अवाप्स्यसि ॥
122.m:
Brahmā said:
Then I gave him an answer: "Praise Janārdana, the god of gods, / with all effort; from that you will attain perfection.

122.s:
sa hy aśeṣajagatsraṣṭā vedavedyaḥ purātanaḥ
sarvārthasiddhidaḥ puṃsāṃ nānyo 'sti bhuvanatraye //
122.d:
स ह्य् अशेषजगत्स्रष्टा वेदवेद्यः पुरातनः
सर्वार्थसिद्धिदः पुंसां नान्यो ऽस्ति भुवनत्रये ॥
122.m: For he is the creator of the entire world, knowable through the Vedas, primeval, / the bestower of all success and aims to men; there is no other in the three worlds."

122.s:
sa jagāma nagaśreṣṭhaṃ himavantaṃ nṛpottamaḥ
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā viṣṇuṃ tuṣṭāva bhaktitaḥ //
122.d:
स जगाम नगश्रेष्ठं हिमवन्तं नृपोत्तमः
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा विष्णुं तुष्टाव भक्तितः ॥
122.m: That best of kings went to Himavat, the foremost of mountains. / Having folded his hands, he praised Viṣṇu with devotion.

122.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
jaya viṣṇo jayācintya jaya jiṣṇo jayācyuta
jaya gopāla lakṣmīśa jaya kṛṣṇa jaganmaya //
122.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
जय विष्णो जयाचिन्त्य जय जिष्णो जयाच्युत
जय गोपाल लक्ष्मीश जय कृष्ण जगन्मय ॥
122.m:
Dhanvantari said:
"Victory, O Viṣṇu! Victory, O inconceivable one! Victory, O victorious one! Victory, O infallible one! / Victory, O Gopāla, Lord of Lakṣmī! Victory, O Kṛṣṇa, whose self is the universe!

122.s:
jaya bhūtapate nātha jaya pannagaśāyine
jaya sarvaga govinda jaya viśvakṛte namaḥ //
122.d:
जय भूतपते नाथ जय पन्नगशायिने
जय सर्वग गोविन्द जय विश्वकृते नमः ॥
122.m: Victory, O Lord of beings, master! Victory to the one reclining on the serpent! / Victory, all-pervading Govinda! Victory, homage to the maker of the universe!

122.s:
jaya viśvabhuje deva jaya viśvadhṛte namaḥ
jayeśa sadasat tvaṃ vai jaya mādhava dharmiṇe //
122.d:
जय विश्वभुजे देव जय विश्वधृते नमः
जयेश सदसत् त्वं वै जय माधव धर्मिणे ॥
122.m: Victory, enjoyer of the universe, O God! Victory, homage to the supporter of the universe! / Victory, O Lord! You are indeed being and non-being. Victory, O Mādhava, to the righteous one!

122.s:
jaya kāmada kāma tvaṃ jaya rāma guṇārṇava
jaya puṣṭida puṣṭīśa jaya kalyāṇadāyine //
122.d:
जय कामद काम त्वं जय राम गुणार्णव
जय पुष्टिद पुष्टीश जय कल्याणदायिने ॥
122.m: Victory, granter of desires, you are desire! Victory, O Rāma, ocean of virtues! / Victory, bestower of nourishment, lord of nourishment! Victory to the bestower of auspiciousness!

122.s:
jaya bhūtapa bhūteśa jaya mānavidhāyine
jaya karmada karma tvaṃ jaya pītāmbaracchada //
122.d:
जय भूतप भूतेश जय मानविधायिने
जय कर्मद कर्म त्वं जय पीताम्बरच्छद ॥
122.m: Victory, protector of beings, lord of beings! Victory to the bestower of honor! / Victory, bestower of action, you are action! Victory, O you who are clad in yellow garments!

122.s:
jaya sarveśa sarvas tvaṃ jaya maṅgalarūpiṇe
jaya sattvādhināthāya jaya vedavide namaḥ //
122.d:
जय सर्वेश सर्वस् त्वं जय मङ्गलरूपिणे
जय सत्त्वाधिनाथाय जय वेदविदे नमः ॥
122.m: Victory, Lord of all, you are all! Victory to the one whose form is auspicious! / Victory to the overlord of goodness! Victory, homage to the knower of the Vedas!

122.s:
jaya janmada janmistha paramātman namo 'stu te
jaya muktida muktis tvaṃ jaya bhuktida keśava //
122.d:
जय जन्मद जन्मिस्थ परमात्मन् नमो ऽस्तु ते
जय मुक्तिद मुक्तिस् त्वं जय भुक्तिद केशव ॥
122.m: Victory, bestower of birth, abiding in the born! Supreme self, homage be to you! / Victory, bestower of liberation, you are liberation! Victory, bestower of enjoyment, O Keśava!

122.s:
jaya lokada lokeśa jaya pāpavināśana
jaya vatsala bhaktānāṃ jaya cakradhṛte namaḥ //
122.d:
जय लोकद लोकेश जय पापविनाशन
जय वत्सल भक्तानां जय चक्रधृते नमः ॥
122.m: Victory, bestower of realms, Lord of the worlds! Victory, destroyer of sin! / Victory, affectionate to devotees! Victory, homage to the bearer of the discus!

122.s:
jaya mānada mānas tvaṃ jaya lokanamaskṛta
jaya dharmada dharmas tvaṃ jaya saṃsārapāraga //
122.d:
जय मानद मानस् त्वं जय लोकनमस्कृत
जय धर्मद धर्मस् त्वं जय संसारपारग ॥
122.m: Victory, bestower of honor, you are honor! Victory, revered by the world! / Victory, bestower of dharma, you are dharma! Victory, crosser to the further shore of saṃsāra!

122.s:
jaya annada annaṃ tvaṃ jaya vācaspate namaḥ
jaya śaktida śaktis tvaṃ jaya jaitravaraprada //
122.d:
जय अन्नद अन्नं त्वं जय वाचस्पते नमः
जय शक्तिद शक्तिस् त्वं जय जैत्रवरप्रद ॥
122.m: Victory, giver of food, you are food! Victory, homage to the Lord of Speech! / Victory, giver of power, you are power! Victory, granter of victorious boons!

122.s:
jaya yajñada yajñas tvaṃ jaya padmadalekṣaṇa
jaya dānada dānaṃ tvaṃ jaya kaiṭabhasūdana //
122.d:
जय यज्ञद यज्ञस् त्वं जय पद्मदलेक्षण
जय दानद दानं त्वं जय कैटभसूदन ॥
122.m: Victory, bestower of sacrifice, you are sacrifice! Victory, lotus-petal-eyed one! / Victory, bestower of charity, you are charity! Victory, slayer of Kaiṭabha!

122.s:
jaya kīrtida kīrtis tvaṃ jaya mūrtida mūrtidhṛk
jaya saukhyada saukhyātmañ jaya pāvanapāvana //
122.d:
जय कीर्तिद कीर्तिस् त्वं जय मूर्तिद मूर्तिधृक्
जय सौख्यद सौख्यात्मञ् जय पावनपावन ॥
122.m: Victory, bestower of fame, you are fame! Victory, giver of form, bearer of form! / Victory, giver of happiness, whose self is happiness! Victory, purifier of the purifiers!

122.s:
jaya śāntida śāntis tvaṃ jaya śaṃkarasaṃbhava
jaya pānada pānas tvaṃ jaya jyotiḥsvarūpiṇe //
122.d:
जय शान्तिद शान्तिस् त्वं जय शंकरसंभव
जय पानद पानस् त्वं जय ज्योतिःस्वरूपिणे ॥
122.m: Victory, giver of peace, you are peace! Victory, source of Śaṃkara! / Victory, bestower of drink, you are drink! Victory to the one whose nature is light!

122.s:
jaya vāmana vitteśa jaya dhūmapatākine
jaya sarvasya jagato dātṛmūrte namo 'stu te //
122.d:
जय वामन वित्तेश जय धूमपताकिने
जय सर्वस्य जगतो दातृमूर्ते नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
122.m: Victory, Vāmana, lord of wealth! Victory to the one whose banner is smoke! / Victory, homage be to you whose form is the giver to the entire world!

122.s:
tvam eva lokatrayavartijīva
nikāyasaṃkleśavināśadakṣa
śrīpuṇḍarīkākṣa kṛpānidhe tvaṃ
nidhehi pāṇiṃ mama mūrdhni viṣṇo
122.d:
त्वम् एव लोकत्रयवर्तिजीव
निकायसंक्लेशविनाशदक्ष
श्रीपुण्डरीकाक्ष कृपानिधे त्वं
निधेहि पाणिं मम मूर्ध्नि विष्णो
122.m: You alone are skilled in destroying the distress / of the multitude of living beings existing in the three worlds. / O lotus-eyed one, ocean of mercy, / place your hand upon my head, O Viṣṇu!"

122.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ stuvantaṃ bhagavāñ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ
vareṇa cchandayām āsa sarvakāmasamṛddhidaḥ //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं स्तुवन्तं भगवाञ् शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः
वरेण च्छन्दयाम् आस सर्वकामसमृद्धिदः ॥
122.m:
Brahmā said:
To him who was praising thus, the blessed bearer of the conch, discus, and mace, / the bestower of the fulfillment of all desires, offered a boon.

122.s:
dhanvantariḥ prītamanā varadānena cakriṇaḥ
varadānāya deveśaṃ govindaṃ saṃsthitaṃ puraḥ //
122.d:
धन्वन्तरिः प्रीतमना वरदानेन चक्रिणः
वरदानाय देवेशं गोविन्दं संस्थितं पुरः ॥
122.m: Dhanvantari, glad at heart with the boon granted by the bearer of the discus, / to Govinda, the lord of gods, standing before him to grant a boon,

122.s:
tam āha nṛpatiḥ prahvaḥ surarājyaṃ mamepsitam
tac ca dattaṃ tvayā viṣṇo prāpto 'smi kṛtakṛtyatām //
122.d:
तम् आह नृपतिः प्रह्वः सुरराज्यं ममेप्सितम्
तच् च दत्तं त्वया विष्णो प्राप्तो ऽस्मि कृतकृत्यताम् ॥
122.m: the bowed king said to him: "Sovereignty over the gods is desired by me, / and that has been given by you, O Viṣṇu; I have accomplished my purpose."

122.s:
stutaḥ saṃpūjito viṣṇus tatraivāntaradhīyata
tathaiva tridaśeśatvam avāpa nṛpatiḥ kramāt //
122.d:
स्तुतः संपूजितो विष्णुस् तत्रैवान्तरधीयत
तथैव त्रिदशेशत्वम् अवाप नृपतिः क्रमात् ॥
122.m: Praised and worshiped, Viṣṇu vanished right there; / and likewise, the king attained the lordship of the thirty [gods] in due course.

122.s:
prāgarjitānekakarmaparipākavaśāt tataḥ
triḥkṛtvo nāśam agamat sahasrākṣaḥ svakāt padāt //
122.d:
प्रागर्जितानेककर्मपरिपाकवशात् ततः
त्रिःकृत्वो नाशम् अगमत् सहस्राक्षः स्वकात् पदात् ॥
122.m: Then, under the sway of the maturation of many deeds previously acquired, / the thousand-eyed one fell three times from his own station:

122.s:
nahuṣād vṛtrahatyāyāḥ sindhusenavadhāt tataḥ
ahalyāyāṃ ca gamanād yena kena ca hetunā //
122.d:
नहुषाद् वृत्रहत्यायाः सिन्धुसेनवधात् ततः
अहल्यायां च गमनाद् येन केन च हेतुना ॥
122.m: on account of Nahuṣa, the slaying of Vṛtra, the killing of Sindhusena, / and the approach to Ahalyā, for one reason or another.

122.s:
smāraṃ smāraṃ tat tad indraś cintāsaṃtāpadurmanāḥ
tataḥ surapatiḥ prāha vācaspatim idaṃ vacaḥ //
122.d:
स्मारं स्मारं तत् तद् इन्द्रश् चिन्तासंतापदुर्मनाः
ततः सुरपतिः प्राह वाचस्पतिम् इदं वचः ॥
122.m: Remembering and remembering those things, Indra became dejected with sorrow and grief. / Then the lord of the gods spoke these words to Vācaspati:

122.s:
indra uvāca
hetunā kena vāgīśa bhraṣṭarājyo bhavāmy aham
madhye madhye padabhraṃśād varaṃ niḥśrīkatā nṛṇām //
122.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
हेतुना केन वागीश भ्रष्टराज्यो भवाम्य् अहम्
मध्ये मध्ये पदभ्रंशाद् वरं निःश्रीकता नृणाम् ॥
122.m:
Indra said:
"For what reason, O Lord of Speech, do I fall from my kingdom? / Rather than a fall from office now and then, loss of fortune is better for men.

122.s:
gahanāṃ karmaṇāṃ jīvagatiṃ ko vetti tattvataḥ
rahasyaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ jñātuṃ nānyaḥ pragalbhate //
122.d:
गहनां कर्मणां जीवगतिं को वेत्ति तत्त्वतः
रहस्यं सर्वभावानां ज्ञातुं नान्यः प्रगल्भते ॥
122.m: Who knows truly the deep course of deeds of living beings? / No other is capable of knowing the secret of all states of being."

122.s:
brahmovāca
bṛhaspatir hariṃ prāha brahmāṇaṃ pṛccha gaccha tam
sa tu jānāti yad bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac cāpi vartanam //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
बृहस्पतिर् हरिं प्राह ब्रह्माणं पृच्छ गच्छ तम्
स तु जानाति यद् भूतं भविष्यच् चापि वर्तनम् ॥
122.m:
Brahmā said:
Bṛhaspati said to Hari: "Go and ask Brahmā; / for he knows what has been, what is to come, and the present.

122.s:
sa tu vakṣyati yenedaṃ jātaṃ tac ca mahāmate
tāv āgatya mahāprājñau namaskṛtya mamāntikam
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā mām ūcatur idaṃ vacaḥ //
122.d:
स तु वक्ष्यति येनेदं जातं तच् च महामते
ताव् आगत्य महाप्राज्ञौ नमस्कृत्य ममान्तिकम्
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा माम् ऊचतुर् इदं वचः ॥
122.m: He will tell by what this came to pass, O great-minded one.’ / Those two of great wisdom, having come before me and bowed down, / folded their hands in supplication and addressed me with these words:

122.s:
indrabṛhaspatī ūcatuḥ
bhagavan kena doṣeṇa śacībhartā udāradhīḥ
rājyāt prabhraśyate nātha saṃśayaṃ chettum arhasi //
122.d:
इन्द्रबृहस्पती ऊचतुः
भगवन् केन दोषेण शचीभर्ता उदारधीः
राज्यात् प्रभ्रश्यते नाथ संशयं छेत्तुम् अर्हसि ॥
122.m: Indra and Bṛhaspati said: / ‘O Lord, through what fault is the husband of Śacī, though noble-minded, / fallen from his kingdom, O protector? You ought to dispel our doubt.’

122.s:
brahmovāca
tadāham abravaṃ brahmaṃś ciraṃ dhyātvā bṛhaspatim
khaṇḍadharmākhyadoṣeṇa tena rājyapadāc cyutaḥ //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तदाहम् अब्रवं ब्रह्मंश् चिरं ध्यात्वा बृहस्पतिम्
खण्डधर्माख्यदोषेण तेन राज्यपदाच् च्युतः ॥
122.m: Brahmā said: / ‘Then, O brahmin, having meditated for a long time, I spoke to Bṛhaspati: / "By the fault called 'broken dharma' he has fallen from the status of his kingdom.

122.s:
deśakālādidoṣeṇa śraddhāmantraviparyayāt
yathāvaddakṣiṇādānād asaddravyapradānataḥ //
122.d:
देशकालादिदोषेण श्रद्धामन्त्रविपर्ययात्
यथावद्दक्षिणादानाद् असद्द्रव्यप्रदानतः ॥
122.m: Through defects of place, time, and so forth, through the corruption of faith and mantras, / through not giving the sacrificial fee properly, through offering unworthy materials,

122.s:
devabhūdevatāvajñāpātakāc ca viśeṣataḥ
yat khaṇḍatvaṃ svadharmasya dehinām upajāyate //
122.d:
देवभूदेवतावज्ञापातकाच् च विशेषतः
यत् खण्डत्वं स्वधर्मस्य देहिनाम् उपजायते ॥
122.m: and especially from the sin of disrespecting gods and brahmins, / the brokenness of one's own dharma arises for embodied beings.

122.s:
tenātimānasas tāpaḥ padahāniś ca dustyajā
kṛto 'pi dharmo 'niṣṭāya jāyate kṣubdhacetasā //
122.d:
तेनातिमानसस् तापः पदहानिश् च दुस्त्यजा
कृतो ऽपि धर्मो ऽनिष्टाय जायते क्षुब्धचेतसा ॥
122.m: Through that comes immense mental anguish and the loss of status, hard to avoid. / Even dharma performed by an agitated mind leads to misfortune;

122.s:
kāryasya na bhavet siddhyai tasmād avyākulāya ca
asaṃpūrṇe svadharme hi kim aniṣṭaṃ na jāyate //
122.d:
कार्यस्य न भवेत् सिद्ध्यै तस्माद् अव्याकुलाय च
असंपूर्णे स्वधर्मे हि किम् अनिष्टं न जायते ॥
122.m: it will not lead to the accomplishment of one's purpose, nor therefore to peace of mind. / Indeed, when one's own dharma is incomplete, what misfortune does not arise?"

122.s:
tābhyāṃ yat pūrvavṛttāntaṃ tad apy uktaṃ mayānagha
āyuṣas tu sutaḥ śrīmān dhanvantarir udāradhīḥ //
122.d:
ताभ्यां यत् पूर्ववृत्तान्तं तद् अप्य् उक्तं मयानघ
आयुषस् तु सुतः श्रीमान् धन्वन्तरिर् उदारधीः ॥
122.m: What had occurred earlier regarding those two was also related by me, O sinless one: / the glorious and noble-minded Dhanvantari, son of Āyus,

122.s:
tamasā ca kṛtaṃ vighnaṃ viṣṇunā tac ca nāśitam
pūrvajanmasu vṛttāntam ityādi parikīrtitam //
122.d:
तमसा च कृतं विघ्नं विष्णुना तच् च नाशितम्
पूर्वजन्मसु वृत्तान्तम् इत्यादि परिकीर्तितम् ॥
122.m: the obstacle caused by darkness and its destruction by Viṣṇu, / the account of previous births—all this was recounted.

122.s: tac chrutvā vismitau cobhau mām eva punar ūcatuḥ //
122.d: तच् छ्रुत्वा विस्मितौ चोभौ माम् एव पुनर् ऊचतुः ॥
122.m: Hearing that, both were amazed, and spoke to me once again:

122.s:
indrabṛhaspatī ūcatuḥ
taddoṣapratibandhas tu kena syāt surasattama //
122.d:
इन्द्रबृहस्पती ऊचतुः
तद्दोषप्रतिबन्धस् तु केन स्यात् सुरसत्तम ॥
122.m: Indra and Bṛhaspati said: / ‘By what means may the obstruction of that fault be removed, O best of gods?’

122.s:
brahmovāca
punar dhyātvā tāv avadaṃ śrūyatāṃ doṣakārakam
kāraṇaṃ sarvasiddhīnāṃ duḥkhasaṃsāratāraṇam //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुनर् ध्यात्वा ताव् अवदं श्रूयतां दोषकारकम्
कारणं सर्वसिद्धीनां दुःखसंसारतारणम् ॥
122.m: Brahmā said: / Having reflected again, I spoke to the two of them: ‘Listen to what removes the fault, / the cause of all attainments, that which carries one across the sorrowful saṃsāra,

122.s:
śaraṇaṃ taptacittānāṃ nirvāṇaṃ jīvatām api
gatvā tu gautamīṃ devīṃ stūyetāṃ hariśaṃkarau //
122.d:
शरणं तप्तचित्तानां निर्वाणं जीवताम् अपि
गत्वा तु गौतमीं देवीं स्तूयेतां हरिशंकरौ ॥
122.m: the refuge of those whose minds are tormented, liberation even for the living: / Go to the divine Gautamī and praise Hari and Śaṅkara.

122.s:
nopāyo 'nyo 'sti saṃśuddhyai tau tāṃ hitvā jagattraye
tadaiva jagmatur ubhau gautamīṃ munisattama
snātau kṛtakṣaṇau cobhau devau tuṣṭuvatur mudā //
122.d:
नोपायो ऽन्यो ऽस्ति संशुद्ध्यै तौ तां हित्वा जगत्त्रये
तदैव जग्मतुर् उभौ गौतमीं मुनिसत्तम
स्नातौ कृतक्षणौ चोभौ देवौ तुष्टुवतुर् मुदा ॥
122.m: There is no other means for purification in the three worlds besides that [river].’ / Just then both went to the Gautamī, O best of sages; / both bathed, took their opportunity, and joyfully praised the two gods.

122.s:
indra uvāca
namo matsyāya kūrmāya varāhāya namo namaḥ
narasiṃhāya devāya vāmanāya namo namaḥ //
122.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
नमो मत्स्याय कूर्माय वराहाय नमो नमः
नरसिंहाय देवाय वामनाय नमो नमः ॥
122.m: Indra said: / ‘Homage to the Fish, to the Tortoise, homage, homage to the Boar, / to the divine Man-Lion, to the Dwarf, homage, homage!

122.s:
namo 'stu hayarūpāya trivikrama namo 'stu te
namo 'stu buddharūpāya rāmarūpāya kalkine //
122.d:
नमो ऽस्तु हयरूपाय त्रिविक्रम नमो ऽस्तु ते
नमो ऽस्तु बुद्धरूपाय रामरूपाय कल्किने ॥
122.m: Homage be to the Horse-formed! O Trivikrama, homage be to you! / Homage be to the Buddha-formed, to the Rāma-formed, to Kalkin!

122.s:
anantāyācyutāyeśa jāmadagnyāya te namaḥ
varuṇendrasvarūpāya yamarūpāya te namaḥ //
122.d:
अनन्तायाच्युतायेश जामदग्न्याय ते नमः
वरुणेन्द्रस्वरूपाय यमरूपाय ते नमः ॥
122.m: Homage to you, Ananta, Acyuta, Lord, son of Jamadagni! / Homage to you whose nature is Varuṇa and Indra, whose nature is Yama!

122.s:
parameśāya devāya namas trailokyarūpiṇe
bibhratsarasvatīṃ vaktre sarvajño 'si namo 'stu te //
122.d:
परमेशाय देवाय नमस् त्रैलोक्यरूपिणे
बिभ्रत्सरस्वतीं वक्त्रे सर्वज्ञो ऽसि नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
122.m: Homage to the supreme Lord, the god whose form is the three worlds! / Bearing Sarasvatī in your mouth, you are omniscient; homage be to you!

122.s:
lakṣmīvān asy ato lakṣmīṃ bibhrad vakṣasi cānagha
bahubāhūrupādas tvaṃ bahukarṇākṣiśīrṣakaḥ
tvām eva sukhinaṃ prāpya bahavaḥ sukhino 'bhavan //
122.d:
लक्ष्मीवान् अस्य् अतो लक्ष्मीं बिभ्रद् वक्षसि चानघ
बहुबाहूरुपादस् त्वं बहुकर्णाक्षिशीर्षकः
त्वाम् एव सुखिनं प्राप्य बहवः सुखिनो ऽभवन् ॥
122.m: You possess Lakṣmī, and hence you bear Lakṣmī upon your chest, O sinless one. / You have many arms, thighs, and feet; you have many ears, eyes, and heads. / Having attained you, the blissful one, many have become happy.

122.s:
tāvan niḥśrīkatā puṃsāṃ mālinyaṃ dainyam eva vā
yāvan na yānti śaraṇaṃ hare tvāṃ karuṇārṇavam //
122.d:
तावन् निःश्रीकता पुंसां मालिन्यं दैन्यम् एव वा
यावन् न यान्ति शरणं हरे त्वां करुणार्णवम् ॥
122.m: Men suffer misfortune, pollution, or destitution only so long / as they do not take refuge in you, O Hari, ocean of compassion!’

122.s:
bṛhaspatir uvāca
sūkṣmaṃ paraṃ jotir anantarūpam
oṃkāramātraṃ prakṛteḥ paraṃ yat
cidrūpam ānandamayaṃ samastam
evaṃ vadantīśa mumukṣavas tvām
122.d:
बृहस्पतिर् उवाच
सूक्ष्मं परं जोतिर् अनन्तरूपम्
ओंकारमात्रं प्रकृतेः परं यत्
चिद्रूपम् आनन्दमयं समस्तम्
एवं वदन्तीश मुमुक्षवस् त्वाम्
122.m: Bṛhaspati said: / ‘Subtle, supreme light, of infinite form, / the syllable Oṃ alone, which is beyond prakṛti, / consisting of consciousness, entirely full of bliss— / thus, O Lord, those desiring liberation speak of you.

122.s:
ārādhayanty atra bhavantam īśaṃ
mahāmakhaiḥ pañcabhir apy akāmāḥ
saṃsārasindhoḥ param āptakāmā
viśanti divyaṃ bhuvanaṃ vapus te
122.d:
आराधयन्त्य् अत्र भवन्तम् ईशं
महामखैः पञ्चभिर् अप्य् अकामाः
संसारसिन्धोः परम् आप्तकामा
विशन्ति दिव्यं भुवनं वपुस् ते
122.m: Here, free of desire, they worship you, the Lord, / even with the five great sacrifices; / having reached the other side of the ocean of worldly existence, their desires fulfilled, / they enter your divine realm and body.

122.s:
sarveṣu sattveṣu samatvabuddhyā
saṃvīkṣya ṣaṭsūrmiṣu śāntabhāvāḥ
jñānena te karmaphalāni hitvā
dhyānena te tvāṃ praviśanti śaṃbho
122.d:
सर्वेषु सत्त्वेषु समत्वबुद्ध्या
संवीक्ष्य षट्सूर्मिषु शान्तभावाः
ज्ञानेन ते कर्मफलानि हित्वा
ध्यानेन ते त्वां प्रविशन्ति शंभो
122.m: Regarding all beings with a mind of equality, / their state pacified amid the six waves [of existence], / relinquishing the fruits of action through knowledge / and through meditation, they enter into you, O Śambhu.

122.s:
na jātidharmāṇi na vedaśāstraṃ
na dhyānayogo na samādhidharmaḥ
rudraṃ śivaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śānticittaṃ
bhaktyā devaṃ somam ahaṃ namasye
122.d:
न जातिधर्माणि न वेदशास्त्रं
न ध्यानयोगो न समाधिधर्मः
रुद्रं शिवं शंकरं शान्तिचित्तं
भक्त्या देवं सोमम् अहं नमस्ये
122.m: Not by caste duties, nor Vedic scripture, / nor yoga of meditation, nor the practice of samādhi [do I approach you]; / Rudra, Śiva, Śaṅkara, whose mind is tranquil, / the god Soma, I revere with devotion.

122.s:
mūrkho 'pi śaṃbho tava pādabhaktyā
samāpnuyān muktimayīṃ tanuṃ te
jñāneṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva
dhyāneṣu homeṣu mahāphaleṣu
122.d:
मूर्खो ऽपि शंभो तव पादभक्त्या
समाप्नुयान् मुक्तिमयीं तनुं ते
ज्ञानेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव
ध्यानेषु होमेषु महाफलेषु
122.m: Even a fool, O Śambhu, through devotion to your feet, / can attain your body consisting of liberation. / In kinds of knowledge, in sacrifices, and in austerities, / in meditations and in oblations of great fruit,

122.s:
saṃpannam etat phalam uttamaṃ yat
someśvare bhaktir aharniśaṃ yat
sarvasya jīvasya sadā priyasya
phalasya dṛṣṭasya tathā śrutasya
122.d:
संपन्नम् एतत् फलम् उत्तमं यत्
सोमेश्वरे भक्तिर् अहर्निशं यत्
सर्वस्य जीवस्य सदा प्रियस्य
फलस्य दृष्टस्य तथा श्रुतस्य
122.m: this supreme fruit is accomplished: / that devotion to Someśvara day and night, / which is always dear to every living being, / a fruit seen as well as heard of.

122.s:
svargasya mokṣasya jagannivāsa
sopānapaṅktis tava bhaktir eṣā
tvatpādasaṃprāptiphalāptaye tu
sopānapaṅktiṃ na vadanti dhīrāḥ
122.d:
स्वर्गस्य मोक्षस्य जगन्निवास
सोपानपङ्क्तिस् तव भक्तिर् एषा
त्वत्पादसंप्राप्तिफलाप्तये तु
सोपानपङ्क्तिं न वदन्ति धीराः
122.m: O abode of the world, for heaven and for liberation / this devotion to you is a flight of stairs. / Yet for attaining the fruit of reaching your feet, / the wise do not speak of any flight of stairs.

122.s:
tasmād dayālo mama bhaktir astu
naivāsty upāyas tava rūpasevā
ātmīyam ālokya mahattvam īśa
pāpeṣu cāsmāsu kuru prasādam
122.d:
तस्माद् दयालो मम भक्तिर् अस्तु
नैवास्त्य् उपायस् तव रूपसेवा
आत्मीयम् आलोक्य महत्त्वम् ईश
पापेषु चास्मासु कुरु प्रसादम्
122.m: Therefore, O merciful one, may I have devotion; / there is indeed no other means than service to your form. / Beholding your own greatness, O Lord, / grant your grace unto us, though we are sinners.

122.s:
sthūlaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ tvam anādi nityaṃ
pitā ca mātā yad asac ca sac ca
evaṃ stuto yaḥ śrutibhiḥ purāṇair
namāmi someśvaram īśitāram
122.d:
स्थूलं च सूक्ष्मं त्वम् अनादि नित्यं
पिता च माता यद् असच् च सच् च
एवं स्तुतो यः श्रुतिभिः पुराणैर्
नमामि सोमेश्वरम् ईशितारम्
122.m: You are the gross and the subtle, beginningless, eternal, / both father and mother, that which is unreal and real. / To Someśvara, the ruler, who is thus praised / by the Vedas and the Purāṇas, I bow down.’

122.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ prītau hariharāv ūcatus tridaśeśvarau //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्रीतौ हरिहराव् ऊचतुस् त्रिदशेश्वरौ ॥
122.m: Brahmā said: / Then Hari and Hara, pleased, spoke to the two lords of the gods.

122.s:
hariharāv ūcatuḥ
vriyatāṃ yan manobhīṣṭaṃ yad varaṃ cātidurlabham //
122.d:
हरिहराव् ऊचतुः
व्रियतां यन् मनोभीष्टं यद् वरं चातिदुर्लभम् ॥
122.m: Hari and Hara said: / ‘Let that which your heart desires and whatever boon is most difficult to obtain be chosen.’

122.s:
brahmovāca
indraḥ prāha sureśānaṃ madrājyaṃ tu punaḥ punaḥ
jāyate bhraśyate caiva tat pāpam upaśāmyatām //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इन्द्रः प्राह सुरेशानं मद्राज्यं तु पुनः पुनः
जायते भ्रश्यते चैव तत् पापम् उपशाम्यताम् ॥
122.m: Brahmā said: / Indra said to the Lord of gods: ‘My kingdom again and again / comes into being and is lost; let that sin be appeased,

122.s:
yathā sthiro 'haṃ rājye syāṃ sarvaṃ syān niścalaṃ mama
suprītau yadi deveśau sarvaṃ syān niścalaṃ sadā //
122.d:
यथा स्थिरो ऽहं राज्ये स्यां सर्वं स्यान् निश्चलं मम
सुप्रीतौ यदि देवेशौ सर्वं स्यान् निश्चलं सदा ॥
122.m: so that I may be firm in my kingdom and everything of mine may become steadfast. / If the two lords of gods are well-pleased, may everything always be steadfast.’

122.s:
tatheti harivākyaṃ tāv abhinandyedam ūcatuḥ
paraṃ prasādam āpannau tāv ālokya smitānanau //
122.d:
तथेति हरिवाक्यं ताव् अभिनन्द्येदम् ऊचतुः
परं प्रसादम् आपन्नौ ताव् आलोक्य स्मिताननौ ॥
122.m: Welcoming Hari’s word ‘So be it!’, the two of them spoke this, / having attained supreme grace, beholding the two [gods] with smiling faces,

122.s:
nirapāyanirādhāranirvikārasvarūpiṇau
śaraṇyau sarvalokānāṃ bhuktimuktipradāv ubhau //
122.d:
निरपायनिराधारनिर्विकारस्वरूपिणौ
शरण्यौ सर्वलोकानां भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदाव् उभौ ॥
122.m: whose nature is free from peril, free from support, and free from change, / who are the refuge of all the worlds, and who bestow both enjoyment and liberation.

122.s:
hariharāv ūcatuḥ
tridaivatyaṃ mahātīrthaṃ gautamī vāñchitapradā
tasyām anena mantreṇa kurutāṃ snānam ādarāt //
122.d:
हरिहराव् ऊचतुः
त्रिदैवत्यं महातीर्थं गौतमी वाञ्छितप्रदा
तस्याम् अनेन मन्त्रेण कुरुतां स्नानम् आदरात् ॥
122.m: Hari and Hara said: / ‘The Gautamī is a great tīrtha belonging to three deities, granting what is desired. / In it, with this mantra, perform the bath with reverence:

122.s:
abhiṣekaṃ mahendrasya maṅgalāya bṛhaspatiḥ
karotu saṃsmarann āvāṃ saṃpadāṃ sthairyasiddhaye //
122.d:
अभिषेकं महेन्द्रस्य मङ्गलाय बृहस्पतिः
करोतु संस्मरन्न् आवां संपदां स्थैर्यसिद्धये ॥
122.m: "May Bṛhaspati perform the consecration of Mahendra / for auspiciousness, remembering us two, for the sake of achieving stability of fortune:

122.s:
iha janmani pūrvasmin yat kiṃcit sukṛtaṃ kṛtam
tat sarvaṃ pūrṇatām etu godāvari namo 'stu te //
122.d:
इह जन्मनि पूर्वस्मिन् यत् किंचित् सुकृतं कृतम्
तत् सर्वं पूर्णताम् एतु गोदावरि नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
122.m: 'Whatever good deed has been done in this birth or in a previous one, / may all that attain completeness! O Godāvarī, homage be to you!'"

122.s:
evaṃ smṛtvā tu yaḥ kaścid gautamyāṃ snānam ācaret
āvābhyāṃ tu prasādena dharmaḥ saṃpūrṇatām iyāt
pūrvajanmakṛtād doṣāt sa muktaḥ puṇyavān bhavet //
122.d:
एवं स्मृत्वा तु यः कश्चिद् गौतम्यां स्नानम् आचरेत्
आवाभ्यां तु प्रसादेन धर्मः संपूर्णताम् इयात्
पूर्वजन्मकृताद् दोषात् स मुक्तः पुण्यवान् भवेत् ॥
122.m: Whoever performs the bath in the Gautamī, having remembered this [mantra], / his dharma shall attain completeness by our grace; / freed from the fault committed in a previous birth, he shall become meritorious.’

122.s:
brahmovāca
tatheti cakratuḥ prītau surendradhiṣaṇau tataḥ
mahābhiṣekam indrasya cakāra dyusadāṃ guruḥ //
122.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेति चक्रतुः प्रीतौ सुरेन्द्रधिषणौ ततः
महाभिषेकम् इन्द्रस्य चकार द्युसदां गुरुः ॥
122.m: Brahmā said: / Then the ruler of the gods and Dhiṣaṇa gladly said, ‘So be it!’ / The preceptor of the celestials performed the great consecration of Indra.

122.s:
tenābhūd yā nadī puṇyā maṅgalety uditā tu sā
tayā ca saṃgamaḥ puṇyo gaṅgāyāḥ śubhadas tv asau //
122.d:
तेनाभूद् या नदी पुण्या मङ्गलेत्य् उदिता तु सा
तया च संगमः पुण्यो गङ्गायाः शुभदस् त्व् असौ ॥
122.m: The holy river that arose from that was called Maṅgalā; / and its holy confluence with the Gaṅgā is auspicious.

122.s:
indreṇa saṃstuto viṣṇuḥ pratyakṣo 'bhūj jaganmayaḥ
trilokasaṃmitāṃ śakro bhūmiṃ lebhe jagatpateḥ //
122.d:
इन्द्रेण संस्तुतो विष्णुः प्रत्यक्षो ऽभूज् जगन्मयः
त्रिलोकसंमितां शक्रो भूमिं लेभे जगत्पतेः ॥
122.m: Praised by Indra, Viṣṇu, who pervades the universe, became manifest before his eyes. / Śakra received from the Lord of the universe the earth measuring the three worlds.

122.s:
tannāmnā cāpi vikhyāto govinda iti tatra ca
trilokasaṃmitā labdhā tena gaur vajradhāriṇā //
122.d:
तन्नाम्ना चापि विख्यातो गोविन्द इति तत्र च
त्रिलोकसंमिता लब्धा तेन गौर् वज्रधारिणा ॥
122.m: And by that name he is renowned as Govinda there, / because by him, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the earth measuring the three worlds was obtained.

122.s:
dattā ca hariṇā tatra govindas tad abhūd dhariḥ
trailokyarājyaṃ yat prāptaṃ hariṇā ca harer mune //
122.d:
दत्ता च हरिणा तत्र गोविन्दस् तद् अभूद् धरिः
त्रैलोक्यराज्यं यत् प्राप्तं हरिणा च हरेर् मुने ॥
122.m: And given there by Hari, Hari then became Govinda. / The kingdom of the three worlds which was obtained by Hari, and from Hari, O sage,

122.s:
niścalaṃ yena saṃjātaṃ devadevān maheśvarāt
bṛhaspatir devagurur yatrāstauṣīn maheśvaram //
122.d:
निश्चलं येन संजातं देवदेवान् महेश्वरात्
बृहस्पतिर् देवगुरुर् यत्रास्तौषीन् महेश्वरम् ॥
122.m: By which it was made secure through the god of gods, Maheśvara; / Where Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the gods, praised Maheśvara

122.s:
rājyasya sthirabhāvāya devendrasya mahātmanaḥ
siddheśvaras tatra devo liṅgaṃ tu tridaśārcitam //
122.d:
राज्यस्य स्थिरभावाय देवेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः
सिद्धेश्वरस् तत्र देवो लिङ्गं तु त्रिदशार्चितम् ॥
122.m: For the stability of the kingdom of the great-souled lord of the gods. / Siddheśvara is the god there, and the liṅga is worshipped by the gods.

122.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ govindam iti viśrutam
maṅgalāsaṃgamaṃ caiva pūrṇatīrthaṃ tataḥ param //
122.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं गोविन्दम् इति विश्रुतम्
मङ्गलासंगमं चैव पूर्णतीर्थं ततः परम् ॥
122.m: From then on, that tīrtha became renowned as Govinda, / And as the confluence of Maṅgalā, and after that Pūrṇatīrtha;

122.s:
indratīrtham iti khyātaṃ bārhaspatyaṃ ca viśrutam
yatra siddheśvaro devo viṣṇur govinda eva ca //
122.d:
इन्द्रतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं बार्हस्पत्यं च विश्रुतम्
यत्र सिद्धेश्वरो देवो विष्णुर् गोविन्द एव च ॥
122.m: It is famed as Indratīrtha and renowned as Bārhaspatya, / Where the god Siddheśvara is, and Viṣṇu Govinda himself.

122.s:
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca yat kiṃcit sukṛtārjanam
sarvaṃ tad akṣayaṃ vidyāt pitṝṇām ativallabham //
122.d:
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च यत् किंचित् सुकृतार्जनम्
सर्वं तद् अक्षयं विद्यात् पितॄणाम् अतिवल्लभम् ॥
122.m: Bathing there and giving gifts, whatever earning of merit [is done], / One should know all that is inexhaustible and very dear to the ancestors.

122.s:
śṛṇoti yaś cāpi paṭhed yaś ca smarati nityaśaḥ
tasya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ bhraṣṭarājyapradāyakam //
122.d:
शृणोति यश् चापि पठेद् यश् च स्मरति नित्यशः
तस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं भ्रष्टराज्यप्रदायकम् ॥
122.m: And whoever listens, or reads, or remembers constantly / The majesty of that tīrtha, it bestows lost kingdom.

122.s:
saptatriṃśat sahasrāṇi tīrthānāṃ tīrayor dvayoḥ
ubhayor muniśārdūla sarvasiddhipradāyinām //
122.d:
सप्तत्रिंशत् सहस्राणि तीर्थानां तीरयोर् द्वयोः
उभयोर् मुनिशार्दूल सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायिनाम् ॥
122.m: There are thirty-seven thousand tīrthas on the two banks, / On both [banks], O tiger among sages, granting all perfections.

122.s:
na pūrṇatīrthasadṛśaṃ tīrtham asti mahāphalam
niṣphalaṃ tasya janmādi yo na seveta tan naraḥ //
122.d:
न पूर्णतीर्थसदृशं तीर्थम् अस्ति महाफलम्
निष्फलं तस्य जन्मादि यो न सेवेत तन् नरः ॥
122.m: There is no tīrtha yielding such great fruit as Pūrṇatīrtha; / Fruitless is the birth and life of that man who would not resort to it.
